### REG-F-116 — the mutation runner stated a CAUSE it never measured, and the check that fixed it read its own test fixtures as evidence
- **Date:** 2026-08-12 · **Type:** INSTRUMENT DEFECT (JAN-VERIF V-4a diagnosis → V-4b repair) · **Status:** FIXED, with three controls and four mutants; **`scripts/mutants/run.ts` remains almost entirely untested and that is OWED.**
- **HOW IT SURFACED, AND THE SYMPTOM POINTED AT THE WRONG THING ENTIRELY.** The full gate reported `SURVIVED: WP12B-M3 … declared a CONTROL, but a test FAILED on it — something asserts on prose`. That sentence sends the reader to find a test asserting on a rationale string. There was none. The message, read at the fourth attempt, was `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms` — 6135ms against a 5000ms default, in an unrelated suite. **The mutation was irrelevant to the failure it was blamed for.**
- **THE V-4a CAUSE, FIXED AT THE CAUSE.** `enforcement-register.test.ts` called `canonFilesContaining` once per registered rule (~112) and each call did a `readdirSync` plus a full `readFileSync` of all six canon artifacts — ~2.6 MB, hundreds of large reads, 740ms in isolation. Read once: **740ms → 26ms**, 62 tests still green. ⚠ **AND IT WAS DEGRADING ON A SCHEDULE, PARTLY BY MY OWN HAND:** `JPWB-REG-005` is one of the six artifacts re-read there and it grows with every finding recorded — ten entries the day before. **A test whose cost scales with the register fails eventually no matter what the code does.** Raising `testTimeout` would have left 168 MB of redundant I/O and the gate one slow machine from the same false verdict.
- **BUT THE FINDING IS UNDER THAT, AND IT IS ABOUT ATTRIBUTION.** `run.ts` decides every verdict from ONE bit — the exit status — and then states a CONCLUSION about the mutation. That inference is sound only if the run exercised it. **A timeout is not a measurement, and the runner had no way to say so.**
- **⚠ IT CUTS BOTH WAYS, WHICH IS WHY THE CHECK SITS ABOVE BOTH ARMS RATHER THAN INSIDE THE CONTROL ARM.** A CONTROL declares `expectRed: []`, so `targetSuites` is empty and vitest runs the WHOLE suite: a timeout there is a **FALSE BLOCKING** — loud, and it cost a long investigation. A **NAMED** victim's run turns the same timeout into a **FALSE KILL**: status non-zero, the ledger records the guard as proven, and nothing that ran ever touched it. REG-F-110 named that asymmetry in terms — *"a false KILL is quieter than a false BLOCK and it had been sitting under a green tick."*
- **MEASURED, NOT DEDUCED — the counterfactual was DRIVEN.** Same mutant, same deliberately-hung victim, two runners: pre-fix (`9ac5609d`'s `run.ts`, extracted from git and run side by side) reported **`KILLED 1 · 0 need attention · exit 0`**; post-fix reported **`INCONCLUSIVE 1 · 1 needs attention · BLOCKING`**. The first is a guard recorded as proven by a run that never reached it. **I drove it rather than reasoning about it because REG-F-110's first fix was verified by hand-run and the plumbing was the part that was broken.**
- **WHAT SHIPPED.** A new verdict `INCONCLUSIVE`, joining `UNANCHORED` / `NO_COMPILE` / `ABORTED_DIRTY` — the verdicts that say **the INSTRUMENT did not work** — rather than `SURVIVED`, which says the CODE did not. It blocks either way; **the sentence is the point.** The predicate is extracted to `scripts/mutants/measured.ts` and quotes the text it observed, because the entire finding is that a verdict asserted something the reader could not check. **The cost is disclosed:** a mutation that genuinely hangs its victim now reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than KILLED and its author must say so deliberately — correct polarity, since the ledger's claim is *"this named test reddens BECAUSE it asserts the guard"*, which a hang cannot establish.
- **⚠ THEN THE REPAIR'S OWN MUTANTS FOUND A SECOND DEFECT ONE LAYER DOWN, ON THEIR FIRST RUN.** Two of them reported INCONCLUSIVE for a mutant their victim killed cleanly. `run.ts` scans the CHILD'S stdout — and a test that ASSERTS on timeout text prints that text into stdout the moment it fails, because vitest renders the expected value on a line of its own, in quotes: `"Hook timed out in 10000ms"`. **The instrument read the FIXTURE OF THE FAILING TEST as a diagnostic from the runner.** The only reason a third mutant escaped is an accident of process boundaries: `run.ts` holds the unmutated function in memory while the child holds the mutated one.
- **THE GENERAL FORM, AND IT IS THE THIRD SIGHTING IN THIS REGISTER — recorded as a class because the next instance will not look like a timeout.** *An instrument that reads a free-text channel cannot distinguish its subject's **DATA** from its own **SIGNAL** — and the test written to prove the instrument is precisely the one most likely to contain that data.* **REG-F-110:** the anchor census could not run under the runner that mutates anchors. **REG-F-113:** prose ABOUT a status counted as a status. **Here:** a fixture QUOTING a timeout counted as a timeout. The repair is the same one all three chose — **separate the signal STRUCTURALLY at the narrowest rule that does it, rather than loosening the check.** Each marker is now anchored to the start of its line and the vitest ones require the `Error: ` prefix, which the runner emits and a quoted diff value never has. **Line-anchoring ALONE does not separate them**, because the diff prints the value at line start too — measured against the real output, not assumed.
- **THE RESIDUAL IS DISCLOSED AND ITS POLARITY IS WHY IT IS TOLERABLE.** A test that dumps a whole multi-line fixture into a diff, one of whose lines genuinely begins `Error: Test timed out in …ms`, would still be misread. That is **over**-detection, and over-detection here **fails CLOSED**: a loud BLOCKING `INCONCLUSIVE`, never a silent false KILL. **Under**-detection is the dangerous direction and the anchoring cannot cause it — a real runner diagnostic is always emitted on a line of its own.
- **THE EVIDENCE, AND THE PREDICTIONS MATCHED TO THE TEST.** Seven cases, **three of them controls**: a genuine assertion failure, a clean run, and — the one the mutants demanded — the real failure output copied verbatim from the run that exposed the second defect. Four mutants, each with its predicted red stated before the run: `F116-a-hung-arrangement-is-graded-as-a-kill` (1 red, the HOOK case), `F116-the-e2e-runner-loses-its-timeout-marker` (1, the Playwright case), `F116-the-instrument-reads-its-subjects-data-as-its-own-signal` (3 — **the shipped defect restored, not a hypothetical**), `F116-the-timeout-check-widens-and-nothing-is-ever-measured` (2, both controls — the failure a REPAIR would introduce). **All four KILLED; every predicted count matched.**
- **⚠ THE THING THIS DID NOT FIX, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR COVERED. `scripts/mutants/run.ts` is ~700 lines of gate logic that exports nothing and has never had a single assertion made about it.** `timeoutEvidence` is the first of it under test, and it is under test only because it was extracted to be. **The instrument that grades every guard in this repository is itself ungraded** — the same question `feedback_check_the_instrument_itself` asks, one turn further. The WIRING half of this fix is proved by the driven counterfactual above, **not by any standing test**, and it will stay that way until `run.ts`'s verdict attribution is extracted behind a seam. Named here as the next V-4 increment rather than left to be re-derived.
- **A RECORDS DEFECT FOUND WHILE CHOOSING THIS ID, and the search is stated because the near-miss was mine.** `REG-F-115` is allocated in commit `689ac61b`'s subject line and has **no entry in this register**: `git grep REG-F-115` over the tracked tree returns **0 files**, and the same search across `docs/` returns **0**. *Positive control:* `REG-F-114` returns **10 files** repo-wide and **1** entry header here. ⚠ **My first pass also reported REG-F-105, REG-F-106 and REG-F-108 as missing, and that was an artifact of the probe** — their headers are struck (`### ~~REG-F-105~~`), so a `### <id>` match misses them; grepping the id itself finds all three. **A false absence produced by matching the decoration rather than the content**, which is REG-F-113's subject arriving inside the search for it. **Safe default:** an id allocated in a commit message is not an entry, and no count of this register's findings may be taken from `git log`.
- **⚠ THE ENTRY ABOVE WAS WRITTEN, COMMITTED, AND THEN THE NEXT GATE RUN PROVED THE FIX WAS ONE SIZE TOO SMALL. Recorded in place rather than as a new finding, because the mistake is *inside* this one.** The full run reported **three declared CONTROLS as `SURVIVED — declared a CONTROL, but a test FAILED on it — something asserts on prose`**. There is no such test. **One unrelated red — a pinned literal in another package's unit test — produced three false findings.** V-4b caught the TIMEOUT case *because a timeout was the instance I had seen*. The general fact is that **a whole-suite run cannot attribute its failure to the mutation AT ALL**; a timeout is merely one way for it to fail. **Recording a general form is not the same as fixing it, and the gate said so on its very next run.**
- **THE SECOND FIX — a control is graded on the DIFFERENCE, not on an exit code.** An unmutated whole-suite BASELINE is taken **once, before the loop**, and only when a control is selected. A failing control that adds **no new red** HELD — and the disclosure travels *with* the verdict, because *"held against a red baseline"* is a weaker statement than *"held against a green one"*. A genuinely new red now **NAMES the suites it reddened** instead of asserting a cause, which was the entirety of V-4a's cost. ⚠ **The baseline is taken BEFORE any mutation reaches disk, deliberately:** taken lazily inside `runMutant` it would contain the mutant being graded against it — *a control that cannot fail, arriving inside the fix for controls that could not pass.* Named-victim mutants are untouched: **170 of 174 distinct mutations stay measurable against a red baseline**, since each runs only its own suite.
- **⚠ AND THERE WAS A FAIL-OPEN INSIDE THE FIX FOR A FAIL-OPEN, found by reading my own diff rather than by running anything.** `failedFiles` returned `[]` for BOTH *"the run reported no failures"* and *"there is no report"*. A control whose run crashed without writing one would have been graded **CONTROL_HELD** — the exact verdict this entry exists to stop being manufactured. It now returns `undefined` for the second, which a control reads as INCONCLUSIVE and the baseline treats as a hard stop. **The two states mean opposite things and the empty array conflated them.**
- **THE THIRD TURN, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT GENERALISES BEYOND THIS GATE. Asking the general form AGAIN turned the finding from an instance into a POPULATION — and the population was measurable rather than guessable.** The criterion is not *"which tests look expensive"* — that is enumeration, and it would have optimised files that cost nothing while missing the ones that mattered. **The criterion is DURATION AGAINST DECLARED BUDGET, and the suite already emits it.** Measured **with a second vitest running**, because that is the real condition — another agent is working in this repository and the machine is shared, so isolated numbers hide the whole defect.
- **WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND: FIVE MORE FILES CARRYING V-4a's EXACT DEFECT — the same bytes read again per item.** `trigger-claim-truth` re-parsed the transition vocab **per arrow** (304, some twice via the fallthrough — ~400 parses in one test). `canon-provenance` re-read the **3100-line register per clause** *and* every canon sidecar per clause — **so it degraded on the same schedule V-4a did, and for the same reason: this register grows every time a finding is recorded.** `arrow-command-census` re-parsed **every handler file with the TypeScript compiler** on each of `declaredArrows` and `birthStates`, the former called three times in one test file. `dead-kernel-census` read every production `.ts` and scanned it per kernel export, from both the census test and its CONTROL. `authority-resolution-census` walked and read the whole production tree **once per each of four tests**.
- **THE NUMBERS, LOADED — the condition that decides a gate.** `arrow-census-coverage` CONTROL **4345ms → 17022ms FAIL**; `canon-provenance` **1489 → 15933 FAIL**; `source-is-reviewable` **1137 → 11032 FAIL**; `dead-kernel-census` CONTROL **1024 → 6013 FAIL**; `authority-resolution` CONTROL **1059 → 5082 FAIL**. **Amplification of 4–10× is far more than CPU contention explains — it is I/O between workers**, and the fix is to stop asking for the same bytes. After: **verif's loaded test time 95.31s → 34.78s, four failures → ZERO.**
- **⚠ THE RULE FOR WHEN A TIMEOUT MAY BE RAISED, because V-4a refused to and was right, and the sixth file here does raise one.** V-4a's test was doing **168 MB of REDUNDANT I/O** — a bigger budget would have left the waste and the gate one slow machine from a false verdict. `source-is-reviewable` reads every authored file **exactly once**; there is nothing to remove, and its corpus grew when `packages/csaa` added ~680 files to the tree it walks. **A test whose cost is REDUNDANT must be fixed at the cause; a test whose cost is INHERENT should DECLARE a budget that fits it rather than run against a default describing a different kind of test.** The distinction is written into the file, with the standing question for the next person who wants to raise it again: *has the walk started reading something it does not review?*
- **MEMOIZATION SAFETY WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED** — a memoized structure that a caller mutates is a corruption that a green suite can hide. Searched every memoized result for in-place `sort`/`push`/`splice`/`set`/`delete`: none. `occupiable()` copies births into fresh `Set`s rather than aliasing them. **Every census pin still holds**, which is the live control: these tests exist to pin exact numbers, so a corrupted shared structure reddens them.
- **THE RESIDUAL, DISCLOSED WITH ITS POLARITY.** External load on a shared machine is not controllable from inside this repository, so a whole-suite run can still tip. **That is exactly what `INCONCLUSIVE` is for**, and it is the designed response rather than a gap: the gate blocks and says *"not measured"*, instead of manufacturing a finding about code that was never exercised.
- **⚠ THE LESSON THAT OUTLIVES THE GATE, and it amends this programme's own standing practice.** *Asking the general form is not a single act — each answer exposed the next size up.* **Instance** (one slow test) → **attribution** (every control graded on an exit code that cannot answer the question) → **population** (five more files, found by a derived criterion rather than a hand-list). **I stopped at the first level, wrote the entry, and shipped a gate that still manufactured false findings.** The tell that a general form is not general enough: it names a mechanism (*a timeout*) rather than a capability (*attribution*). **Ask again until the answer is about what the instrument can and cannot know.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/measured.ts`, `scripts/mutants/run.ts`, `verif/mutant-verdict.test.ts`, four ledger entries, and the six repaired suites (`trigger-claim-truth.ts`, `canon-provenance.ts`, `arrow-command-census.ts`, `dead-kernel-census.test.ts`, `authority-resolution-census.test.ts`, `source-is-reviewable.test.ts`). **Safe default:** no `KILLED` verdict from a run predating this fix may be quoted as evidence for a guard whose victim is slow, and no `SURVIVED` on a CONTROL from such a run may be read as a finding about the code.
- **✅ CLOSED ON A FULL GREEN GATE, and the green is attributable rather than lucky.** `KILLED 167 · SURVIVED 0 · UNANCHORED 0 · NO_COMPILE 0 · KILLED_UNNAMED 0 · CONTROL_HELD 5 · INCONCLUSIVE 0` over **174 distinct mutations**. ⚠ **The suite was NOT green when this passed, and that is the proof rather than a caveat:** the baseline reported `1 suite(s) ALREADY RED before any mutation — packages/csaa/src/subject/subject.test.ts`, and each control reported `held on the DIFFERENCE; 1 suite(s) already red without it`. **Before this entry those same five controls would have reported SURVIVED.** Re-verified by driving one control on its own after the full run, because a summary line is not an attribution.

### REG-F-117 — REG-F-114's recorded remedy for `advanceIntent` was WRONG: the Intent arrows were declared and enforced all along, and only the MACHINE was unrecoverable
- **Date:** 2026-08-12 · **Type:** CORRECTION to a recorded remedy (REG-F-114) + INCREMENT · **Status:** ✅ BUILT — coverage 164 → 170 arrows / 15 → 16 machines, three mutants KILLED on exact predicted counts.
- **WHAT REG-F-114 RECORDED, VERBATIM:** *"NOT BUILT: `advanceIntent` — five call sites, **identical shape**, deliberately a separate slice."* Its ruling had named the increment as a `PWU_LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_SPECS`-style table for Intent, *"the same for `advanceIntent`"*.
- **⚠ IT IS NOT AN IDENTICAL SHAPE, AND THE DIFFERENCE INVERTS THE WORK. Every one of the five sites ALREADY DECLARED ITS SOURCE SET, and it was ALREADY ENFORCED.** `precondition: fromStates(...)` — `RAW`, `UNDER_DISCOVERY`, `PROVISIONAL`, `FORMALIZED`+`REVISED`, `APPROVED` — **required by the type** since JAN-CMDPRE DWP-06 (D5), evaluated by `advanceIntent` *before* the precheck and *before* `checkTransition`, with the `FROM_STATES` arm of `evaluatePrecondition` minting the code and a widening mutant already in the enforcement register. **And `verif/arrow-command-census.ts` already knew how to read `fromStates`** — that branch has existed since the `advanceStatus` idiom landed.
- **SO REG-F-114's HEADLINE IS TRUE FOR PWU AND FALSE FOR INTENT.** *"The census is not under-reading, the COMMANDS are under-declaring"* was derived from `advancePwuLifecycle`, which genuinely took `{ target }` and had **no `from` at all**. Generalising that to the other machine was the error. **The only fact the census could not recover for Intent was WHICH MACHINE**, because the primitive closed over a module constant (`const MACHINE = 'Intent.intentStatus'`) instead of being told.
- **THE FIX IS ONE REQUIRED FIELD — no spec table, no new check, no control flow moved.** `advanceIntent` takes `machine` and passes it to `checkTransition`, which makes its call sites structurally identical to `kit.advanceStatus` in exactly the three dimensions the census reads: `machine`, `target`, and `fromStates` inside `precondition`. **The census therefore grows by a NAME in a set, not by a code path** — REG-F-114's own warning was that *"widening a reader is how C-0b dropped 30%"*, and this is the third option that ruling named: **make the idiom self-declaring**, applied to a command family that was already 2/3 self-declaring.
- **⚠ `args.machine`, NOT THE MODULE CONSTANT — and that substitution is the whole difference between a field and a hollow.** All five sites pass the same value, so had the primitive kept closing over `MACHINE`, the field would have been declared five times, read by nothing, and unkillable: **a hollow authored inside the fix for an invisibility**, which is this programme's most-repeated defect. **MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED:** declaring a machine the command does not drive validates an Intent arrow against the PWU machine — which has no `RAW` state — and applying it by hand reddens **4 of 6 tests in `intent.test.ts`**.
- **PREDICTED FROM THE MACHINE BEFORE IMPLEMENTING, AND IT MATCHED TO THE ARROW.** `Intent.intentStatus` declares **15** arrows; the five handlers claim **6**. Measured after: `arrowsSeen` **164 → 170**, `machinesSeen` **15 → 16**, C-0 `uncovered` **153 → 147**, `orphans` **10 → 9**, `unanalysed` **2 → 3**. The C-0 baseline was re-pinned with `PIN_ARROW_BASELINE=1` — from `census()` itself, never from a report — and **names exactly the six arrows derived beforehand**.
- **THE ORPHANS/UNANALYSED SWAP IS NOT A REGRESSION, and it is the same step PWU made.** A machine can only join `unanalysed` by **first becoming visible**: Intent now has arrows and no declared birth. **So REG-F-086's birth work is unblocked for Intent on exactly the argument that unblocked it for PWU** — and both are blocked by the same known mechanism, that the birth census reads only `createObject(...)` while `captureIntent`/`proposePwu` never call it.
- **WHAT IS NOW VISIBLE THAT WAS NOT: nine Intent arrows NO command performs** — six to `SUPERSEDED` (from every state) and three to `WITHDRAWN` (from `RAW`, `UNDER_DISCOVERY`, `PROVISIONAL` **only**). ⚠ **That asymmetry is ratified design, not an oversight:** an intent is WITHDRAWN before it is formalized and SUPERSEDED after. They remain in `uncovered`, pinned by name — cause **(a)**, nothing performs them, rather than a census defect. **This is precisely the value REG-F-114 predicted a declaration buys: an arrow nobody implements becomes UNIMPLEMENTED-and-visible instead of invisible.**
- **⚠ A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FOUND IN THE READING, recorded because a mutant would otherwise "repair" it.** `ApproveIntent` declares `fromStates('FORMALIZED', 'REVISED')` — authored **from the MACHINE** and deliberately **wider** than the vocab's `drivesFrom`, which says `FORMALIZED` only (DS-001 D4: the vocab has no ratified authority and is narrower than the machine here). It is the **only multi-source site**, which is what makes it the discriminating case: five sites yielding six arrows is the entire claim, and a reader that counted SITES would report five and be indistinguishable from a correct one everywhere else.
- **THE EVIDENCE — three mutants, every predicted count exact.** `F117-the-census-stops-reading-advanceIntent` (**2** red: the coverage pin and the blind set), `F117-a-site-declares-a-machine-it-does-not-drive` (**4** red in `intent.test.ts`), `F117-the-only-multi-source-site-loses-an-arrow` (**1** red: `arrowsSeen` 170 → 169). **All KILLED.** The relational CONTROL — *"census-blindness and C-0c-unanalysability are different failures"* — **stayed green throughout**, which is what it was rewritten to do: it does not redden with the herd when coverage merely moves.
- **⚠ ALSO CORRECTED WHILE HERE (P-5), and it is the same disease one layer down.** The blind-set comment read *"the four PWU axes and Intent.intentStatus"* while the list beside it already held **three** — `PWU.workLifecycleState` left under REG-F-114 and the prose was never re-read. **A count in prose beside a list that is pinned BY NAME is a count nothing checks**, so it rotted silently through one increment and would have rotted through this one.
- **THE GENERAL FORM, and it is about remedies rather than arrows.** *A recorded remedy is a hypothesis about code the recorder did not re-open.* REG-F-114 wrote "identical shape" while holding `advancePwuLifecycle` in mind, and the sentence read as a finding for two days. **Executing it would have built a spec table duplicating a declaration that already existed, added a second enforcement path beside a working one, and reported the arrows as newly declared** — coverage would have moved by the same +6 and every number would have looked right. **The check that costs nothing is opening the file the remedy names before writing the increment that obeys it.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/intent.ts`, `verif/arrow-command-census.ts`, `verif/arrow-census-coverage.test.ts`, `verif/arrow-command-census.baseline.json`, three ledger entries. **Safe default (REG-F-087's, updated):** no count from the arrow census may be described as complete — **it now describes 56% (170 of 304)**, and what remains missing is missing for two DIFFERENT reasons that must not be conflated: commands whose idiom the census cannot read, and arrows no command performs at all.

### REG-F-118 — NO dead-arrow claim in this repository was ever sound: occupancy answered a question its evidence could not support
- **Date:** 2026-08-12 · **Type:** INSTRUMENT DEFECT (C-0 / C-0c / C-0d, since each was written) + INCREMENT (REG-F-086's births) · **Status:** ✅ FIXED — `dead` 11 → 2 and both survivors are PROVABLE; verif green (176). **The mutation gate has NOT been run on this and is OWED.**
- **HOW IT SURFACED, AND IT WAS NOT WHAT I SET OUT TO DO.** The increment was REG-F-086: declare the births for `Intent.intentStatus` and `PWU.workLifecycleState`, which REG-F-114 and REG-F-117 had just unblocked by giving both machines arrows to grow along. Declaring the PWU birth made the machine analysable — and the census immediately reported **35 dead arrows**. ⚠ **They were false.**
- **THE CAUSE, AND THE SHAPE OF IT IS THE FINDING.** `PWU.workLifecycleState` has **49 of 57** arrows declared, and the eight undeclared ones form **A SPINE WITH ONE FORK** — ⚠ this first said *"ONE UNBROKEN CHAIN"*, named eight arrows and then drew **seven**: `READY → PLANNED → EXECUTING → EVIDENCE_PENDING → UNDER_ASSURANCE → SATISFIED → RECOMPOSING → RECOMPOSED`, **plus `UNDER_ASSURANCE → CONDITIONALLY_SATISFIED`**. `UNDER_ASSURANCE` has TWO out-arrows in the undeclared set, so the shape forks at the assurance verdict — which is exactly where a lifecycle SHOULD fork, and the tidier word hid it. **That is the main lifecycle spine the workbench drives every day.** Occupancy seeds from the birth and grows along DECLARED arrows, so it stopped at READY and called thirteen live states unreachable. **REG-F-114's +49 covered the PERIPHERY** — abandon, supersede, block, challenge — **and the happy path declares nothing.**
- **THEN THE GENERAL FORM, MEASURED RATHER THAN FEARED — every machine that emitted a dead arrow:** `PWU.workLifecycleState` 49/57 (35 dead), `Assumption.status` 9/17 (5), `Claim.status` 7/15 (4), `AssuranceAssessment.state` 11/19 (1), `ExecutionPlan.status` 10/11 (1). **NOT ONE dead-arrow claim in the repository rested on complete arrow coverage — including the eleven already sitting in the baseline.**
- **WHY THAT IS UNSOUND AND NOT MERELY IMPRECISE.** `occupiable()` grows along declared arrows, so a partial declaration set makes it an **UNDER-estimate**. Reachability can be proven (you got there); **UNreachability never can** — you may simply not have been able to see the road. *"Never occupied"* meant *"not shown reachable"*, and those are different claims. ⚠ **The polarity is the dangerous one: a DEAD arrow invites deleting code or a ratified arrow**, so acting on a false one removes something real.
- **THREE LAYERS READ IT AS UNREACHABILITY** — C-0's `deadCovered`, C-0c's `auditClaims` (`deadFrom`/`deadTo`), and C-0d through `auditClaims`. The rule now lives in ONE shared place, `occupancyAnalysable()`, **because a soundness rule that must be remembered in three readers is a rule that will hold in two.**
- **TWO GROUNDS NOW, AND KEEPING BOTH IS WHAT SAVED THE REAL FINDINGS.** ⚠ The SOUND one needs no coverage at all: **a state the ratified machine gives NO in-arrow, and no birth declares, can never be occupied — because the arrows that would rescue it do not exist to be declared.** The weaker, occupancy-based one is now gated on complete coverage. A sound rule and a weak one can disagree about the METHOD and still agree about the ANSWER.
- **✅ REG-F-088 AND REG-F-089 BOTH SURVIVE, ON BETTER GROUND THAN THEY HAD.** `ExecutionPlan.status` has **zero** ratified arrows into `PROPOSED` and its handler births `UNDER_REVIEW` — provable on 10/11 coverage, where the occupancy argument was worthless. **REG-F-089's three rows survive with their pin UNEDITED**: `REQUESTED`, `DRAFT` and `PROPOSED` are all birth-only states nothing births. ⚠ **A pin whose expectations survive a correction to its own instrument is evidence the finding was REAL rather than an artifact of how it was measured** — which is the question this entry forced about every deadness claim here, and the one those two can now answer yes to.
- **❌ REG-F-085's ROW IS WITHDRAWN, AND WITHDRAWN IS NOT FIXED — stated in the file so it cannot be misread as a repair.** Its claim was `RecompositionContract.status COMPOSABLE → SATISFIED [to SATISFIED is never occupied]`, derived from occupancy on a **7/15** machine. Unlike REG-F-088's, **`SATISFIED` DOES have a ratified in-arrow** — the very arrow under audit — so nothing proves it unreachable. **The underlying concern may still be real and is not disposed of:** W-4.6's `CompletePwuRecomposition` is blocked on exactly this. What changed is that this census may no longer be cited as the proof.
- **THE MEASUREMENTS.** `dead` **11 → 2**, both provable (`AssuranceAssessment.state REQUESTED → CANCELLED`, `ExecutionPlan.status PROPOSED → SUPERSEDED`). `unanalysed` **3 → 12** (C-0), **3 → 18** (C-0c), **3 → 11** (C-0d). ⚠ **Those lists GROWING is the census becoming honest, not weaker** — `unanalysed` now carries two causes that share a remedy but not a diagnosis: **no declared birth**, and **incomplete arrow coverage**. **Only four machines in the repository have every ratified arrow declared**, so only four can support an unreachability claim at all.
- **⚠ THREE MISTAKES OF MINE, ALL CAUGHT BY CONTROLS RATHER THAN BY ME, ALL RECORDED WHERE THEY HAPPENED.** (1) I gated `auditBirth` behind the completeness rule too — it reads `births` and never consults occupancy, so it was SOUND, and the control pinning the five REG-F-068 rows went red. **A soundness rule applied one scope too wide removes true findings.** (2) I then rewrote that control to expect `deadFrom === []`, believing the detections lost; **they were not** — the sound ground re-derives all three, and the control's ORIGINAL numbers were right. (3) I briefly added an exported no-op to hold a docstring — **a hollow, inside the fix for a census.** Deleted.
- **THE INCREMENT THAT STARTED IT, which did land.** `refuseOnBirthDrift` extracted and shared by `createObject` and `commitState`; `births` declared for `Intent.intentStatus` (RAW) and `PWU.workLifecycleState` (PROPOSED), read off the state each command actually commits rather than off `initialState`, which lies for five machines (REG-F-071); `BIRTH_PRIMITIVES` as a NAME in a set, per REG-F-117; and a **RATCHET** — a `commitState` site that creates (`expectedRevision: undefined`) and declares no `births` now FAILS the census. ~~⚠ Its one exemption is STRUCTURAL — *"this call sits inside another birth primitive"*, which is `createObject` delegating — **not a list of exempt files, which would rot into an allowlist the first time someone added a creation to one of them.**~~ **⚠ STRUCK: THAT EXEMPTION WAS DELETED AT `8f580e84`, TWO COMMITS AFTER THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN, BECAUSE ITS OWN MUTANT SURVIVED.** `handlerFiles()` has excluded `kit.ts` since long before any of this, so the census never walks `createObject`'s delegating call and the exemption guarded a case that **cannot arise** — a hollow, authored inside the fix for a census. The ratchet is now **unconditional**, and the argument above (structural beats a file allowlist) was sound reasoning about a problem that did not exist. **Struck rather than rewritten, because an entry that quietly acquires the right answer hides that the wrong one was believed and defended in prose.**
- **THE GENERAL FORM, and it is the reusable part.** *An instrument that reasons FORWARD from a seed can prove presence but never absence, and every negative claim it makes carries an unstated completeness precondition.* This one had been making negative claims for as long as it existed, and each was believed because the positive half was correct. **The question to ask of any census: what would have to be TRUE about my inputs for this NEGATIVE answer to be justified — and do I check it?**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/{kit,intent,pwu}.ts`, `verif/{arrow-command-census,binding-row-truth}.ts`, three pinned suites, `verif/arrow-command-census.baseline.json`. **Safe default:** no `dead`/`deadFrom`/`deadTo` verdict from a run predating this entry may be quoted as evidence, and no new one may be quoted for a machine outside `occupancyAnalysable()` unless it rests on the zero-in-arrow ground. **OWED:** the mutation gate on this increment; mutants for both deadness grounds and for the birth ratchet; and the eight PWU spine arrows, whose absence is now a named finding rather than a silence.

### REG-F-119 — the PWU's MAIN SPINE was performed by the generic setter and declared by nothing; declaring it makes the first PWU axis analysable, and proves REG-F-118's withdrawal was right
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** INCREMENT (REG-F-118's named residue) + a DESIGN corrected before it was built · **Status:** ✅ BUILT — 170 → 178 arrows, `PWU.workLifecycleState` at 57/57, three mutants resolved as predicted.
- **WHO PERFORMS THEM, which is the question REG-F-118 named but did not answer.** The eight arrows are **not unimplemented**. `ChangePwuState` — the GENERIC setter — performs every one, and its target is `payload.newState`, resolved at RUNTIME. ⚠ **Its call site therefore declares NOTHING** — not a destination, let alone an arrow. ### REG-F-120 — an audit of THIS SESSION'S OWN 26 COMMITS: two defects inside the fixes, one of which arms itself when the repository gets healthier
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** INSTRUMENT DEFECT (mine, found by auditing my own increments) · **Status:** FIXED — one with a mutant, one deliberately without and the absence recorded.
- **WHY THE AUDIT WAS RUN AT ALL, and the reason is a measurement rather than a mood.** Across this session I shipped **nine defects of my own and not one was caught by my own review** — each died to a control or an independent reader. Three hollows, two over-corrections, a stale count, an expired premise, a mutant that measured the compiler, and a superlative contradicting a number I had taken one step earlier. **A fix's own author is the worst-placed reader of it**, so the fixes were audited by readers who had not written them: five dimensions over `2ac7b046..HEAD`, each finding then refuted independently. **37 raised, 23 survived.** The two below were verified by hand before anything was changed.
- **① THE LEAKED CONTROL REPORT — a fail-open walking around the fail-open fix.** `controlVerdict`'s passing arm returns `CONTROL_HELD` **without calling `failedFiles`**, and only `failedFiles` deletes. So a control that PASSES leaves `.control-run.json` on disk, and the next control that exits non-zero **without writing one** reads the stale file, sees `[]`, computes `fresh.length === 0`, and is graded HELD — **precisely the hole the `reported === undefined` arm was added to close**, walked around by a file that outlived its run.
- **⚠ AND THE AUDITOR HAD ITS REACHABILITY BACKWARDS, WHICH MAKES IT WORSE RATHER THAN BETTER.** It is **not live today**: one suite is red, so every control exits non-zero, takes the differencing path, and `failedFiles` deletes the report on the way through — **verified by running a control and finding no file**. **It arms itself the day that suite goes green**, when controls begin passing and the report begins surviving. **A defect whose precondition is *"the gate is finally clean"* is the worst kind to leave for later**, because it waits for the moment everyone stops looking. Fixed by deleting BEFORE the spawn, which also covers an invocation killed mid-flight.
- **② THE PLAYWRIGHT ANCHOR WAS GUARDED BY NOTHING — and REG-F-116's own conclusion is why I would not have found it.** That entry recorded *"the runner's own prefix does [the separating]"*. **True, and measured — for VITEST.** Drop `^[ \t]*` from the vitest markers and all cases stay green, because the `Error: ` prefix carries the whole load. ⚠ **The Playwright marker has NO prefix.** Its line anchor is its entire defence, and **every poisoning fixture written for REG-F-116 was vitest-shaped**, so dropping THAT anchor was green too — measured, 7 passed. **A reader could have deleted it as redundant, correctly reasoning from the vitest evidence, and re-opened the self-poisoning hole on the e2e path alone.** A quoted-Playwright fixture now objects; predicted red driven first — the drop reddens that control **alone**, 1 failed / 7 passed.
- **THE GENERAL FORM, and it is about EVIDENCE rather than about anchors.** *A conclusion measured on one instance of a class gets written as a conclusion about the class.* REG-F-116 tested two vitest markers, found the prefix sufficient, and recorded a general rule; the third marker had different structure and inherited a defence it does not have. **The tell is a summary sentence with no quantifier** — "the prefix does the separating" names no population. **Ask of any such sentence: measured on how many of what, and is the untested member structurally the same?**
- **⚠ ONE FIX HAS NO MUTANT, DELIBERATELY, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE RECORD.** ① guards a condition no current test can reach, so **a mutant for it would report SURVIVED and be right to**. Declaring one anyway would either block the gate on a false finding or teach the next person to weaken the mutant until it passed — which is how a ledger starts lying. This repository set the precedent and states it in `run.ts`: the atomicity guard *"shipped with no ledger entry and a comment saying so"*, because **a fake measurement is worse than a declared absence**. It becomes killable the day the suite goes green, which is the same day it becomes necessary; the ledger note says to add the mutant then.
- **WHAT WAS REFUSED, because a refuter defended it and was right.** Two proposed citation "corrections" would have **broken correct references** — one was byte-exact at its authoring commit and only drifted when a LATER commit inserted a line above it. **Damaging working content to satisfy a finding is the failure an audit list must not cause**, and an auditor confident enough to file it is exactly why the refutation pass exists.

The `OwnedLifecycleTarget` hollow is resolved IN PLACE at `handlers/pwu.ts:465-475`: kept, narrowly scoped — *“a NAME for the owned set … with NO enforcement behind it. ### REG-F-121 — every coverage percentage this census ever published divided DECLARATION ROWS by RATIFIED ARROWS; and the split exposed 19 declared arrows no machine ratifies
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** MEASUREMENT DEFECT (inherited, quoted in five entries) + a finding it exposed · **Status:** CORRECTED and both figures pinned; **the 19 unratified declarations are OPEN and deliberately undecided.**
- **THE DEFECT.** `arrowsSeen` counted one row per `(site, source, target)` and was divided by the machines' ratified arrow total. Two different populations. Measured: **178 declaration rows · 175 distinct arrows declared · 156 of those RATIFIED · 19 declared but not ratified.** So the published *"178 of 304 = 59%"* is really **156 of 304 = 51%**, and the same arithmetic produced 38%, 54% and 56% before it.
- **TWO THINGS THAT ARE TRUE AND EASY TO LOSE IN A CORRECTION.** The inflation is **INHERITED** — the gap existed at 170 rows and at 115 — so no increment introduced it. And **the DIRECTION of every claim was right**: each increment really did add covered arrows, REG-F-119's eight among them. What was wrong is the absolute figure. ⚠ **A legitimate arrow declared by TWO commands counts twice** (`SkipExecutionStep` and `PruneExecutionStep` both reach `SKIPPED`); that is correct behaviour for a ROW count and wrong for a COVERAGE count, which is the whole confusion in one example.
- **BOTH NUMBERS ARE NOW PINNED, because they answer different questions and conflating them IS the defect.** `declarationRows` is about the **READER** — did an idiom stop being read? `ratifiedArrowsCovered` is about the **PRODUCT** — how much of the ratified surface can any command perform? **A change to one and not the other is itself information**, and a single field could not express it.
- **⚠ THE SECOND FINDING, PINNED SO IT CANNOT DRIFT WHILE IT IS OPEN: NINETEEN DECLARED ARROWS ARE RATIFIED BY NO MACHINE.** Commands declaring transitions the corpus does not have. Several are **self-transitions** — `Claim.status SUPPORTED -> SUPPORTED` and kin — which is the **HOLD** shape the generic setter also produces and which the machines do not model. **Whether the declarations are wrong or the machines are incomplete is UNDECIDED and must not be guessed.** Pinned by count so the question stays visible; absorbed into a coverage number is exactly where it has been for this census's entire life. **⚠ CORRECTED BY REG-F-124 (2026-08-13): NINETEEN became FIFTEEN, and the four that left REFUTE THE DICHOTOMY THIS BULLET STATES.** The question *"whether the declarations are wrong or the machines are incomplete"* admits exactly two answers, and for four of its own members BOTH are false — the four `ValidatorRegistryEntry.status` rows were declared by no command and ratified by no machine, because the CENSUS minted them. **A third category — arrows nothing declares at all — that the pinned question could not express.** The count is corrected in `arrow-census-coverage.test.ts`; this sentence is corrected here, because a number fixed beside prose that still frames it wrongly is REG-F-121's own defect recurring.
- **THE PRIOR ENTRIES ARE NOT EDITED, and that is deliberate.** REG-F-087, REG-F-114, REG-F-117, REG-F-118 and REG-F-119 each quote a percentage computed this way. **They stand as records of what was measured and believed at the time** — rewriting their numbers would falsify the audit record in the name of tidying it, which is the opposite of what this register is for (`feedback_retire_by_striking_not_deleting`). This entry supersedes the figures; the entries keep their history.
- **⚠ HOW IT WAS MISSED, AND THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE KIND OF CHECK.** I rewrote this census's header **one commit before** this finding — carefully restating 38% → 54% → 56% → 59% as a derivation, having verified each number against its pin. **Every number was faithfully copied and the arithmetic underneath was never questioned.** Correcting a STALE number is not the same as auditing WHAT THE NUMBER MEASURES: the first checks a value against a source, the second asks whether the source computes the thing its name claims. **I have now done the first three times this session and the second once, and only the second found anything.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `verif/arrow-census-coverage.test.ts`. **Safe default (supersedes REG-F-087's and REG-F-119's):** the arrow census covers **51% (156 of 304)** of the ratified surface; `declarationRows` is not a coverage figure and may not be quoted as one; and no conclusion may rest on the remaining 148 being a single kind of gap — they are commands whose idiom the census cannot read, arrows nothing performs, and now a third category, arrows declared against a machine that does not ratify them.

### REG-F-122 — the census's own from-half inference is DELETED, and the one site that used it now declares at the literal
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** INSTRUMENT DEFECT (the census violating its own ruling; surfaced by REG-F-119's adversarial pass, worked as its own increment) · **Status:** FIXED — declaration + ratchet + synthetic-fixture victims + one mutant.
- **THE DEFECT, AS RECORDED WHEN IT WAS FOUND.** `arrow-command-census.ts:322` closed the SOURCES walk with `sources ?? def!.transitions.filter((t) => t.to === to).map((t) => t.from)`: when no `fromStates(…)` was readable, the census silently substituted the MACHINE's in-edges for the site's declaration — the exact inference REG-F-114 forbade, live inside the instrument that enforces REG-F-114. One site of 46 reached it: `governance.ts:293`, where `makeDecisionEffective` passed `precondition` as a SHORTHAND property bound to a factory parameter. **The declaration existed** — both callers composed `fromStates('PROPOSED')` — the walk just could not see through the name, so the site was read as "not narrowed by source state".
- **MEASURED NIL EFFECT, AND WHY THAT IS LUCK RATHER THAN SOUNDNESS.** `Decision.status` ratifies a SINGLE in-arrow to EFFECTIVE (`PROPOSED`), so the fabricated set coincided with the declared one and every census number was accidentally right. I predicted the count would DROP before looking; the machine's shape says it cannot move at all, and the re-pin agreed — `declarationRows` 178, `distinctArrowsDeclared` 175, `ratifiedArrowsCovered` 156, bit-identical. The spine design doc's caution (*"the arrow count can MOVE"*) was the right reason to make this its own increment and wrong about the direction: the coincidence is the finding.
- **THE FIX HAS TWO HALVES, AND THE ORDER WAS RED-FIRST.** (a) THE RATCHET: the walk now REFUSES what it cannot read — a shorthand or bare-identifier `precondition` fails as UNINSPECTABLE (the declaration may exist behind the name; misdiagnosing it as absent is the V-4a class), and a visible precondition with NO readable `fromStates` fails instead of inheriting the machine's in-edges. The inference expression NO LONGER EXISTS in the census. Landed first, alone: all four coverage pins failed naming `governance.ts:293` verbatim — the predicted red, measured. (b) THE DECLARATION: `fromStates('PROPOSED')` hoisted into the factory's `advanceStatus` literal; callers now pass their KIND predicate, and ApproveDecision's version-pin check rides as a POST-STATE precondition so composition stays kind → state → pin. Refusal codes unchanged — 867 rph-application tests green, unmodified.
- **THE POSITIVE CASE LEFT THE POPULATION IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE GUARD, so the guard is held by SYNTHETIC sources.** Every failing arm's only live instance was the site the same commit fixed — the `insideBirthPrimitive` lesson (REG-F-120) arriving as a foreseen event instead of a discovered one. The per-file walk is exported as a seam (`declaredArrowsInFile(sf)`) and four fixtures in `arrow-command-census.test.ts` are the arms' entire population: shorthand, bare-name, predicate-only, and a two-source reading CONTROL against a throw-on-everything walk.
- **THE MUTANT, AND WHAT ONLY THE FIXTURE CAN KILL.** `F122-the-census-resumes-inferring-the-from-half` restores the deleted expression VERBATIM. Measured before declaring: the predicate-only fixture reddens ALONE (1 failed / 9 passed) — and every repo-wide pin stays GREEN under the resurrection, because after the fix all 46 real sites declare readable `fromStates` and the fallback is dead code against the live tree. The pins cannot hold this; the fixture is the assertion.
- **ONE ARM IS DIAGNOSIS, NOT DEFENCE, AND NO MUTANT PRETENDS OTHERWISE.** Dropping the uninspectable-name arm leaves both name shapes REFUSED by the general arms (a shorthand is not a PropertyAssignment; an identifier initializer contains no `fromStates`) — with a message that misdiagnoses the cause. A mutant over it would SURVIVE and be right to, so none is declared; recording that here is the record.
- **RESIDUAL, NAMED SO IT CANNOT PASS AS COVERED.** A precondition composed inside a HELPER whose callee holds the `fromStates` is still invisible to the walk — and the failure direction is now SAFE: a loud false refusal at the site, never a silent fabrication. If that idiom is ever wanted, it is taught deliberately, with its own ruling.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/governance.ts` (factory + both callers), `verif/arrow-command-census.ts` (seam + ratchet, inference deleted), `verif/arrow-command-census.test.ts` (four fixtures), one ledger entry. **Safe default (retires REG-F-119's):** the from-half of every advance-site arrow is DECLARED AT THE SITE or the census fails loudly — *"declared, except one site inferred"* is struck, and arguments may now rest on universal declaration.

It did not, and the difference matters: **an intermittent blocker is worse than a persistent one, because a green run can be quoted as proof while the hazard sits exactly where it was.** A CONTROL_HELD earned on a run that happened not to time out is a measurement of THAT RUN, and the gate may re-block on any other. **REG-F-120 ① THEREFORE REMAINS DORMANT**, for precisely the reason its arming was predicted: the baseline suite is still red, so every control still exits non-zero, takes the differencing path, and deletes the report on the way through. The leaked-report mutant is **still not declarable** and the trigger recorded above **stands unfired** — checked, not assumed.
- **⚠⚠ SECOND UPDATE, 2026-08-17 — BOTH FIGURES IN ITEM (a) WERE WRONG, AND THE SECOND HAD NEVER BEEN OBSERVED BY ANY RUN.** The CSAA owner acted, and re-derived rather than copied: `scripts/tsconfig.json` is **6 → 8**, not 6→7 — this entry was written when only `scripts/mutants/measured.ts` had landed, and `verdict.ts` followed it — and `verif/tsconfig.json` is **40 → 45**, not 40→41, the merge adding `control-verdict`, `mutant-verdict`, `observation-command-surface`, `register-citations` and `unreachability-grounds` test files. ⚠ **The second was MASKED**: `subject.test.ts:1865` throws before `:1866` executes, so no run had ever seen that assertion, and applying the recorded 6→7 would have left the file red twice over. Both derived from each tsconfig's own include globs and corroborated three ways — filesystem enumeration, `git ls-tree` at the pre-merge HEAD (**6** and **40**, exactly the pinned values), and the merge's own add-list (**+2** and **+5**) — with the method validated BEFORE it was trusted by reconstructing four merge-INVARIANT pins (0, 28, 10, 82) on the nose. **Item (a) is DISCHARGED** at `0018a34b`; the suite-weight item (b) stands. See REG-F-195.

### REG-F-124 — the census's THIRD fabrication route: two factory parameters, flattened and crossed, minting four arrows no command ever declared
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** INSTRUMENT DEFECT (mine by inheritance, found by an adversarial audit I commissioned against my own finding) · **Status:** FIXED — pairing + a `fail()` arm + two synthetic fixtures + one mutant; the remaining question deliberately untouched.
- **THE DEFECT.** `factoryParameter` answers ONE parameter at a time and flattens its answers into a `Set`. When BOTH the target and the source list come from a factory's parameters, the emission loop crossed the two flattened sets — so `validator-registry.ts`'s `statusChange`, called four times, was read as `|∪targets| × |∪sources|` = **9 arrows where the calls declare 5**. **The correlation EXISTS in the source — each call binds its own (target, froms) — the reader discarded it and then re-inflated the remains into a rectangle.** Third route to the same wrong after REG-F-114 (inference from the machine) and REG-F-122 (its surviving fallback): **union, not inference.**
- **THE FOUR MANUFACTURED ARROWS,** all carrying `site: validator-registry.ts:82` and all sitting in REG-F-121's pinned unratified list as though a command had claimed them: `ACTIVE -> ACTIVE`, `DEGRADED -> DEGRADED`, `DISABLED -> DISABLED`, `DISABLED -> DEGRADED`.
- **⚠ THE AUDIT CORRECTED MY FINDING THREE TIMES, AND EVERY CORRECTION IS LOAD-BEARING.** I commissioned seven agents against my own claim. (1) **My arithmetic was wrong**: I wrote "N calls → N²"; the truth is `Σᵢ|targetsᵢ|×|sourcesᵢ| = 5` vs `|∪t|×|∪s| = 9` — `disableValidator` legitimately declares TWO (`['ACTIVE','DEGRADED'] -> DISABLED`), so any rule phrased in CALL COUNTS is false. (2) **The union is CONDITIONAL, not unconditional**: `factoryParameter` returns from the parameter's declared TYPE first and only falls through to the call-site union when the type carries no literal — `statusChange` falls through solely because it types `target: string`. (3) **The union loses the information; the CROSS PRODUCT mints the rows** — which is what scoped the fix. My prediction of the counts was right; **not one of my arguments for it was.**
- **THE HAZARD THAT DECIDED THE SCOPE, and it would have destroyed real coverage.** Two other sites emit full rectangles — `recordClaimAssessment` (5×4) and `authorizeRuntimeBinding` (2×2) — and at both the rectangle is DELIBERATE, documented at the site since 2026-08-06/08: *"Which DESTINATIONS are legal from each is the machine's judgement; duplicating it here would create a second, drifting copy of the arrow table."* A fix scoped to **"stop emitting rectangles"** would have dropped the ratified `Claim.status` arrows that rectangle really declares. **Scoped to the ARMS instead — both halves resolved through the CALL-SITE arm — exactly one site pairs today**, and `arm: 'type' | 'calls'` is now a load-bearing field rather than a diagnostic: a type is a RANGE with no per-call structure, and pairing one would invent tuples the source does not have.
- **⚠ AND IT MUST NEVER BE "FIXED" BY CONSULTING THE MACHINE.** Three of the four fabrications are self-edges, and `checkTransition` ADMITS `from === to` as a NOOP (`ValidatorRegistryEntry.status` declares `illegal: []`). A reader that filtered its own output against `STATE_MACHINES` would re-mint them — REG-F-114's forbidden inference wearing a filter's clothes. Recorded because it is the obvious repair.
- **MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED — and the control is the number that did NOT move.** `declarationRows` **178 → 174**, `distinctArrowsDeclared` **175 → 171**, the pinned unratified finding **19 → 15**, `machinesSeen` 16 unchanged, and the whole C-0 baseline (`uncovered`/`orphans`/`total`/`dead`/`unanalysed`) **bit-identical**. **`ratifiedArrowsCovered` stayed at 156** — as it did through REG-F-122. Two fabrication removals, zero ratified arrows lost, because a fabricated arrow is by construction one no machine ratifies. **If a future fabrication-removal moves that number, it removed truth as well and is not the same act.**
- **THE ARM WITH NO LIVE POSITIVE CASE, held the REG-F-122 way.** Under the union, a call passing a computed target was RESCUED by its literal-passing siblings; under pairing it contributes NOTHING, so a real declaration would vanish silently — the file header's own oldest lesson. That arm `fail()`s, and since all four live calls pass literals, **a synthetic fixture through `declaredArrowsInFile` is its entire population.** The pairing fixture is TWO calls with disjoint targets and disjoint sources, deliberately: one call cannot distinguish paired from crossed (a single tuple's cross product IS that tuple), and four would mirror the live site closely enough to pass by coincidence.
- **INDEPENDENT REPOSITORY-SIDE WITNESSES, found by the audit and verified here.** `verif/guard-enforcement-ledger.data.ts` enumerates the same **five** arrows per call site and never the four phantoms; `validator-registry.test.ts` is titled *"the five declared arrows"* and its `REFUSES arrows the machine does not declare` case **drives two of the four phantoms to a refusal** (`RestoreValidator`/`EnableValidator` from ACTIVE = `ACTIVE -> ACTIVE`; `MarkValidatorDegraded` from DISABLED = `DISABLED -> DEGRADED`), green, 10 passed. **The other two (`DEGRADED -> DEGRADED`, `DISABLED -> DISABLED`) are argued statically and NOT driven** — stated because the audit flagged exactly this as an unearned "cannot fire", and an undriven half must not shelter under a driven one.
- **DELIBERATELY NOT SETTLED HERE.** Whether the two remaining rectangles OVER-CLAIM is a question about what the SITES declare; this was a fix to what the READER fabricates, and folding them together would put one movement inside another. Also open and now sharper: the **DECLARED vs PERFORMABLE** framing in `docs/_working/DESIGN-the-nineteen-unratified.md` was authored by me this session and is **ratified nowhere**, while this file's own first line says it reports arrows a command *"can actually perform"* — the audit was right to flag that my reframe is doing load-bearing work it has not earned.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `verif/arrow-command-census.ts`, `verif/arrow-command-census.test.ts` (2 fixtures), `verif/arrow-census-coverage.test.ts` (both pins + the corrected dichotomy), one ledger entry. **Safe default:** the census's declared-arrow count is now "declared at the site, paired per call, inferred nowhere"; the 15 remaining unratified rows hold TWO populations — same-state HOLDS admitted as NOOPs by design (which need DECLARING, not ratifying) and genuine cross-state pairs — and no argument may treat them as one.

### REG-F-125 — one measurement, copied to fourteen comments in nine files, gated by nothing: it said FOUR and the answer was FIVE
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** RECORDS DEFECT (systemic — a claim about the code, asserted repeatedly, checked nowhere) · **Status:** FIXED — the claim is now DERIVED, pinned BY NAME, and the fourteen copies point at the pin instead of carrying a digit.
- **HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the method is the finding.** Four instances of "prose contradicting the code it documents" had been found this session ONE AT A TIME, by incidental reading. That is not a search, so the class was swept deliberately: six agents over 97 non-test files (2.3 MB), each partition's findings then handed to an adversarial refuter whose default was REFUTED. **69 findings survived refutation.** This entry is the first and highest-leverage of them; the rest are worked in their own increments.
- **THE DEFECT.** REG-F-071 measured that some machines declare an `initialState` no creation ever writes. The measurement was right when taken and was then COPIED — as the byte-identical clause **`a fiction on four machines`** — to **fourteen sites across nine files**: eight handlers, `verif/binding-row-truth.ts`, and this census's own docstring. **Nothing gated it.** `AssuranceAssessment.state` later joined the set when its request path moved to land in `EVIDENCE_PENDING|READY` instead of `REQUESTED`, and fourteen comments went on asserting four.
- **⚠ THE REPOSITORY HELD THREE DIFFERENT VALUES FOR ONE FACT, which is what a copied measurement decays into.** `a fiction on four machines` (×14), `lies for at least six machines` (`arrow-command-census.test.ts`), and `a fiction on several machines` (`trigger-claim-truth.test.ts`). **Only the vague one was not wrong** — it survived because it declined to say a number, which is a poor way for a claim to stay true.
- **DERIVED, NOT PATCHED — the answer is FIVE, and it is now nameable:** `AssuranceAssessment.state` (declares REQUESTED, born EVIDENCE_PENDING|READY) · `Baseline.status` (DRAFT / CANDIDATE) · `DecompositionContract.status` (DRAFT / UNDER_REVIEW) · `ExecutionPlan.status` (PROPOSED / UNDER_REVIEW) · `RecompositionContract.status` (DRAFT / READY). The old prose could not name one of them, which is why nobody could check it.
- **PINNED BY NAME AND NOT BY COUNT (REG-F-121's rule).** `toBe(5)` goes green when a machine is DELETED — the number improves by destroying the evidence. The pin lists each machine WITH the contradiction it carries (declared vs actually written), so a failure tells the reader which machine moved and how, rather than that a total changed.
- **⚠ THE SCOPE IS THE CARE OF IT, and getting it wrong would inflate a governance-facing number.** The derivation counts ONLY machines that declare a birth. A machine with no `births` declaration is not evidence that its `initialState` is a fiction — it is evidence that nothing here can tell, which is C-0c's `unanalysed` set and a different claim. **Six machines are in that state**, and folding them in would have produced "eleven" and read as a worse defect than exists. A CONTROL holds the scope; another holds the discriminating half (`Intent` and `PWU` are born exactly where they declare and must be ABSENT), because a pin listing five machines is equally satisfied by a function that calls every machine a liar.
- **THE MUTANT INVERTS THE PREDICATE, because that is the only way this derivation lies without looking broken.** `F125-the-fiction-census-reads-the-diagram-again` flips `!born.has(declared)` — the census then reports the machines that AGREE and stays silent about the five that do not, and **the resulting list is a similar length**, so a reader checking "is the number about right" sees nothing wrong. That is exactly how the original survived.
- **THE GENERAL FORM, and it is not "docstrings rot".** A measurement that is COPIED becomes a claim in N places with ONE origin and NO checker; the copies then outlive the fact, and the more load-bearing the original measurement was, the more widely it was copied. **The remedy is not to correct the copies — it is to delete the number from the prose and put it where something reads it.** Applied here: fourteen sites now say "a fiction on some machines (the set is DERIVED and pinned by name)" and the fact lives in one gated place.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `verif/arrow-command-census.ts` (`initialStateFictions()`), `verif/arrow-command-census.test.ts` (pin + 2 controls), ten files de-duplicated, one ledger entry. **Safe default:** no comment in this repository may state a COUNT of a code property unless a test derives that count; where one appears, it is to be replaced by a pointer to the deriving pin, not by a corrected digit.

### REG-F-126 — the stale-prose class, SWEPT instead of stumbled into: 69 findings, and four hazards that live in APPLYING an audit rather than in producing one
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** RECORDS DEFECT (systemic, repository-wide) + METHOD · **Status:** APPLIED — 59 re-anchored replacements (47 in LF files, 12 in the CRLF register), 3 docblock moves, 9 companion edits, across 21 files. REG-F-125 is the largest single finding and has its own entry.
- **WHY A SWEEP AT ALL.** Four instances of *prose that contradicts the code it documents* had been found in one session, every one by incidental reading. **Four found by accident is not a measurement of four; it is a measurement of how often I happened to look.** So the class was DERIVED: six agents over 97 non-test files (2.3 MB), partitioned by size, each partition's findings then handed to an adversarial refuter whose default was REFUTED. **69 survived refutation** — an order of magnitude more than incidental discovery had produced.
- **⚠ THE REPORT'S OWN CITATIONS WENT STALE BEFORE IT COULD BE APPLIED, which is the finding arriving inside its own remedy.** Between the sweep finishing and the fixes landing, REG-F-125 edited ten of the reported files, so line numbers in a report *about stale line numbers* had drifted. A second pass re-anchored every finding against HEAD **by CONTENT**, and re-derived every number a replacement asserted. **59 of 59 anchors resolved uniquely; zero skips.** Applying the first report directly would have introduced the defect it documents.
- **THE FOUR HAZARDS OF APPLYING AN AUDIT — the transferable part of this entry, because each is invisible in the findings themselves.**
  - **① BURIED COMPANIONS.** Ten required edits existed only inside `notes` prose, invisible to any runner reading the schema — and several were the OTHER HALF of a claim being changed. **A batch that corrects one half and drops the other MANUFACTURES the defect it is fixing**, and I proved it by doing it: batch 2 rewrote a header to *"FOUR DEAD PREDICATES"* while two sites forty lines away still said FIVE. Predicted by the adjudication before it happened, found by grep after.
  - **② HALF-APPLIABLE MOVES.** Three findings were RELOCATIONS, and the three specs disagreed about which half they carried: one held only the PASTE (duplicates — recoverable), one **only the CUT (deletes the docblock outright)**, one neither. Applied instead as ONE cut+paste per file, asserting the sorted line multiset is IDENTICAL before and after — a move that cannot be half-applied, and that refuses to write if one character of prose changed.
  - **③ THE LINE-ENDING BOUNDARY IS A BATCH BOUNDARY.** Exactly one of the 21 files (`enforcement-register.ts`) is CRLF; the LF form of its anchors matches ZERO times. A newline-normalising applier corrupts one group or the other, and a text-mode write there rewrites ~3100 lines and buries the change — which had already happened to me once this session. The register got its own pass, and its 62-insert / 36-delete diff is the evidence the handling held.
  - **④ A SUITE CAN SHRINK SILENTLY WHILE REPORTING GREEN.** Two replacements embedded RAW double quotes inside double-quoted TypeScript strings — byte-exact and syntactically invalid. The file stopped parsing and **vitest reported `176 passed` with ZERO failures**: one file had failed to transform and its 11 tests simply were not there. **A green run with a shrunken population is indistinguishable from a green run, unless the previous count is known.** Caught only because it was.
- **THE ANCHOR QUESTION, ASKED BECAUSE PROSE EDITS COULD SILENTLY DISARM THE MUTATION LEDGER.** Mutant anchors are literal `find` strings and several live inside comments the sweep rewrote, so a corrected comment could leave a mutant UNANCHORED and its guarantee unmeasured. Preflight over the whole ledger after all four batches: **185 applicable, 0 ROTTED.** The risk was real and did not land.
- **WHAT THE AGENTS GOT RIGHT, recorded because the previous two workflows got their arguments wrong.** **No number in any replacement was copied unverified.** Six specs caught their OWN finding's count being stale (a "13 §32 commands" that was 14; a "215" that was 216), and one **rejected an unsupported attribution outright** and derived its own partition instead — the defect class being fixed, reappearing inside its own fix, detected and stopped by the pass that was fixing it.
- **AND ONE ESCALATION WAS REFUTED ON THE CODE.** The sweep reported `transition-gate.ts` as hiding a live defect — *"with no evaluator every guarded arm is skipped and the first unconditional arm is silently selected … not fail-closed"*. Three checks say otherwise: `resolveBranchSelection` has ONE production caller and it DOES supply the evaluator; the grammar is FIRST-MATCH, stated at the head of the same file, so an unconditional arm preceding a conditional one is a match and not a bug; and with no evaluator and only conditional arms it returns `undefined`, which is fail-closed. **Both the withdrawal and the refutation are recorded at the site**, so the next reader does not re-raise a finding this one already answered.
- **THE GENERAL FORM, which is NOT "comments rot".** This repository writes long, load-bearing docblocks that record why a rule exists and what was ruled — which is why its prose is worth trusting, and exactly why a stale one is dangerous: it is detailed, authoritative, and wrong. The population splits into ORPHANED (a function inserted beneath an existing docstring silently reassigns it), SUPERSEDED (a claim withdrawn by a later edit, left standing), STALE MECHANISM, STALE NUMBER (REG-F-125's copied-measurement shape) and STALE CITATION. **Only the last is cosmetic. The rest change what a reader DOES.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — 21 files across `packages/rph-{application,domain,engine,projections}`, `verif/`, `scripts/mutants/`. **Safe default:** a drifted `file.ts:NN` citation is repaired by DROPPING the ordinal and citing the SYMBOL or a quoted row, never by re-pinning a number — a new number re-arms the same trap on the next insertion above it. And no audit output may be applied as a batch until its companions are promoted to first-class edits, its moves are made atomic, and its files are grouped by line ending.

### REG-F-127 — a second identical claim assessment appended a second ClaimSupported: the first of the fifteen unratified declarations to be driven, and it was a live defect
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** ENGINE DEFECT (append-only integrity) · **Status:** FIXED — narrow guard + 3 tests incl. the discriminating CONTROL + one mutant, measured.
- **DRIVEN BEFORE IT WAS DESIGNED, and only the drive found it.** `ROADMAP-the-fifteen-unratified.md` required each machine-admitted self-edge to be DRIVEN rather than argued. Through the real bus: `AssertClaim` → `RecordClaimAssessment(UNDER_ASSESSMENT)` → admit evidence → `RecordClaimAssessment(SUPPORTED)` → **a second, byte-identical `RecordClaimAssessment(SUPPORTED)` was ACCEPTED**, leaving `["ClaimAsserted","ClaimUnderAssessment","ClaimSupported","ClaimSupported"]`. **Reading the guard said "admissible"; only the drive said "and it appends a duplicate".** The second event records an assessment that did not happen — AX-7's permanent false entry in an append-only log, the same shape as governance's `REVOKED -> REVOKED` and RuntimeBinding's N-22 before it was guarded.
- **⚠ THE FIX IS THE NARROW ONE, ON A PRECEDENT THIS REPOSITORY ALREADY PAID FOR.** `runtime-binding.ts` records itself adopting the broad form — refuse every `from === to` — and WITHDRAWING it: *"the defect is 'NOTHING CHANGED', not 'THE STATUS STAYED THE SAME'."* A second assessment reaching the same conclusion **by a distinct assessment** is a real professional act (it is what DIFFERENT_AGENT independence looks like), and refusing every self-edge would strand exactly the act the assurance plane most wants. So the rule is: at the same status, the assessment must record something the last one did not.
- **⚠ THE REUSABLE HELPER WOULD HAVE INVERTED THE RULE WHILE LOOKING LIKE IT WORKED — the trap this entry most exists to record.** `noOpEditPrecondition` (DWP-08) compares payload fields against the OBJECT'S STATE. Measured: `recordClaimAssessment`'s `mutate` persists neither `assessmentId` nor `rationale` — **they ride the EVENT**. So comparing `assessmentId` against `state.assessmentId` compares against `undefined` ALWAYS, making the helper's "changed" test TRUE for every assessment that supplies one and FALSE only for those that do not. **The guard would have passed exactly the re-issues it must refuse and refused the ones it must admit** — a control that cannot fail, wearing a helper's clothes. Reaching for the existing helper because it is there was the obvious move and was wrong.
- **THE COMPARISON BASIS IS THE LAST EVENT OF THAT ARM, AND THE ARMS DIFFER.** `ClaimContested` carries `contradictingEvidenceIds` and NOT `assessmentId`/`rationale`; `ClaimSupported` and `ClaimUnderAssessment` carry `assessmentId`. **A field the emitted event does not carry cannot make a re-issue distinguishable to any later reader**, so supplying it changes nothing observable and must not count as change — which is the whole difference between comparing the EVENT and comparing the raw command payload. The per-arm table is TRANSCRIBED from the payload builder rather than derived, on REG-F-119's ground: a derived table would agree with the builder by construction and could never fail; hand-written it can be wrong, and each arm is driven separately so a wrong row surfaces as an admitted duplicate.
- **THE MUTANT IS THE POINT, BECAUSE THE MOTIVATING TESTS CANNOT TELL THE TWO RULES APART.** `F127-the-reassessment-rule-widens-to-every-self-edge` forces the narrow check off, restoring the withdrawn broad form. **Both duplicate-refusal tests stay GREEN under it** — a widened guard still refuses the identical re-issue — so the tests that motivated the fix cannot distinguish the narrow rule from the over-broad one. Only the CONTROL can. Measured before declaring: it reddens *"CONTROL — a DISTINCT re-assessment at the same status is still ACCEPTED"* **alone** (1 failed / 8 passed).
- **DISCLOSED RESIDUAL, CITED RATHER THAN RE-DECIDED.** A caller that mints a FRESH `assessmentId` on every re-issue passes this check, and the log then accumulates events distinguished only by an id the caller chose. That may be right (each IS a distinct assessment) or an unbounded-append hole — and it is the SAME question `AppendConversationEntries` reached and deferred as **JAN-CMDPRE residual R2**, awaiting a stable per-act id. Deferred on that precedent; not settled silently here.
- **WHAT THIS SETTLES IN THE FIFTEEN.** Three of the five machine-admitted self-edges (`Claim.status` SUPPORTED/CONTESTED/UNDER_ASSESSMENT) are DEFECTS, now refused. The other two are already ruled and remain legitimate holds — `ExecutionPlan ACTIVE -> ACTIVE` (JAN-CMDPRE DWP-05's declared HOLD) and `RuntimeBinding PARTIALLY -> PARTIALLY` (N-22's incremental grant). **So the same shape was a defect on one machine and correct behaviour on another**, which is precisely why the roadmap forbade a blanket rule and required a per-site drive.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts`, `claim-assessment.test.ts` (+3), one ledger entry. **Safe default:** the census's `from === to` criterion identifies pairs the MACHINE would admit; whether each is a hold or a duplicate-append defect is a per-site question answered by DRIVING it, and three of five have now gone each way.

### REG-F-129 — STA-6 clause (d) enforced BEFORE the command that makes its antecedent reachable; and my own guard scope was an inference this register had already ruled an error
- **Date:** 2026-08-13 · **Type:** GOVERNANCE RULE ENFORCED (a rule closed only by unreachability) · **Status:** LANDED — guard + 4 tests (3 of them controls) + one mutant, measured. `SupersedeIntent` itself is the NEXT increment and is deliberately not in this one.
- **THE ORDERING IS THE FINDING.** `RPH-INT-007` closes *"a superseded intent cannot authorize new PWUs"* as `NOT_A_COMMAND_REFUSAL` on one ground — SUPERSEDED is COMMAND-UNREACHABLE — and states its own trigger: *"if SUPERSEDED ever becomes reachable, this rule becomes a live UNENFORCED_DISCLOSED row on the same day."* Building `SupersedeIntent` first would have shipped six new arrows, a green gate, and a governance rule that had silently stopped being closed. **The guard therefore lands FIRST, against an antecedent nothing can yet produce** — which is why its test SEEDS the status rather than driving it, guarded by `getMachine` so a state the machine cannot represent cannot be rehearsed against.
- **⚠ MY OWN SCOPE WAS WRONG, AND IT REPEATED AN ERROR THIS REGISTER HAS ALREADY RATIFIED AS ONE.** The design said the guard should refuse *"SUPERSEDED (and WITHDRAWN)"*. STA-6 names **"a superseded intent"** and nothing else: the ratified Canonical Domain Model mentions WITHDRAWN exactly twice — the enum member and the §6.2 matrix row — and none of §6.3's seven invariants names it. My ground was `terminalStates: ['SUPERSEDED','WITHDRAWN']` — *the two terminal states should behave alike* — and **REG-F-083 records that `terminalStates` is WHOLLY A REPOSITORY SHAPE**: *"The ratified Canonical Domain Model contains the word 'terminal' ZERO times."* **So the inference reasons from a repository artifact as though it were canon — the exact mistake REG-F-083 exists to record, made again, in the same register, by the same author.** The corpus does not treat them alike either: Supersede has SIX in-arrows (*"any active"*), Withdraw only THREE (*"permitted only from these three early states"*).
- **WITHDRAWN IS THEREFORE PINNED AS A DELIBERATE NON-RULE.** A test asserts that a WITHDRAWN intent STILL authorizes a proposal — not as an endorsement, but so that changing it is a visible act with a stated justification rather than a quiet widening. If the sponsor rules that a withdrawn intent should not authorize work, that test is the artifact that must change, and that is its purpose.
- **⚠ THE TEMPTING REUSE IS A GATE FOUR TIMES TOO WIDE, and the motivating test cannot see it.** STA-6 has FOUR clauses, two about intent maturity, so the obvious move is to reach for the set the READINESS gate already uses — `INTENT_AT_LEAST_PROVISIONAL` = {PROVISIONAL, FORMALIZED, APPROVED, REVISED}. That would refuse RAW, and **proposing under a RAW intent is the repository's normal, deliberate pattern: measured, 56 of the 71 files that dispatch both `CaptureIntent` and `ProposePwu` never mature the intent in between.** Clause (a) governs READINESS; clause (d) governs CREATION; they take different sets. The mutant `F129-the-creation-gate-reuses-the-readiness-set` is exactly that reuse — **and the SUPERSEDED test stays GREEN under it**, because a widened gate still refuses SUPERSEDED. Only the controls distinguish them: measured before declaring, it reddens the RAW control AND the WITHDRAWN pin (2 failed / 2 passed).
- **THE SURFACE WAS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED, and the derivation is what made a one-site guard defensible.** An AST walk over 636 files found **27 aggregate-creation call sites repo-wide** (creation = `expectedRevision: undefined`, the only branch that reaches the adapter's INSERT), of which **exactly TWO carry a PWU objectType — `pwu.ts:317` and one test.** Decomposition does NOT create children (it creates a contract over children that must already exist); the engine seeds dispatch through the bus (`handle.dispatch`); `rph-authoring` scaffolds PWU **Types**, not instances. **So one guard covers every creation, and "there is no other creator" is measured rather than hoped.** Scope is every PWU, root and child: clause (d) carries no root qualifier (clause (a) does), and this same handler mints children via its `parentWorkUnitId` payload field.
- **THE OTHER THREE CLAUSES, since STA-6 is compound and reading it as one rule is how three quarters of it goes unnoticed:** (a) READINESS — **ENFORCED** at `pwuGuards.ts:150` via `markPwuReady`; (b) AUTHORITATIVELY SATISFIED without approved intent — **UNENFORCED, no code path to SATISFIED reads an Intent at all**; (c) an intent cannot be DELETED — **UNREACHABLE ANTECEDENT**: `StorageAdapter` declares exactly one write (`commit`) and no delete/purge exists at any layer; (d) this entry. **Clause (b) is now the outstanding half and is recorded here as owed.**
- **DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED HERE:** PWU-002 is existence-only and never asserts the referent's `objectType`, so an `intentId` naming a non-INTENT object carries `intentStatus: undefined` and passes this check. That gap predates the guard and is unchanged by it; closing it alters PWU-002's own rule and belongs in its own increment rather than being smuggled in beside a canon-grounded one.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwu.ts`, `sta6-superseded-intent.test.ts` (new), one ledger entry. **Safe default:** `RPH-INT-007` may NOT be re-dispositioned to ENFORCED until `SupersedeIntent` exists — until then the rule is enforced against an antecedent nothing can produce, which is a guard waiting correctly, not a discharged obligation.
