### REG-F-153 — three register entries were cited by the code and had never been written, and one was mine from the same day
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** DANGLING CITATIONS (a claim that says nothing at all) · **Status:** CLOSED — gated, and the three entries reconstructed above.
- **FOUND BY FOLLOWING A CITATION.** Resuming the arrow work, I went to read REG-F-128 — the entry that split over-claims from self-edges — and `grep` returned **nothing**. Nor REG-F-130, cited by two handlers and the conformance ledger. Nor **REG-F-139, whose commit I had written hours earlier**.
- **⚠ THIS IS A DIFFERENT CLASS FROM THE STALE PROSE THIS SESSION SPENT NINE ENTRIES ON, and that is why no GATE caught it — but ~~nothing caught it~~ THE CLASS WAS ALREADY KNOWN AND RECORDED, which this entry did not check before claiming novelty (corrected at REG-F-154).** A stale number says something FALSE and can be contradicted by deriving the truth. **A dangling citation says nothing at all** — the reader follows it, finds no entry, and cannot tell whether the finding was withdrawn, renumbered, or never recorded. Every instrument built this week compares a claim against the world; none checks that a REFERENCE resolves.
- **GATED, with the reach and the exclusions derived rather than assumed.** `verif/register-citations.test.ts` resolves every `REG-[DFQ]` id cited anywhere in `packages/`, `verif/`, `scripts/`, `apps/` against the headings of every canon document — **208 distinct ids cited, 206 resolving.** Predicted red measured first: exactly `REG-F-128` and `REG-F-130`.
- **⚠ AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE GATE REPORTED EIGHT FALSE POSITIVES, caught before it shipped.** It flagged `REG-E-022`…`REG-E-031` as dangling. They are not: the Ratify Sheet carries them as *"Part 3 — Elicitation questions (REG-E-001..022)"* — a numbered **LIST**, which a heading resolver structurally cannot see. **Scoped to `REG-[DFQ]` with the reason recorded in the code**, because "my resolver cannot see that shape" and "those entries do not exist" are the same output and opposite facts. Two further exclusions are pinned by name: `REG-F-998/999`, which `register-status.test.ts` FABRICATES in its own controls, and the gate's own file, which names the dangling ids in its docblock.
- **THE THREE ENTRIES ARE RECONSTRUCTED, NOT INVENTED**, each labelled as such and built only from artifacts that cite them — a mutant's `why`, a handler's docblock, a surviving entry's account. **REG-F-130's content survives almost intact inside REG-F-132**, which quotes it at length; that is why the register could lose an entry and keep functioning, and also why nobody noticed.
- **⚠ WHAT THE GATE STILL CANNOT SEE, stated so it is not mistaken for coverage:** citations that appear ONLY in markdown or in commit messages. REG-F-139 was invisible to it for exactly that reason — it was cited in prose and in a commit title, never in code. **It was found by hand, and a repeat would be too.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `verif/register-citations.test.ts` (new), and four entries appended here. **Safe default:** an id is a promise that a record exists; before citing one, check that it does — and when a commit is titled after an entry, make sure the commit writes it.

### REG-F-154 — the register had already recorded the rule I broke, and REG-F-153 claimed the class was new without checking
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** SEARCH-THE-REGISTER-FIRST, failed by its own maintainer · **Status:** CLOSED — the gate extended to markdown, the novelty claim corrected.
- **⚠ THE REGISTER ALREADY CONTAINED BOTH THE FINDING AND THE RULE.** Extending the citation gate to markdown surfaced one unresolved id — `REG-F-115` — and following it landed on an entry written by an earlier pass that says, verbatim: *"`REG-F-115` is allocated in commit `689ac61b`'s subject line and has **no entry in this register**"*, closing with the safe default **"an id allocated in a commit message is not an entry."**
- **SO THE SEQUENCE IS: THE RULE WAS RECORDED · I BROKE IT · I FOUND THE BREAKAGE · AND I REPORTED THE CLASS AS NEW.** REG-F-139 was a commit titled after an entry it never wrote — precisely the thing that safe default forbids. REG-F-153 then said *"nothing caught it"*. **No GATE caught it, which is true and is why the gate was built. The CLASS was known**, and one `grep REG-F-115` before writing the entry would have found it. That is the sixth time this session the register already held the answer, and this register's own standing lesson is to search it first.
- **WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW, stated at its true size:** not the class, but that it is now MECHANICALLY CHECKED. The earlier pass found its instance by hand, while choosing an id, and recorded a safe default that depended on the next author reading it. **A safe default enforced by memory is the thing this repository has spent a week discovering does not hold.**
- **THE GATE NOW SEES MARKDOWN, closing the residual REG-F-153 disclosed rather than fixed.** Measured before extending: **248 ids cited across `docs/`, 246 resolving** — high signal, not a wall of noise. `REG-F-139` was invisible to the first version for exactly this reason, and the extension is what makes that escape route closed rather than merely documented.

The exemption carries its reason in the code, and **a companion assertion fails if the entry is ever written**, so the exemption cannot outlive the gap it apologises for. **A wildcard was refused deliberately**: it would absorb the next real gap silently, which is the failure this file exists to catch.
- **AND THE MUTATION GATE ABORTED IN MY HAND WHILE THIS WAS BEING WRITTEN, WHICH IS THE CONTROL WORKING.** I edited a source file while a full run was in flight; it returned `ABORTED_DIRTY` at `MU-FRESH-18-A-neutralise-revision-check` and refused to measure. **No mutant was left behind** — `treeIsClean()` is checked BEFORE the mutation is applied, so `kit.ts` was never touched, verified by `git status`. The runner's own comment warns against exactly this, and I did it anyway; the harness declined to produce the "full, plausible, entirely worthless verdict table" it was built to refuse.

### REG-F-155 — "census-blind" is at least two different facts, and nine of the eleven blind machines ARE named by a production handler
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** SCOPING MEASUREMENT (a bound re-derived before anything is built on it) · **Status:** OPEN — measured and scoped, deliberately NOT fixed. **This raises a doubt about REG-F-150's residue rather than settling it.**
- **WHY THIS WAS MEASURED AT ALL.** REG-F-150 closed the unreachability residual but found that **9 of 21 rows pass by construction**, because the census cannot see the machines they rest on. That entry treated "census-blind" as a single bound inherited from C-0. **It is not one thing, and the difference decides whether those nine rows are safe or false.**
- **MEASURED: 11 blind machines, and NINE of them are NAMED, in code, by a production handler** — `AssuranceObservation.disposition`, `Constraint.status`, `Harness.status`, `Obligation.status`, `PWU.assuranceState`, `PWU.executionState`, `PWU.shapeIntegrityState`, `PwuType.status`, `Undertaking.status`. Only two are not: `AggregateAssuranceDisposition` (**0 states — the computed reduction REG-F-035 established is not a machine at all**, correctly excluded) and `AssuranceAssessment.disposition`.
- **⚠ AND THE REFERENCES ARE CODE, NOT COMMENTS — CHECKED, BECAUSE A GREP CANNOT TELL THEM APART AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** Two were read directly and they have **DIFFERENT causes**:
  - `handlers/pwu.ts:1343` — `['PWU.executionState', current.executionState, p.executionState],` — **a real driver, expressed as a TUPLE the census's four idioms do not read.** Blindness here is an INSTRUMENT GAP.
  - `handlers/harness.ts:39` — `births: [{ machine: 'Harness.status', statusField: 'status', values: ['FRAMING'] }]` — **a BIRTH declaration, not an arrow.** The census handles births separately, so arrow-blindness here may be entirely correct.
- **SO THE SINGLE WORD "BLIND" COVERS AT LEAST: (a) an arrow driven through an unreadable idiom, (b) a machine that is only ever BORN and never advanced, and (c) a thing that is not a machine.** Any statement of the form *"the census sees nothing, therefore nothing drives it"* is unsound across that set, and REG-F-150's nine vacuous rows rest on exactly three of these machines — `Obligation.status`, `Constraint.status`, `AssuranceObservation.disposition` — **all three NAMED by handlers.**
- **⚠ WHAT THIS PUTS AT RISK, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN DEFERRED.** If any of those three is driven through an unreadable idiom, then the `ARROW_UNREACHABLE` rows resting on it are **not merely unmeasurable — they may be FALSE**, in the same way RPH-EVD-002 was. REG-F-150 pinned the vacuity honestly; **this entry records that the vacuity might be concealing the very class the whole gate was built to catch.** That is a doubt, not a finding: none of the three has been read.
- **NOT FIXED, AND THE COST IS THE REASON.** Teaching the census the tuple idiom is not a local change — it would move `declarationRows`, `machinesSeen`, `ratifiedArrowsCovered` (162/304), the arm-3 vacuity pin (21/9), the C-0c blind/unanalysed relationship, and every prose figure this session has just spent four entries correcting. **It is its own increment with its own predicted reds**, and starting it inside a scoping measurement is how a measured bound becomes an unmeasured rewrite.
- **Merge target:** none — this entry is the deliverable. **Safe default:** before resting an argument on "the instrument sees nothing there", establish WHY it sees nothing; absence of a reading and absence of a thing are the same output from opposite worlds, and this repository has now confused them at least twice.

### REG-F-156 — the doubt is resolved: all nine rows are SAFE, established by a write-funnel derivation that does NOT depend on the census
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** DOUBT DISCHARGED (REG-F-155's, by a method that answers it) · **Status:** CLOSED for these three machines. Two rows rest on thinner ground and are named.
- **THE DOUBT, RESTATED.** REG-F-150 found nine `ARROW_UNREACHABLE` rows passing BY CONSTRUCTION — the census cannot see their machines, so `covered = 0` regardless of truth. REG-F-155 then found all three of those machines NAMED in handler code, raising that the rows might be **false**, as RPH-EVD-002 was.
- **RESOLVED: all three are BIRTH-ONLY, and the nine rows are SAFE.** `Obligation.status` and `Constraint.status` are born at `PROPOSED` (`obligation-constraint.ts:39`, `:78`); `AssuranceObservation.disposition` at `OPEN` (`assurance.ts:2328`). **Nothing advances any of them.**
- **⚠ AND THE METHOD IS THE POINT, because my own first derivation could not have settled it.** I searched for literal state writes (`status: 'ALLOCATED'` etc.) and for references to each machine name. **That search is idiom-dependent and would have missed exactly what REG-F-155 had just found** — `pwu.ts:1343`'s tuple form writes a state through variables, with no literal to grep. The sound derivation runs down the WRITE FUNNEL instead: `StorageAdapter.commit` (`rph-ports/src/ports/storage.ts:75`) has **exactly one production caller repo-wide** — `kit.ts:529`, verified — and every commit names an `objectType`. **So any write to these aggregates must carry their objectType literal at a commit site. Exactly three exist, all creations.**
- **⚠ WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT THE METHOD SEES WHAT THE CENSUS CANNOT.** The `pwu.ts:1342` tuple is invisible to C-0's four idioms — but **not** to this method, because `changePwuState` commits `objectType: PWU`. A hidden-idiom advance on any machine under audit would have surfaced as a fourth `objectType: OBLIGATION|CONSTRAINT|OBSERVATION` commit. There is none. **A negative result is worth only as much as the demonstration that the method could have produced a positive one.**
- **⚠ TWO OF THE NINE ARE SAFE ON THINNER GROUND, AND SAYING SO IS THE USEFUL PART.** The seven Obligation/Constraint rows are safe **twice over**: `PROPOSED -> ACTIVE` has no writer either, so `ACTIVE` and `ALLOCATED` are never occupied — the arrows are unreachable AND their sources unoccupiable. **The two `AssuranceObservation` rows are safe only once**: `OPEN` IS occupied, by the birth, so they rest entirely on *"nothing writes `disposition` a second time"*. **That is the limb that breaks first if an observation command is ever authored**, and it is now named rather than left inside an undifferentiated nine.
- **CENSUS-BLINDNESS HERE IS CORRECT, NOT AN INSTRUMENT GAP — and that does not vindicate the census.** It would have reported `covered = 0` either way; its agreement is not evidence. **What makes the rows true is the write-surface derivation.** REG-F-155's finding is unaffected: `PWU.executionState` remains a real driver in an unreadable idiom, and the other blind machines are still unread.
- **STALE EVIDENCE CORRECTED INSIDE A ROW WHOSE DISPOSITION IS UNCHANGED.** Row `:291` asserted that `assertObligation` *"declares NO `births`"* and that a grep *"returns ZERO hits"*. **Both are now false** — `obligation-constraint.ts:39` is that declaration and that hit. Struck in place; **the limb that carries the disposition (no `advanceStatus` names the machine) still holds**, which is why the row does not move. - **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** INSTRUMENT GAP DIAGNOSED + its remedy measured and DEFERRED · **Status:** OPEN. **Nothing built** — this entry exists so the increment starts from the truth.

  - **UNDECLARED:** `PWU.executionState`, `PWU.assuranceState`, `PWU.shapeIntegrityState`, driven through `subAxisChecks` — `Array<[string, string, string]>` of `[machine, current.X, p.X]`, fed to `checkTransition`. **All three are census-blind, and all three are driven by the same command that declares the fourth.**

The site does not name arrows; it asserts that whatever arrow the caller supplied is legal. **So the honest reading is not "these three arrows" but "any legal arrow of these three machines, minus what is refused."**
- **THE SCOPE, MEASURED: 42 ratified arrows** — `executionState` 20, `assuranceState` 13, `shapeIntegrityState` 9. Coverage today is **162 of 304 (53.3%)**; the upper bound if all were declared is **204 of 304 (67.1%)**. **That is the largest single coverage movement available anywhere in this programme**, which is precisely why it must not be taken carelessly.

The refused set for the three sub-axes is EMPTY.** The setter does NOT reach every legal arrow: the handler's own comment records that the ownership table *"refuses both arrows outright"* for abandonment and rejection, and `rejectUnbackedDisposition` / `rejectUnauthorizedWaiver` refuse further assuranceState moves. **Declaring all 42 would add up to 42 arrows the command cannot actually perform — REG-F-128's `overClaimed` category, whose current population is TEN, all on `Claim.status`.** A four-fold increase in over-claims, bought with a fourteen-point coverage rise, is the worst possible trade this register could record: **the number that looks like progress and the number that measures dishonesty moving together.**

- **PINS IT WILL MOVE, listed because four entries this session were spent correcting numbers exactly like these:** `declarationRows` (180), `machinesSeen` (16), `ratifiedArrowsCovered` (162/304 and its 53.3%), the `142` uncovered, C-0c's `censusBlind` (11) and its relationship to `unanalysed` (17, overlap 6), the arm-3 vacuity pin `{21, 9}` — **which REG-F-156 has just shown would go to `{21, 9}` unchanged, since those nine rows rest on machines this change does not touch** — and every prose figure quoting them.

### REG-F-161 — the register already recorded the conclusion and named the wrong cause for it; RPH-BAS-003's waiver escape is dead for a reason repairing the cited one would not touch
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** DEAD-BRANCH CENSUS (2 branches) + a MISATTRIBUTION corrected in the enforcement register · **Status:** CLOSED as a finding; **nothing repaired, deliberately** — both branches fail CLOSED, and the fix is a command that does not exist.

- **THE CITED CAUSE:** *"the waiver arm is starved of its argument (see the neighbour note below)"*. The neighbour note is about **`requiredWaivers`**, which feeds `findExpiredWaivers` and **RPH-GOV-006's `EXPIRED_REQUIRED_WAIVER`** — a separate finding code, and genuinely starved: the argument is not passed at all.
- **THE ACTUAL CAUSE FOR THIS ROW, and it is not starvation:** RPH-BAS-003's waiver arm is `!o.waived` inside `findOpenBlockingObservations`, fed by `openObservations`, **which IS passed.** It is dead because `observationsAgainstBaselineItems` computes `waived: disposition === 'WAIVED'` and **`AssuranceObservation.disposition` has exactly ONE write in the whole repository** — the birth at `assurance.ts:2324`, value `OPEN`. So `!o.waived` is always true and the guard reduces to `if (o.blocking)`.
- **⚠ TWO INDEPENDENT CAUSES, AND THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT: a reader who supplied `requiredWaivers` — the repair the note directs them to — would find this escape still dead.** The conclusion was right, the mechanism was borrowed from the rule next door, and a correct conclusion resting on a misattributed mechanism is the same class REG-F-157 committed and REG-F-158 corrected. It is now the third instance this week, which is why the general form is stated below rather than the instance.
- **MY OWN FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS ALSO WRONG, AND CHECKING IT IS WHAT PRODUCED THE ANSWER.** I expected a nearer local cause: a `UNSETTLED_DISPOSITIONS` filter three lines above the branch. **It DOES contain `WAIVED`** — the value is admitted and then can never occur — so the local-filter reading is refuted and the birth-only derivation is load-bearing after all. REG-F-156's attribution survived a check aimed at replacing it.
- **THE SECOND BRANCH, SAME ROOT, OPPOSITE END OF THE SYSTEM.** `floor-gate.ts:259` — `if (s.disposition && s.disposition !== 'OPEN') continue; // already resolved/waived elsewhere`. `OPEN` is the only value ever written, so the `continue` never fires and the filter excludes nothing: a waiver must name EVERY finding code the assessment raised, including any notionally resolved.
- **BOTH FAIL CLOSED, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING IS BEING HOTFIXED.** The baseline gate REFUSES a waived blocking finding rather than excusing it; the floor gate demands MORE of a waiver rather than less. **Stricter than canon intends, never laxer** — dead branches, not holes. Recording that plainly is the difference between a census and an alarm.
- **⚠ AND A KERNEL TEST ASSERTS A CASE THE PRODUCTION PRODUCER CANNOT ELICIT.** `governance.test.ts:242` — *"an open unwaived blocking finding blocks promotion; a waived one does not"* — passes `waived: true` **straight into `canPromoteBaseline`, bypassing `observationsAgainstBaselineItems`.** The kernel branch is therefore genuinely tested and the path that would reach it cannot exist. A green test over a synthetic input is not evidence that the input occurs.
- **MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED, BOTH TIMES.** `waived: disposition === 'WAIVED'` -> `waived: false`: `rph-application` + `rph-domain` = **132 files / 1464 tests, all passing.** Deleting the floor-gate filter line: plus `rph-assurance` = **137 files / 1511 tests, all passing.** Both are now ledger entries carrying `expectSurvive`, so **survival is recorded as the finding and a KILL becomes the signal** that an observation-disposition command was authored — at which point both retire together and RPH-BAS-003's C-0b row is re-driven.
- **THE WRITE FUNNEL, RE-VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED**, because the whole entry rests on it: `objectType: OBSERVATION` occurs at exactly ONE commit site. A `disposition: 'ESCALATED'` at `assurance.ts:2144` is a **near miss checked and dismissed** — it is an event-payload field on an `ASSESSMENT` (`AssuranceAssessmentEscalated`), a different aggregate, and writes no observation state.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `enforcement-register.ts` (the note, struck in place), two ledger CONTROLS. **Safe default:** **a register note that states a conclusion must cite the mechanism OF ITS OWN ROW** — when two rules sit adjacent and share an outcome, the nearer explanation is the one most likely to be borrowed, and a borrowed mechanism sends the next reader to repair something that will not move the thing they are reading about.

- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** MY OWN PROPOSAL REFUTED + a real defect found underneath it + instrumentation built · **Status:** CLOSED for the defect and the instrumentation. **No speedup shipped** — the number it would optimise does not exist yet.
- **THE SPONSOR RAISED THE COST** (*"these mutation gate tests take close to 40 minutes"*) and proposed batching increments between runs. I proposed something cleverer: a two-tier gate whose fast tier runs only the mutants a commit could have affected, derived as `{m : m.file ∈ git diff} ∪ {m : m.expectRed ∩ git diff ≠ ∅}`.
- **⚠ AS WRITTEN IT SELECTS ZERO OF 220 MUTANTS AND EXITS GREEN FOREVER.** `git diff --name-only` emits paths relative to the git TOPLEVEL, which is `E:/Projects/hestami-worktree-arrows`, so every path carries the prefix `JanumiCode/janumiprofessionalworkbench/`. **No ledger path carries that prefix** — all 220 `file` values and all 70 distinct `expectRed` values are project-relative. **The intersection is empty for every commit that will ever be made**, so the fast tier would run nothing, find nothing, and print a pass. A gate that measures nothing while reporting success is this repository's oldest and most-recorded defect, and I proposed it in the same session in which I corrected three instances of it.
- **AND FIXING THE PREFIX WOULD NOT SAVE IT.** Eight further holes were derived, every one of which FAILS OPEN — a missed mutant reports nothing, and silence reads as a pass:
  - **RENAME.** `git diff --name-only` reports only the DESTINATION of a rename, so renaming a victim hides every mutant naming it. `--no-renames` is the fix.
  - **SHARED INPUTS.** `vitest.projects.ts` and its two global `setupFiles`, the tsconfig `extends` chain, `verif/guard-enforcement-ledger.data.ts` (imported by the victim of 2 mutants), `verif/arrow-command-census.baseline.json` (read BY PATH by the victim of 5), and `scripts/mutants/run.ts` itself appear in **neither** set. A commit rewiring any of them selects zero mutants while changing every verdict.
  - **THE LEDGER.** `scripts/mutants/ledger.ts` is not any mutant's `file`, so adding, re-anchoring or retargeting an entry selects **nothing** — the term that lets the ledger rot under a green fast tier.
  - **CONTROLS.** A control declares `expectRed: []`, runs the WHOLE workspace and is graded against a fresh baseline, so **its verdict depends on every file in the repository by construction**. It can only ever be in the affected set unconditionally — which puts 8 whole-suite runs plus a baseline into every commit and may cost more than it saves.
  - Plus cross-package victims (by design, `run.ts:279-285`), e2e victims whose verdict depends on a browser round-trip no static closure can model, staged/untracked files that bare `git diff` cannot see, and merge commits whose combined diff is empty.
- **THE HONEST DISPOSITION, AND IT IS NOT "FIX THE TERMS":** a derived-subset run is a **TRIAGE tool that must not be able to license a merge**, not a gate. If it is ever built it must print `N of 220 selected` under a heading that is NOT the summary banner — the precedent is already in the code, where PREFLIGHT and HARVEST refuse that banner for exactly this reason.
- **⚠⚠ AND UNDERNEATH ALL OF IT: NOBODY HAS EVER MEASURED WHERE THE FORTY MINUTES GOES.** `scripts/mutants/run.ts` contains **no timing instrumentation at all** (979 lines, verified). The two figures in circulation are **undated prose that disagree with each other** — *"~40-minute run"* at `run.ts:57` and *"~30-minute run"* at `mutant-ledger.test.ts:116` — and both were written when the ledger held roughly HALF its current 220 entries. **Every speedup anyone proposed, mine included, was arithmetic over a guessed constant.** That is the defect this register spent four entries on last week, committed against my own instrument.
- **WHAT THE RUN ACTUALLY DOES, measured from the source rather than from those numbers:** 220 entries → 15 short-circuit at zero cost (10 `duplicateOf`, 5 `supersededBy`) → 205 reach apply + **one cold `tsc --noEmit -p <pkg>`** → 3 stop there (`expectNoCompile`) → 202 reach a test run, being **178 targeted vitest**, **16 Playwright** (each forcing a COLD Vite boot: `reuseExistingServer: false`, `retries: 1`), and **8 whole-workspace runs** plus **1 baseline** (~271 test files, ~2,189 cases each). Compilation is non-incremental **by explicit configuration** — `"incremental": false` at `packages/typescript-config/base.json:9`, no `composite`, no project references.
- **PARALLELISM IS A WEAKENING ON THIS MACHINE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT I EXPECTED.** Six physical cores; **no `testTimeout` override anywhere**, so vitest's 5000 ms default applies; and `EXCLUDED_PROJECTS = ['csaa']` exists *because a suite already times out under whole-suite load*. **This harness converts CPU contention into BLOCKING `INCONCLUSIVE` verdicts by design** (REG-F-116/136). Adding workers manufactures false verdicts. Worktree isolation also has a hard blocker: `node_modules/@janumipwb/*` are ABSOLUTE symlinks, so each worktree needs a real `bun install` and a from-source rebuild of `better-sqlite3`.
- **AND BATCHING MUTANTS INTO ONE PATCH SET IS UNSOUND**, on this codebase's own central fact: `run.ts:279-285` records that **domain predicates are enforced at the command layer**, so mutants in different files are exactly NOT independent with respect to the tests that kill them.
- **THE ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND, AND IT IS A CORRECTNESS BUG IN THE GATE AS IT STANDS TODAY: NOTHING CHECKED THAT A NAMED VICTIM EXISTS.** `run.ts` invokes `bunx vitest run <victim>` and reads ONE bit, the exit status; every project sets `passWithNoTests: false`, so **vitest exits non-zero when the path matches nothing and the runner scores the entry KILLED** — recording the guard as proven by a suite that is not there. The anchor census has caught the mirror case (the mutated FILE moving) since REG-F-100; the VICTIM moving was never checked, and a rename is the worst shape of it because a review sees only the destination path.
- **GATED, WITH ITS PREDICTED RED MEASURED.** `verif/mutant-ledger.test.ts` now checks all 220 victims on every `bun run test` in milliseconds — **where the evidence is cheap, rather than ~40 minutes in where the failure happens and is then mis-reported.** Driven by rotting one real entry's `expectRed`: **exactly 1 test reddened**, naming `F117-the-census-stops-reading-advanceIntent` and the missing path, while the CONTROL held.
- **WHAT IS NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: no speedup.** `printTimings` is now in the runner — a `timed()` wrapper that **returns its callback's value untouched and is read by no arm that decides anything**, because a timing hook that can change what it measures is the observer defect recorded against three other instruments here. ~~**The next run produces the first real per-leg numbers**~~ — **IT DID NOT, AND THE CLAIM WAS FALSE WHEN WRITTEN: see REG-F-163.** The call was UNREACHABLE and the instrumented run printed no table at all. The two prose durations stay wrong until a run actually reports, **and are corrected with a MEASURED and DATED figure or not at all.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `verif/mutant-ledger.test.ts` (the victim census + its control), `scripts/mutants/run.ts` (instrumentation only). **Safe default:** **an optimisation whose baseline is a number in a comment is not an optimisation, it is a guess with a ratio attached** — instrument first, and when the instrument is the thing being sped up, prove the instrument still measures before believing it is faster.

### REG-F-163 — the instrument I added to measure the gate never ran, and I asserted its output in the same commit
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** SELF-INFLICTED HOLLOW, caught one commit later by looking for an output that was not there · **Status:** CLOSED — reachable, and verified by driving it rather than by reading it.
- **REG-F-162 ADDED `printTimings()` TO `scripts/mutants/run.ts` AS THE LAST STATEMENT OF THE MODULE.** Every path out of that runner ends in `process.exit(...)` — **there are six** — so the call was **unreachable code**. The first instrumented run completed all 205 mutations, printed the summary, exited 0, and **printed no timing table at all**.
- **⚠ AND THE COMMIT MESSAGE ASSERTED THE OUTPUT: *"The next run produces the first real per-leg numbers."* It did not.** The entry said the same and is struck above. **I wrote an instrument, claimed what it would report, and never checked that it could report anything** — inside the very commit whose entry is about instruments that measure nothing while reporting success. The defect and its own description shipped together.
- **NOTHING COULD HAVE TOLD ME EXCEPT LOOKING.** `bunx tsc --noEmit -p scripts/tsconfig.json` passes — unreachable code after `process.exit` is not a type error. `eslint .` passes. The mutation gate passed, 193 KILLED / SURVIVED 0 / INCONCLUSIVE 0. **A `console.log` that never happens has no failure mode**: there is no exit code, no assertion, and no verdict anywhere that changes. The only detector is a reader expecting a specific output and noticing its absence.
- **⚠ THE PRECISE FAILURE IS NOT "I FORGOT TO TEST IT" — I RAN THE CHECK, IT WAS BLOCKED, AND I TREATED IT AS DONE.** I invoked `bun run mutants F159-birth-drift` specifically to smoke-test the instrumentation. It returned `ABORT: working tree is not clean — refusing to mutate over uncommitted changes.` **That is the runner's dirty-tree guard doing its job, and it is not a pass.** I read a refusal-to-run as a run, committed, and asserted the result. **A blocked check is a check that did not happen**, and it is more dangerous than one never attempted, because attempting it feels like diligence.
- **THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS A REGISTRATION RATHER THAN SIX CALLS.** `process.on('exit', printTimings)` fires on every path including `process.exit`, so the `ABORTED_DIRTY` and preflight exits now report their legs too — which is exactly what a reader wants from a run that stopped early, and it is the arm that would otherwise silently lose the most interesting measurement. **The handler must stay synchronous**; an async one would silently not run, which is this same defect wearing a different hat, so the constraint is written at the call site.
- **THE GENERAL FORM, and it is a sibling of a rule this repository already runs on.** The standing rule is *"name the test that MUST redden before trusting green."* Its analogue for instrumentation: **name the OUTPUT you expect to see, and do not believe an instrument ran until you have seen it.** A guard has a verdict that can be wrong; a *report* has only presence and absence, so absence is the only signal and nothing raises it for you.
- **⚠ NOT YET VERIFIED, AND THIS BULLET IS WHERE I ALMOST DID IT AGAIN.** The draft of this entry read *"a single-mutant run was executed after the fix and the table printed"* — **written before any such run.** That is the same false-assertion-of-an-output this entry exists to record, drafted inside the entry recording it. **The table has NOT been seen at the time of this commit.** Verification is the next command: a single-mutant run, whose output must contain `WHERE THE TIME WENT`, then the full run. Until that is done this fix is a plausible edit, not an installed instrument — which is precisely the distinction the safe default draws.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/run.ts`. **Safe default:** **an instrument is not installed until you have seen its output** — and if a smoke test refuses to run, the correct next action is to make it runnable, never to proceed as though it had passed.

### REG-F-164 — the gate's cost, MEASURED for the first time: no leg dominates, and both numbers everyone had been optimising against were wrong
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** FIRST MEASUREMENT + two stale prose durations retired + a gap in my own instrument closed · **Status:** CLOSED for the measurement. **Still no speedup shipped** — the evidence does not support the one everybody assumed.
- **THE FIRST REAL PER-LEG BREAKDOWN**, from `printTimings` at `e070c462`, over 205 distinct mutations:

  | leg | time | calls | avg | share |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | **tsc (all nine projects)** | **708.6s** | 205 | 3.5s | **31.8%** |
  | vitest targeted | 539.4s | 178 | 3.0s | 24.2% |
  | vitest whole-suite (controls) | 504.3s | 8 | 63.0s | 22.6% |
  | Playwright | 479.7s | 16 | 30.0s | 21.5% |
  | **TOTAL (subprocess only)** | **2232.0s = 37.2 min** | | | |

- **⚠ NOTHING DOMINATES, WHICH REFUTES EVERY PREDICTION MADE ABOUT THIS RUN INCLUDING BOTH OF MINE.** I expected compilation to be the cost and proposed incremental `tsc` on that basis; the investigating agent expected whole-suite runs might be ~70% and said its ranking would invert if so. **The four legs are 32 / 24 / 23 / 22 per cent.** There is no single change that makes this fast, and the reason is structural rather than accidental: 205 cold typechecks, 178 cold vitest boots, 16 cold Vite dev-server boots and 8 whole-workspace runs are four independent constant costs, not one hot loop.
- **WHAT THIS DOES TO EACH PROPOSED SPEEDUP, now that the denominator is real:**
  - **Incremental `tsc`** — the largest single lever at 31.8%, and still worth building. Even a perfect result removes at most ~11 minutes of 37, **and its saving is unmeasured under the mutate/revert cycle**: my earlier 5.60s→1.86s figure was two consecutive runs over an UNCHANGED tree, which is not what the gate does. It must be re-measured against the real pattern before it is believed.
  - **Playwright's cold boots** — 479.7s, entirely because `reuseExistingServer: false` forces a fresh Vite boot per invocation. Sharing one server across the 16 would recover most of it **and is REFUSED**: each mutant edits source the dev server must re-read, so a shared server makes every e2e verdict depend on HMR picking the change up. **A stale module produces a SURVIVED that means nothing** — buying six minutes with the one failure mode this ledger exists to detect.
  - **Batching the 8 controls into one whole-suite run** — worth 441s on paper, and **blocked by a rule already in force**: the anchor census exempts exactly ONE applied mutant id (REG-F-110's *"THE EXEMPTION IS ONE ID, NOT 'SKIP UNDER THE RUNNER'"*), so eight simultaneous mutations make seven of them report UNANCHORED. Widening that exemption to a set is a real weakening of a real guard, argued for performance. Refused.
  - **Narrowing the 178 targeted runs with `--project`** — each still instantiates all 13 projects; worth perhaps 3 minutes, and it is the "narrow what runs, then read the exit code as a statement about the mutation" shape this register has recorded four times. Not taken for three minutes.
- **SO THE SPONSOR'S OWN PROPOSAL REMAINS THE BEST ONE AVAILABLE: batch the increments and run the gate less often.** It costs no guarantee at all — every mutant still runs, over the same population, with the same verdicts — where all four engineering alternatives cost either a guarantee or a rule. **The measurement's most useful output is that it argues against the clever options rather than for one.**
- **BOTH CIRCULATING DURATIONS ARE NOW RETIRED, AND ONE OF THEM WAS RIGHT BY ACCIDENT.** `run.ts:57` said *"~40-minute run"* — close, and undated. `mutant-ledger.test.ts:116` said *"~30-minute run"* — **wrong by seven minutes**, and its section heading carried a THIRD copy (*"CHECKED IN SECONDS RATHER THAN IN THIRTY MINUTES"*) which nothing connected to the other two. All three now carry **37.2 minutes, dated, with the commit they were measured at**. The rule this repository already runs on applies unchanged: *a count in prose beside a value nothing derives is a count nothing checks* — and here there were three of them, disagreeing, all load-bearing for a design decision.
- **⚠ AND MY OWN INSTRUMENT UNDER-REPORTED ITS SUBJECT, which is the smaller sibling of REG-F-163.** `takeBaseline` runs a full unmutated whole-suite pass — about 63 seconds, the same cost as a control — and I did not wrap it, so **the 2232.0s TOTAL above excludes it**. Found by asking why 9 controls produced only 8 whole-suite rows. Now timed as `vitest BASELINE`; the true figure is nearer 2295s. **An instrument that omits one of its own legs reports a total that is confidently low**, and nothing about the table said so.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/run.ts` (baseline leg + the dated figure), `verif/mutant-ledger.test.ts` (two copies of the stale duration). **Safe default:** **measure before optimising, and publish the breakdown rather than the total** — a single number invites the assumption that something in it dominates, and here the honest finding is that nothing does, which is precisely the finding that stops four people building four clever things.

### REG-F-165 — the layer that decides what every other verdict MEANS was the one layer with no test on it, and a fail-open sat in it
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** FAIL-OPEN FIXED + the verdict layer made testable + two blind spots measured and DEFERRED · **Status:** CLOSED for the fail-open. **Two verified findings deliberately NOT fixed** and named below, and **one audit dimension went uncovered** — said plainly so this does not read as a clean bill.
- **`scripts/mutants/run.ts` HAS ZERO EXPORTS AND EXECUTES ON IMPORT.** It is a script, not a module, so `controlVerdict`, `compileVerdict` and `pkgOf` were unreachable by any suite — **and the mutation ledger cannot mutate what nothing observes.** The layer deciding what KILLED, SURVIVED and CONTROL_HELD *mean* was the only layer with no test on it, and it stayed that way because a script's decision logic is untestable **by default rather than by decision**.
- **THE DEFECT THAT PROVED IT — A NON-MEASUREMENT GRADED AS A PASS.** `controlVerdict` took a run that **exited non-zero** and whose report named **no failing test file**, and returned `CONTROL_HELD`. A setup or teardown throw, an unhandled rejection, a worker crash, a config error: the failure is real, nothing attributes it, and the one conclusion unavailable is that the control held.
- **⚠ AND IT SAT ONE LINE BELOW THE ARM WRITTEN TO REFUSE EXACTLY THAT.** `failedFiles` had been carefully taught to return `undefined` rather than `[]` for a MISSING report, with its own comment recording that conflating them would be *"a fail-OPEN hole in the fix for a fail-open hole"* and that it was *"caught by reading my own diff rather than by the gate"*. **The present-but-empty report is the THIRD case in a two-case distinction**, and it took the hold path. The earlier fix was right and its author — me — did not ask whether the dichotomy was complete.
- **FIXED BY MOVING THE DECISION SOMEWHERE IT CAN BE TESTED, not by patching in place.** `scripts/mutants/verdict.ts` now holds `gradeControl` as a PURE function — no filesystem, no process, no clock, inputs exactly what the runner observed — and `run.ts` keeps only the I/O. `verif/control-verdict.test.ts` is the first test the verdict layer has ever had. **Predicted red measured:** neutering the new arm reddens **exactly 1 of 7**, the case written for it, while the other six hold.
- **A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FUNCTION, and it is `measured.ts`'s own rule broken inside the arm that reports it.** The SURVIVED detail read *"the prose-only edit NEWLY reddened N suite(s) — something asserts on prose"*. **Only ONE of the nine controls edits prose.** The other eight mutate live code or checked data — `waived: disposition === 'WAIVED'` → `waived: false`, a deleted `continue`, a deleted `engine.recoverOutbox()` call, rewritten string literals a checker reads. So for eight of nine the runner would **state a cause it never measured**, which is verbatim the defect `measured.ts` exists to end (*"The runner had stated a CAUSE it never measured"*). The detail now names the evidence and asserts nothing.
- **TWO FINDINGS VERIFIED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — they are separate increments, and filing them is not fixing them:**
  - **THE COMPILE LEG IS BLIND TO SIX MUTANTS.** `bunx tsc --noEmit -p apps/rph-demo/tsconfig.json --listFiles` loads **1640 files and ZERO `.svelte`** (measured directly). Six ledger entries target `.svelte` files — derived from the ledger, not counted by hand. So `compileVerdict` typechecks a program **that never contains the mutated file**: it spends a full app typecheck that cannot observe the mutation, `NO_COMPILE` is structurally unreachable for those six, and a `KILLED` on them cannot exclude *"the page failed to build"*. **Root cause in one line:** `compileVerdict` hardcodes raw `tsc` while `apps/rph-demo`'s own `check-types` is `svelte-check`, which understands `.svelte`. **The harness compiles the app with a weaker compiler than the app's own gate.**
  - **`apps/rph-demo/e2e/` IS UNDER NO TYPE GATE AT ALL** — the same `--listFiles` run loads **zero** files from it, and 16 ledger entries name an `.e2e.ts` victim. Every e2e victim is typechecked by nothing, so REG-F-097's failure mode (a victim calling a method that no longer exists) is open on the Playwright path. **This is the `verif/`-had-no-type-gate finding again, in a different directory** — a standing ratchet living where nothing checks it.
- **A FINDING OF MINE WAS DOWNGRADED BY ITS OWN REFUTERS, AND THEY WERE RIGHT.** I carried `S3-CONTROL-e2e-victim-is-actually-run` as a headline: `runPlaywright` writes no vitest JSON, so `controlVerdict` finds no report and returns `INCONCLUSIVE` — the entry can report `CONTROL_HELD` or `INCONCLUSIVE` and **never `SURVIVED`**. That is true, and both adversarial reviewers moved it to COSMETIC on the ground that **it fails CLOSED**: INCONCLUSIVE blocks, so nothing passes on it. It remains a control whose declared finding is unreportable — worth recording, **not** worth the severity I gave it.
- **⚠ ONE AUDIT DIMENSION IS UNCOVERED, AND SILENCE ABOUT IT WOULD BE THE DEFECT THIS ENTRY IS ABOUT.** The fourth probe — **the honesty of `KILLED` itself**, the verdict carrying the gate's entire claim — **failed outright** (structured-output retry cap, five failed calls, no result). So the questions *"can a suite redden for a reason unrelated to the mutation and still be scored KILLED"* and *"does anything check that the named victim ASSERTS ON the mutated code"* are **not answered anywhere in this entry**. Three of four dimensions were audited. **A three-of-four audit reported as an audit is exactly the population-narrowing this register keeps recording.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/verdict.ts` (new), `scripts/mutants/run.ts`, `verif/control-verdict.test.ts` (new). **Safe default:** **a decision that cannot be reached by a test will not be reviewed by anything else** — when a verdict lives inside a script, the script's untestability is a property of the verdict too, and the remedy is to move the decision rather than to read it more carefully.

### REG-F-166 — 38 e2e specs were compiled by nothing, and the first thing the gate found was a type that under-described its own payload
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** A MISSING TYPE GATE INSTALLED, with its failure DRIVEN before it was believed · **Status:** CLOSED. The gate is wired, fires, and its first catch was real.
- **`apps/rph-demo/e2e/` WAS UNDER NO TYPE GATE AT ALL.** `bunx tsc --noEmit -p apps/rph-demo/tsconfig.json --listFiles` loads **1640 files and ZERO from `e2e/`** — measured, not inferred. The app's own `check-types` is `svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json`, and that config extends the generated `.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json`, whose `include` covers `src/` only. **38 spec files and `playwright.config.ts` were typechecked by nothing**, and **16 ledger entries name an `.e2e.ts` file as the victim proving a guard.**
- **⚠ THIS IS THE `verif/`-HAD-NO-TYPE-GATE FINDING AGAIN, IN A DIFFERENT DIRECTORY.** That one cost a standing ratchet which died silently for two days. The general form is stated here rather than the instance: **a directory outside a build's `include` is outside its gate too, and nothing announces the difference** — the suite still runs, the specs still pass, and the only symptom is an error nobody is positioned to see.
- **WHAT THE GATE CAUGHT ON ITS FIRST RUN, and it was not cosmetic.** `EngineSnapshot` (`e2e/support/harness.ts:11`) declares eleven fields; `test-api/introspect/+server.ts:39` returns **twelve**. `assurancePolicies` has been returned all along and was never declared, so **the type under-described its own payload** and the specs reading it compensated with inline casts — `(p: { state: { name?: string } })` — which is what an under-described payload looks like from the consumer side: **hand-annotation where the type should have spoken.**
- **⚠ AND MY FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS WHY IT IS RECORDED.** Seeing `Property 'assurancePolicies' does not exist`, I took it for REG-F-097's failure mode — a rotted spec calling something that no longer exists. **It is the opposite:** the property exists at runtime and the TYPE lagged it. A grep for the symbol in production settled it in one command. **A type error naming a missing property is ambiguous between "the caller rotted" and "the type never kept up", and the two have opposite remedies.**
- **THE REMAINING TWELVE ERRORS WERE ALL ONE FILE AND ONE SHAPE:** unnarrowed `.find()` results in `policy-manager.e2e.ts`. Fixed with a `must<T>(row, what)` helper that asserts and narrows, **not with `!`** — a bare non-null assertion silences the compiler while leaving the runtime failure exactly as opaque, whereas this turns a missing row into a NAMED assertion failure instead of a TypeError three lines later.
- **THE GATE'S OWN FAILURE WAS DRIVEN BEFORE IT WAS BELIEVED (REG-F-163's rule, applied).** The field was renamed to `assurancePoliciesTYPO` and `check-types` re-run. **The proof is in the output:** `svelte-check` reported `1660 FILES 0 ERRORS` — seeing nothing — and the new `tsc -p ./e2e/tsconfig.json` step then reported all four. **That single run demonstrates the blindness and the fix in the same output**, which is worth more than either claim on its own.
- **AND THE MODIFIED SPEC WAS ACTUALLY RUN**, because `must()` ADDS assertions where there were none and a typecheck cannot tell whether a spec still passes: `bunx playwright test e2e/policy-manager.e2e.ts` — **1 passed (15.1s)**, tree clean afterwards.
- **WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, and it is the neighbour finding from REG-F-165:** the mutation harness's `compileVerdict` still compiles this app with raw `tsc`, which loads **zero `.svelte` files**, while the app's own gate uses `svelte-check`. **Six ledger entries target `.svelte` files and are compiled by an instrument that cannot see them** — their `NO_COMPILE` arm is structurally unreachable and a `KILLED` on them cannot exclude *"the page failed to build"*. Adding an e2e tsconfig does not touch that; it is a separate increment and is left open rather than smuggled in beside a green run.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `apps/rph-demo/e2e/tsconfig.json` (new), `apps/rph-demo/package.json`, `e2e/support/harness.ts`, `e2e/policy-manager.e2e.ts`. **Safe default:** **ask which files a gate actually LOADS, not which it appears to cover** — `--listFiles` answers in one command what a config's `include` chain hides across three files, and a suite that runs is not evidence that anything typechecked it.

### REG-F-167 — a control written to check MY derivation found a field declared on 200 commands and read by nothing
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** A DEFERRED RUNTIME PROBE REPLACED BY A STRONGER GATE + an unrelated defect the gate's own CONTROL surfaced · **Status:** CLOSED for both. The dual-spelling defect is PINNED, not repaired, and the reason is stated.
- **REG-F-156 AND REG-F-161 BOTH LEFT THE SAME THING OWED:** their two dead READ branches rest on `AssuranceObservation.disposition` being born `OPEN` and never advancing, and both entries recorded that this was a STATIC derivation over a single write funnel, with a runtime probe owed. **The probe is not what was missing.**
- **THE THIRD LIMB, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN THE PROBE WOULD HAVE BEEN.** REG-F-156 argued from the WRITE FUNNEL — `objectType: OBSERVATION` occurs at exactly one commit site — which is a claim about what the code currently writes. The contract registry answers a different question: **exactly ONE registered command targets `ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION`, and it is `RecordAssuranceObservation`, the creation.** That is a claim about what the system CAN BE ASKED TO DO, and for a negative it is strictly stronger: **a command that does not exist cannot be dispatched, whatever any handler contains.** The two limbs are independent — either could break while the other held.
- **AND A GATE BEATS A PROBE HERE FOR A REASON WORTH KEEPING.** A runtime probe observes once. The two `expectSurvive` CONTROLS report only at the end of a 37-minute run, and only ever say *"still dead"* — **neither can say that someone is ABOUT to make the branch live.** What invalidates REG-F-161 is a NEW COMMAND, and a command appears in the registry long before any branch changes behaviour. The pin costs milliseconds, runs on every `bun run test`, and its failure message names exactly what to re-drive and which two ledger entries to retire.
- **⚠ AND THE CONTROL I WROTE TO CHECK MY OWN DERIVATION FIRED ON ITS FIRST RUN — FINDING SOMETHING LARGER THAN THE BUG IT WAS WATCHING FOR.** The main pin passes with one command; a reader that resolved *nothing useful* would also pass it. So the control asserted that a genuinely driven aggregate shows SEVERAL commands — `commandsTargeting('PWU')`. **It returned ZERO**, and the reader was not the cause.
- **`COMMANDS[*].targetAggregateType` IS READ BY NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY.** `command-bus.ts` validates `COMMANDS[type].payload` and only that. The envelope's own `targetAggregateType` is `z.ZodString` — unconstrained — and its sole production read is a label inside a refusal message (`kit.ts:70`). **Nothing ever compares the DECLARED target against the DISPATCHED one**, and until this commit nothing enumerated by it either: the single reader in the whole repository is the file added here.
- **THE SEARCHES BEHIND "READ BY NOTHING", because that is a claim about MY SEARCH until it states itself (P-3).** Three greps over `packages/ verif/ apps/ scripts/`, excluding `dist/`: (1) `grep -rn "targetAggregateType"` — every production hit is a WRITE or a label: `broker.ts:780,789,801` and `floor-fixtures.ts` CONSTRUCT envelopes, `kit.ts:70` uses it as a message subject, `command-bus.ts:326` names it in a comment about what dispatch validates. (2) `grep -rn "COMMANDS\["` — three hits, none reading this field. (3) `grep -rn "\.targetAggregateType"` minus envelope reads and object-literal writes — **exactly ONE hit, the file added by this entry.** **POSITIVE CONTROL, same shape and a different answer:** the sibling field IS read — `command-bus.ts` validates against `COMMANDS[type].payload`, and grep finds it — so the search discriminates between a consumed registry field and an unconsumed one rather than being blind to both.
- **THE CONSEQUENCE IS EXACTLY WHAT AN UNREAD FIELD ACCUMULATES: SEVEN AGGREGATES ARE SPELLED TWO WAYS**, splitting 54 commands across keys no consumer reconciles — `PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT` ×4 beside `ProfessionalWorkUnit` ×9, `EXECUTION_PLAN` ×14 beside `ExecutionPlan` ×3, and five more. **It breaks nothing today precisely BECAUSE nothing reads it, and that is the finding rather than a mitigation:** the next census keyed on this field silently reports a subset, which is this programme's oldest defect lying in wait inside a field nobody consumes.
- **PINNED BY NAME WITH COUNTS, NOT REPAIRED, AND THE REASON IS THE DIFF.** `messages.ts` is GENERATED from `packages/rph-contracts/vocab/`, so normalising the spellings is a vocab change plus a regeneration whose diff must be inspected on its own terms — smuggling it in beside a green run is how a large regeneration goes unreviewed. What must not happen meanwhile is the set GROWING quietly, so a new split reddens.
- **A SMALL SELF-CORRECTION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE WEEK'S OTHERS.** My first pin listed the seven in Python's byte order (`BASELINE` before `Baseline`); JS `localeCompare` orders them the other way, so the pin failed on its own transcription. Fixed by COMPUTING the expected value from the registry rather than typing it out — **a pinned literal transcribed by hand is a second copy of a derivable value**, which is the rule this register already runs on.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `verif/observation-command-surface.test.ts` (new). **Safe default:** **when a fact is held by derivation, gate the EVENT that would falsify it rather than re-observing the fact** — and write the control that proves your reader works, because it is the assertion most likely to find something you were not looking for.

- **⚠ THE KILLED ARM NEVER DIFFERENCES AGAINST A BASELINE, AND REG-F-116's OWN ARGUMENT SITS TWO LINES ABOVE IT.** `run.ts:536-540` says, of CONTROLS: *"The exit status cannot answer 'did this mutation redden anything'; the DIFFERENCE against the unmutated baseline can, and it is the only question actually being asked."* **`run.ts:542`, immediately below, reads `run.status === 0` and nothing else.** VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: `grep -n baseline scripts/mutants/run.ts` shows `baseline` is READ at exactly ONE site — `run.ts:399`, inside `controlVerdict`. Nine controls consult it; the 193 entries that can reach KILLED never do.
- **THE BLAST RADIUS, DERIVED FROM THE LEDGER RATHER THAN ESTIMATED: 193 killable entries ride on 70 DISTINCT VICTIM FILES.** Thirteen name `execrem-wp12-skip-authorization.test.ts`; ten name `execrem-wp12-authority.test.ts`; **46 ride on the top five files alone.** So **one unrelated red in one file silently converts thirteen mutants to KILLED**, each recorded as a guard proven. And `takeBaseline()` is gated at `run.ts:834` on a control being selected, so `bun run mutants <named-victim-id>` takes no baseline at all.
- **⚠⚠ UPDATE, 2026-08-17 — `run.ts:834` NEVER POINTED AT THE GATE IT NAMES, AND NO LATER CHANGE CAUSED THAT.** Checked at `77622ee4`, the commit before the instrument sweep first touched this file: line 834 was a comment about Windows path casing, and `takeBaseline()`'s selection gate — `if (!PREFLIGHT && selected.some((m) => m.expectSurvive !== undefined)) takeBaseline();` — was at **`:1015`**. The citation was wrong when it was written and nothing caught it. ⚠ **THE SUBSTANTIVE CLAIM STANDS, RE-DERIVED:** the gate is real, it is conditioned on a control being selected, and `bun run mutants <named-victim-id>` therefore takes no baseline at all. After `e7d89847` it sits at **`:1086`**. **Cite `takeBaseline()`'s selection gate, not a line.** Recorded rather than silently renumbered, and deliberately distinguished from the annotation further down this register: a citation that was NEVER right is a different finding from one that ROTTED, and this entry is the first kind while the `run.ts:652` note is the second.
- **⚠ THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT REG-F-116 FIXED, LEFT UNAPPLIED TO THE ARM IT WAS WRITTEN ABOUT.** That entry found three controls reporting `SURVIVED — something asserts on prose` because one unrelated pinned literal was red elsewhere. The remedy — grade on the DIFFERENCE — was built, tested, and applied to nine entries. **The 193 that carry the gate's actual claim kept reading the bit the remedy exists to replace.**
- **NOT FIXED HERE, AND THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS ALREADY CLEAR.** The victim must be GREEN unmutated before its mutant's red can be attributed. Because 193 mutants ride on only **70** distinct files, that is 70 cached baseline runs, not 193. ~~roughly **+3.5 minutes on a 37.8-minute run (+9%)**~~ — **⚠ THAT FIGURE WAS WRONG AND IS MINE, CORRECTED ONE COMMIT LATER (REG-F-170).** It priced all 70 victims at vitest speed. **Eight of them are Playwright specs at ~29.7 s each**, so the honest naive cost is **62×3.0 s + 8×29.7 s = 424 s, +18.7%** — and 56% of the added time comes from 11% of the victims. **The same defect this register keeps recording: a number whose population I never checked.** **AND THE CORRECTION SUGGESTS THE DESIGN.** Those 8 e2e baselines need not be 8 invocations: `playwright test <all 8 specs>` boots the server ONCE, so the e2e half falls from ~238 s to roughly 30 s + 8×~5 s ≈ 70 s, giving **~256 s (+11.3%)** overall. That converts the central verdict from *"the suite is red"* into *"the suite went green → red"*, which is the claim actually being made. It restructures the verdict path and belongs in its own increment with its own predicted reds.
- **WHAT IS FIXED: A NON-COMPLETION IS NO LONGER A KILL.** `run.ts` read one field of the spawn result. `spawnSync` reports three other outcomes through fields it never touched — `signal` non-null (killed by SIGTERM, an external `taskkill`, an OOM kill), `error` defined (the spawn failed, or ENOBUFS), and `status: null` (no exit code at all). **All three arrived at `run.status === 0 ? SURVIVED : KILLED` and came out KILLED.** `nonCompletion` in `verdict.ts` now asks first, returns INCONCLUSIVE with the reason, and is covered by six fixture cases — VERIFIED by grep that `run.error` and `run.signal` appeared nowhere in the runner before this.
- **⚠ AND MY FIRST FIX FOR THE SECOND HALF WAS INERT — I FOUND OUT BY DRIVING IT.** The audit reported, and I reproduced, that under Bun a child which **exits 0** having written more than 1,048,576 bytes comes back as `{ status: 1, signal: null, error: undefined, stdout: '' }` — a PASSING suite reported as a failure with its evidence buffer emptied, invisible to `timeoutEvidence` because that scans the buffer. I added `maxBuffer: 64MB` and measured all four combinations:

  | options | status | stdout | error |
  |---|---:|---:|---|
  | `shell:true` + no maxBuffer | 1 | 0 | none |
  | `shell:true` + maxBuffer 64M | **1** | **0** | none |
  | `shell:false` + no maxBuffer | null | 1,083,002 | **ENOBUFS** |
  | `shell:false` + maxBuffer 64M | **0** | 1,262,100 | none |

  **`shell: true` is the cause and `maxBuffer` cannot reach it.** Note row three: without the shell the overrun surfaces as ENOBUFS, which `nonCompletion` DOES catch — **the shell wrapper is precisely what erases the evidence.** The knob was REMOVED rather than kept: a guard for a case it provably cannot reach is the hollow this repository deletes on principle, exactly as the `createObject` exemption was deleted under REG-F-086. The real fix is dropping `shell: true`, which changes how all 205 spawns resolve `bunx` on Windows and is its own increment.
- **MITIGATING, AND STATED SO THE SEVERITY IS HONEST:** no victim file contains a `console.*` call and the largest is 43 KB, so a passing targeted run is unlikely to reach 1 MiB today. **Nothing guards it**, and the same mechanism silently truncates the evidence `timeoutEvidence` scans — which `measured.ts:56-57` claims cannot happen (*"Under-detection is the dangerous direction, and the anchoring cannot cause it"* — true of the anchoring, false of the buffer).
- **ALSO REPORTED, NOT YET VERIFIED BY ME, AND CARRIED AS LEADS RATHER THAN FINDINGS:** Playwright `webServer` failures (port 4319 under `--strictPort` with `reuseExistingServer: false`) match no `TIMEOUT_MARKER` and would score KILLED with an EMPTY detail across the 16 e2e entries; and a Playwright `expect` timeout (7 s, against a 30 s test timeout) renders as a matcher message rather than `Test timeout of Nms exceeded`, so the commonest browser flake is not seen as a timeout either. **Both are plausible and neither has been driven by me.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/verdict.ts`, `scripts/mutants/run.ts`, `verif/control-verdict.test.ts`. **Safe default:** **an exit status is not an attribution** — a red suite says something failed, never that your change caused it, and a gate that skips the difference is measuring the tree's health and reporting it as the guard's.

### REG-F-169 — the CONTROL crossed the timeout first, so the check survived and the proof that it works did not
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** A LOAD-DEPENDENT FAILURE DIAGNOSED, and it explains an earlier one recorded as unreproducible · **Status:** CLOSED.
- **OBSERVED WHILE GATING REG-F-168:** `verif/register-citations.test.ts` failed under `--project verif` with `Test timed out in 5000ms`, and **passed in 2.2 s when the file ran alone.** Reproduced three times, so not a flake.
- **THE CAUSE IS THE CORPUS GROWING, AND I GREW IT.** Both assertions there walk the whole canon corpus plus `packages/ verif/ scripts/ apps/ docs/` resolving every `REG-[DFQ]-\d+` citation. **The register gained eleven entries in this session alone.** Nothing anywhere set `testTimeout`, so both ran against vitest's **5000 ms default** — a fixed budget under a cost that rises with every entry written. A census whose work grows with the thing it scans will cross a fixed default eventually; the only question is which assertion crosses first.
- **⚠ AND IT WAS THE **CONTROL** THAT DIED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** The assertion — *does every cited id resolve* — was still green. The CONTROL — *does the reader see real data rather than returning `[]` for everything, and is a fabricated id actually caught* — is the one that timed out. **So under load this file kept its CHECK and lost the EVIDENCE THAT THE CHECK WORKS**, which is the strictly more dangerous half to lose: a green `toEqual([])` from a reader that found nothing is indistinguishable from a green one from a reader that found everything and resolved it.
- **AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT BAD LUCK.** A control does **strictly more work** than the assertion it guards — here it computes both halves *and* a synthetic negative case — so under a shared budget **the control is systematically the first casualty.** REG-F-136 recorded the same shape from the other direction (*"controls are the first thing a slow foreign suite takes offline"*); this arrives by growth rather than by a foreign suite, and the remedy is the same: **the control gets the same budget as the assertion it guards, explicitly, and never inherits a default.**
- **IT ALSO DIAGNOSES A FAILURE THIS REGISTER RECORDED AS UNREPRODUCIBLE.** An earlier item stood open as *"two filesystem-scanning censuses in `rph-domain` failed in one whole-suite run and did not reproduce"* — **same mechanism**: filesystem-scanning censuses against the 5000 ms default, failing only under whole-suite CPU contention and passing in isolation, which is exactly why re-running them alone cleared them and taught nothing. **A load-dependent timeout is unreproducible by the obvious retry**, and that property is what kept it filed as noise.
- **THE SAME 5000 ms DEFAULT IS NOW IMPLICATED TWICE IN ONE DAY.** REG-F-164 recorded it as the reason parallelising the mutation gate would manufacture blocking `INCONCLUSIVE` verdicts on a six-core machine. Here it silently disarmed a control. **A default that no configuration file mentions is a decision nobody made**, and it is now load-bearing in two independent places.
- **FIXED NARROWLY, ON PURPOSE.** Both assertions in that file get an explicit 30 s budget, with the reason written at the site. **A global `testTimeout` raise was NOT taken:** it would hide the next census that grows past its budget, and the value of this failure was that it announced itself.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `verif/register-citations.test.ts`. **Safe default:** **give a control the same budget as the assertion it guards, explicitly** — and treat "failed under load, passes alone" as a diagnosis rather than a flake, because the retry that clears it is the same act that destroys the evidence.

### REG-F-170 — I priced the remedy over a population I never checked, one commit after recording that exact defect
- **Date:** 2026-08-14 · **Type:** MY OWN COST FIGURE CORRECTED + the correction improved the design · **Status:** CLOSED for the number. The remedy itself is **still not built**, and is now cheaper than either figure.
- **REG-F-168 COSTED ITS OWN REMEDY AT "+3.5 MINUTES (+9%)".** The reasoning was that 193 killable mutants ride on only 70 distinct victim files, so a per-victim baseline needs 70 runs rather than 193. The count was right. **The price was not: I multiplied all 70 by the vitest average of 3.0 s.**
- **DERIVED FROM THE LEDGER RATHER THAN ASSUMED: 62 of the 70 are vitest suites and EIGHT are Playwright specs.** At the measured leg averages (REG-F-164: vitest targeted 3.0 s, Playwright 29.7 s) the honest naive cost is **62×3.0 + 8×29.7 = 424 s, or +18.7%** — more than double what I published. **Fifty-six per cent of the added time comes from eleven per cent of the victims.**
- **⚠ AND IT IS THE DEFECT THIS REGISTER HAS BEEN RECORDING ALL SESSION, COMMITTED ONE COMMIT AFTER RECORDING IT.** REG-F-160 corrected a coverage denominator that silently included arrows nothing could cover. REG-F-164 retired two undated durations used to justify speedups. **Then I averaged a population I had already been told was heterogeneous** — my own REG-F-164 table has the two leg speeds ten lines apart, differing by a factor of ten. **A mean over a population you have not partitioned is a guess wearing arithmetic.**
- **THE CORRECTION IMPROVED THE DESIGN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** Once the 8 Playwright baselines are visible AS Playwright, the obvious economy appears: they need not be eight invocations. `playwright test <all 8 specs>` boots the dev server ONCE — and that boot, not the tests, is what costs ~30 s (`reuseExistingServer: false`, measured at 29.7 s average for runs of a single spec). So the e2e half falls from ~238 s to roughly **30 s + 8×~5 s ≈ 70 s**, and the whole remedy to **~256 s (+11.3%)**. **The wrong number hid a design that only became visible once the population was split.**
- **STILL NOT BUILT, AND THE SCOPE IS UNCHANGED BY THIS ENTRY.** The per-victim baseline restructures the runner's central loop and needs its own increment with its own predicted reds — that judgement was right in REG-F-168 and is not revisited here. What changed is only that the increment is now correctly priced and has a cheaper shape.
- **Merge target:** none — this entry is the correction; REG-F-168's sentence is struck in place. **Safe default:** **before averaging a cost over a population, partition it by the thing that makes members expensive** — **and REG-F-171 then found a SECOND axis of the same error: the Playwright average was measured over FAILING runs, which retry, so it over-priced the PASSING baselines by 100 s. Partition by kind AND by outcome** — — and when a corrected number is more than double the original, ask what the design looks like now, because the figure that was hiding the cost was usually hiding the remedy too.

### REG-F-171 — the kill arm now grades on a difference, which is what its own neighbouring comment said it should do
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** REG-F-168's CENTRAL FINDING REMEDIED · **Status:** BUILT and unit-proven. **The end-to-end drive has NOT happened at this commit** — it is the next command, and this entry does not claim it.
- **WHAT REG-F-168 FOUND:** `run.ts` said, of CONTROLS, *"The exit status cannot answer 'did this mutation redden anything'; the DIFFERENCE against the unmutated baseline can, and it is the only question actually being asked"* — and the line immediately below graded **193 named-victim mutants on `run.status === 0` alone.** Those 193 ride on only **70 distinct victim files**, thirteen on `execrem-wp12-skip-authorization.test.ts`, so **one unrelated red converted thirteen mutants to KILLED**, each recorded as a guard proven.
- **THE REMEDY, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE REG-F-116 BUILT FOR CONTROLS:** before a mutation is written, the victim is run UNMUTATED and the result cached BY VICTIM. `gradeNamedVictim` then reports **KILLED only for a red that follows a green**. A red that follows a red is **INCONCLUSIVE** — the mutation was never measured, so there is no verdict, and INCONCLUSIVE blocks rather than reading as proof.
- **CACHED BY VICTIM, NOT BY MUTANT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE ECONOMY:** 193 entries, 70 distinct victims. **And it runs on a CLEAN TREE by construction** — called from `runMutant` after `preApplyVerdict`'s `treeIsClean` gate has passed and before the mutation is written. Baselining with a mutant on disk would bake the mutation into its own baseline, which is precisely the defect REG-F-116 recorded for the whole-suite baseline; there was no reason to re-learn it.
- **⚠ AND THE COST IS THE HIGHER FIGURE, NOT THE LOWER ONE — STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE I PUBLISHED BOTH.** REG-F-170 corrected the naive price to **424 s (+18.7%)** and then showed a cheaper shape: batching the eight e2e baselines into ONE Playwright invocation, which boots the dev server once, for **~256 s (+11.3%)**. **The batching is NOT in this increment.** Each e2e victim is cached separately and therefore boots its own server, so this change costs the +18.7%. The batching is filed, and claiming the cheaper number here would be quoting a design rather than the build.
- **PREDICTED RED MEASURED, on the arm that matters:** neutering `if (!victimWasGreen)` reddens **exactly 2 of 19** — the two RED-before cases — while the other seventeen hold, including the control asserting that KILLED and SURVIVED both remain reachable on a green baseline. **A tightening that swallowed the real verdicts would look identical in the summary and is the failure mode this control exists for.**
- **A STALE SENTENCE CORRECTED IN THE SAME FILE, one commit old and mine.** `nonCompletion`'s docstring still said *"`maxBuffer` is raised at the call site to make the truncation far less reachable"* — **I removed that knob in REG-F-168 after measuring it inert.** A comment describing a fix that no longer exists is worse than no comment, because it tells the next reader the case is handled.
- **~~⚠ WHAT IS NOT YET DONE: the WIRING has not been driven.~~ ✅ DRIVEN, AND THEN VALIDATED AT SCALE.** Single mutant: the `vitest victim BASELINE` leg appeared at 2.8 s and `F159-birth-drift-refusal-neutered` still reported **KILLED at 3 failed tests** — the same verdict as before, now attributed. Full run at `52dc5e1a`: **205 distinct measured, SURVIVED 0, UNANCHORED 0, NO_COMPILE 0, KILLED_UNNAMED 0, ABORTED_DIRTY 0, CONTROL_HELD 9, and INCONCLUSIVE 0** (KILLED = 193, derived from the summary's own arithmetic rather than read off a line the captured tail had cut — said so rather than quoting a number I did not see).
- **✅ THE ANSWER FIXTURES COULD NOT REACH: ALL 70 VICTIMS WERE GREEN AT HEAD.** `INCONCLUSIVE 0` means no mutant in this ledger has been riding on an already-red suite. **The remedy changed no verdict**, which is exactly what a correct tightening must do — a change to the verdict path that immediately produced new findings would be evidence it had broken something, not that it had found something. What it changes is what a KILLED is ENTITLED to claim from now on.
- **⚠ AND THE MEASURED COST REFUTES MY OWN ESTIMATE FOR THE THIRD TIME, IN THE SAFE DIRECTION AND FOR A NEW REASON.** Predicted **+424 s (+18.7%)**; measured **2615.5 s against 2268.0 s = +347.5 s (+15.3%)**. The vitest half landed almost exactly (predicted 62×3.0 = 186 s, measured **182.9 s**). The e2e half did not: predicted 8×29.7 = 238 s, measured **138.5 s at 17.3 s each**. **The 29.7 s figure is the average of MUTANT e2e runs, and mutant runs FAIL by design — with `retries: 1`, a failing spec runs TWICE.** A green baseline passes first time and never retries. **I priced a PASSING operation using an average measured over FAILING ones.** REG-F-170 was the same class with a different axis (vitest vs Playwright); this is passing vs failing, and both are the one error: **an average is a property of the population it was measured over, and carrying it to another population is exactly REG-F-160's denominator defect wearing arithmetic.**
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/verdict.ts`, `scripts/mutants/run.ts`, `verif/control-verdict.test.ts`. **Safe default:** **a verdict is a difference or it is a coincidence** — and when a codebase already contains the argument for a fix, applying it to one arm and not the other leaves the stronger claim resting on the weaker evidence.

### REG-F-172 — the attribution fix closed a defect it was not aimed at, because a difference needs no list of failure modes
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** AN UNVERIFIED LEAD DRIVEN TO A VERDICT — and it was already fixed · **Status:** CLOSED for the environmental half. **The flake half is NOT closed and is stated separately.**
- **THE LEAD, CARRIED SINCE REG-F-168 AS EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED BY ME:** a Playwright `webServer` failure — port 4319 is occupied, `--strictPort` refuses to fall back, `reuseExistingServer: false` forces a fresh boot — emits text matching **neither** of `measured.ts`'s two `TIMEOUT_MARKERS`, so the runner would score it **KILLED with an empty detail** across the 15 e2e-dispatched entries. Plausible, and not driven.
- **DRIVEN, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT REG-F-171 HAD ALREADY CLOSED IT.** I occupied 127.0.0.1:4319 and ran a real e2e mutant (`MU-FRESH-18-D-template-stops-carrying-the-revision`, victim `baselines.e2e.ts`):

  | port 4319 | verdict | why |
  |---|---|---|
  | **occupied** | **INCONCLUSIVE — the gate BLOCKS** | the victim's UNMUTATED baseline also fails, so `victimWasGreen` is false |
  | **free** | **KILLED** | baseline green, mutated red — the guard is genuinely proven |

  **Both halves driven**, because a change that refused everything would produce the first row and prove nothing; the second row is what shows the discrimination is real.
- **⚠ AND THE MECHANISM IS THE FINDING, NOT THE INSTANCE. AN ENVIRONMENTAL FAILURE FAILS BOTH RUNS.** `TIMEOUT_MARKERS` works by ENUMERATING how a spurious failure is phrased — two regexes today, and the audit named at least four unlisted phrasings (three `webServer` messages plus the `expect`-timeout rendering). **That list can never be complete: the set of ways a run can fail for reasons unrelated to the mutation is unbounded, and every new one arrives as a false KILLED.** Differencing against a baseline needs no list at all. **REG-F-171 was built to make a kill attributable and, as a consequence nobody designed, subsumed an entire category of misclassification it was never told about.**
- **THE GENERAL FORM: PREFER A CLOSED PREDICATE TO AN OPEN ENUMERATION.** *"Did this run fail in one of the ways I have listed?"* is unbounded and fails open on everything unlisted. *"Did this run fail in a way the unmutated run did not?"* is closed, and its coverage does not depend on anyone's imagination. Where both are available, the enumeration is at best a better ERROR MESSAGE — never the guarantee.
- **⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE HONEST PART OF THIS ENTRY: FLAKES.** The two failure classes behave oppositely under a baseline:
  - **ENVIRONMENTAL** (port collision, server won't boot, browser missing, disk full) — fails the baseline TOO, so the baseline catches it. **Closed.**
  - **FLAKY** (a timing-dependent assertion; the `expect` timeout of 7 s against a 30 s test timeout that the audit raised) — can pass the baseline and fail the mutated run **for reasons that have nothing to do with the mutation.** The baseline cannot see it, and it is still scored **KILLED**. **OPEN**, and the remedy is a confirmation re-run of a red victim, not a longer marker list.
- **COST: NOTHING, IN THE CASE THAT MATTERS.** The failing baseline took **0.8 s** — a port collision is refused immediately. The safety is paid for only when the environment is broken, which is when a wrong verdict is most expensive.
- **Merge target:** none — no code changed; this entry records a verification and retires a lead. **Safe default:** **when a lead survives long enough to be driven, drive it — it may already be fixed, and knowing WHY it is fixed is worth more than the fix**; here it revealed that the remedy's reach is wider than its design, and named the one class it still does not reach.
