### REG-F-173 — the channel with no flake protection was the one whose flakes had been measured
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** REG-F-172's OPEN HALF CLOSED, at roughly no cost · **Status:** BUILT. **The drive has NOT happened at this commit** — it is the next command and this entry does not claim it.
- **REG-F-172 SPLIT THE FAILURE MODES AND CLOSED ONE.** A per-victim baseline catches ENVIRONMENTAL failures because those fail the baseline too. It is blind to FLAKES: a timing-dependent test can pass the baseline and fail the mutated run for reasons unrelated to the mutation, and that was still scored **KILLED**.
- **⚠ THE ASYMMETRY, AND IT IS THE FINDING.** `playwright.config.ts:30` has set `retries: 1` all along, so **the e2e channel has always confirmed its reds** — a fail-then-pass exits zero and reports SURVIVED. **Vitest had neither a retry nor a `testTimeout` override.** And REG-F-169 measured that this repository's actual, observed flake mechanism is precisely a load-dependent crossing of vitest's **5000 ms default** — the same mechanism that had already disarmed a control and left two `rph-domain` censuses filed as unreproducible. **The unprotected channel was the one whose flakes had been observed**, and the protected one was where no flake had ever been recorded.
- **`--retry=1` RE-RUNS THE FAILED TEST, NOT THE SUITE**, so confirmation costs milliseconds. The obvious alternative — re-run the whole victim on every red — would have cost roughly **+20%** on top of REG-F-171's +15.3%, which is why the cheap shape mattered rather than merely being nice.
- **⚠ AND IT IS A CLOSED PREDICATE, WHICH IS REG-F-172's RULE APPLIED RATHER THAN QUOTED.** It does not ask *"did this fail in one of the ways I listed"* — the `TIMEOUT_MARKERS` shape whose list can never be complete. It asks whether the failure **REPRODUCES**. Every nondeterministic failure gets a second chance, including mechanisms nobody has thought of.
- **⚠⚠ APPLIED TO ALL FOUR VITEST INVOCATIONS, BASELINE INCLUDED, AND THE SYMMETRY IS LOAD-BEARING.** Retrying only the mutated run would let a flaky BASELINE red stand, flipping `victimWasGreen` to false and manufacturing a spurious INCONCLUSIVE — **a new false verdict introduced by the fix for false verdicts.** This is REG-F-116's rule (*"the baseline must carry the IDENTICAL filter as the control run"*) restated for a different option, which is why it is a shared constant rather than a literal typed at four call sites.
- **THE POLARITY, STATED SO NOBODY HAS TO DERIVE IT:** a flake now exits zero, so the mutant reports **SURVIVED and BLOCKS**. That is a false BLOCKING finding, never a false KILL — the same direction Playwright has always failed in, and the safe one: **a gate that over-blocks wastes time; a gate that under-blocks certifies a guard that does not exist.**
- **AND IT IS NOT A REVERSAL OF REG-F-169, WHICH REFUSED A GLOBAL TIMEOUT RAISE.** That refusal stands and this does not touch it: **no timeout is changed anywhere**, `bun run test` keeps the 5000 ms default, and a census that outgrows its budget still announces itself exactly as REG-F-169 required. What changes is only whether a NON-REPRODUCING failure is allowed to certify a guard.
- **~~⚠ NOT YET DRIVEN~~ ✅ DRIVEN, SINGLE AND AT SCALE.** Single mutant: `F159-birth-drift-refusal-neutered` still **KILLED at 3 failed tests**. Full run at `7df537cd`: **205 distinct, SURVIVED 0, UNANCHORED 0, NO_COMPILE 0, KILLED_UNNAMED 0, ABORTED_DIRTY 0, INCONCLUSIVE 0, CONTROL_HELD 9** (KILLED = 193, derived from the summary arithmetic — the captured tail cut the line again). **`SURVIVED 0` is the check that mattered: not one real kill was softened into a survival.** The cost, however, could not be measured — see REG-F-174.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/run.ts`. **Safe default:** **when two channels do the same job, ask which one lacks the protection the other has** — and expect the gap to be where the failures were actually observed, because that is the channel people were looking at when they built the protection elsewhere.

### REG-F-174 — I have been quoting single-run costs all day, and the noise floor is bigger than most of the effects
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A METHOD DEFECT IN MY OWN MEASUREMENTS, found by looking for a cost that was not there · **Status:** CLOSED as a method. **Two cost figures I published are qualified in place.**
- **THE OCCASION:** REG-F-173 added `--retry=1` to the vitest victim runs. The run afterwards totalled **2848.7 s against 2615.5 s — +233.2 s, +8.9%.** That is far more than a retry should cost when no test fails spuriously, so before attributing it I asked whether the number was even measurable.
- **⚠ IT IS NOT. THE NOISE FLOOR EXCEEDS THE EFFECT, AND THE CONTROL IS PERFECT.** `tsc packages/rph-application` runs **78 calls in every single run** — identical work, and **no change of mine can touch a typecheck**. Across four runs it took **314.0 s, 302.2 s, 304.6 s, 351.5 s: a spread of +16.3%.** `vitest targeted` spreads +10.2% over the same runs. **A leg nothing changed moved further than the total I would have attributed to the change.**
- **SO THE `--retry=1` COST IS UNMEASURABLE WITH THIS INSTRUMENT**, and the honest statement is that it is *at most a few per cent and cannot be separated from machine variance* — not "+8.9%".
- **⚠⚠ AND THE SAME CAVEAT REACHES BACKWARDS INTO REG-F-171, WHICH I PUBLISHED AS "+15.3%".** That was also a single-run total difference (2615.5 vs 2268.0), and 15.3% sits inside a 16.3% noise band. **The figure is not wrong so much as unresolvable by the method that produced it.**
- **BUT REG-F-171'S COST IS RECOVERABLE, BECAUSE THAT CHANGE ADDED ITS OWN LEGS.** `printTimings` reports them directly: **`vitest victim BASELINE` 182.9 s + `playwright BASELINE` 138.5 s = 321.4 s of work that did not exist before.** That is a DIRECT measurement of the new operation, not a difference of two noisy totals, and it does not depend on the rest of the run being reproducible. **REG-F-171 costs ~321 s. The +15.3% was the right order by luck, arrived at the wrong way.**
- **THE GENERAL FORM, and it is the whole value of this entry: TO COST AN ADDED OPERATION, MEASURE THE OPERATION — NEVER THE DIFFERENCE OF TWO TOTALS.** Differencing totals inherits every source of variance in the run; reading the new leg's own line inherits none of it. **This is REG-F-160's denominator defect in the time domain**: I compared two numbers whose populations were not the same run, and only the CONTROL — a leg with a fixed call count — revealed it.
- **AND IT EXPLAINS WHY `--retry=1` HAS NO RECOVERABLE COST EITHER.** The retry happens INSIDE existing vitest invocations, so it adds no leg of its own; there is nothing to read directly, and total-differencing is below the noise floor. **An operation that adds no leg cannot be costed by this instrument at all** — which is a limit of the instrument, worth knowing before the next optimisation is justified by one.
- **WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED: THE CORRECTNESS CLAIMS.** REG-F-171 and REG-F-173 were built because the gate's verdicts were unattributed and unconfirmed, not because they were cheap. **`SURVIVED 0` at `7df537cd` is a verdict count, not a timing**, and it is exactly as sound as it was. Only the prices are qualified.
- **Merge target:** none — REG-F-171's and REG-F-173's cost sentences are qualified in place. **Safe default:** **before quoting a before/after delta, check a leg the change CANNOT have touched** — if that leg moved as much as your effect, you measured the machine.

### REG-F-175 — the harness compiled the app with a weaker compiler than the app's own gate, and six mutants were checked by a program that never contained them
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** THE LAST VERIFIED HOLE IN THE COMPILE LEG, CLOSED · **Status:** BUILT, and the blindness and its fix were demonstrated in a single experiment. **The runner drive is still owed** and is the next command.
- **`tsc` DOES NOT LOAD `.svelte` AT ALL.** `bunx tsc --noEmit -p apps/rph-demo/tsconfig.json --listFiles` reports **1640 files and ZERO `.svelte`**, because that config extends the generated `.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json`. **Six ledger entries target `.svelte` files** — derived from the ledger, not counted by hand — so for those six `compileVerdict` was typechecking a program **that never contained the mutated file.**
- **THREE CONSEQUENCES, AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.** The leg spent a full app typecheck proving nothing; `NO_COMPILE` was structurally unreachable for those six; and — the real cost — **a `KILLED` on them could not exclude *"the page simply failed to build"***. Separating *the compiler rejected this* from *the guard caught this* is the entire reason `compileVerdict` runs before the tests, and for `.svelte` mutants that separation was unavailable.
- **DEMONSTRATED IN ONE EXPERIMENT RATHER THAN ARGUED.** I inserted a deliberate type error into `apps/rph-demo/src/routes/baselines/+page.svelte` — a file two ledger entries target — and ran both compilers:

  | compiler | result |
  |---|---|
  | `tsc --noEmit -p apps/rph-demo/tsconfig.json` | **exit 0** — it cannot see the file at all |
  | `bun run --cwd apps/rph-demo check` (`svelte-check`) | **1 ERROR**, naming `+page.svelte 2:8`, exit 1 |

  **The blindness and the fix in the same output**, which is worth more than either claim separately.
- **⚠ IT INVOKES THE APP'S OWN SCRIPT RATHER THAN REIMPLEMENTING ITS COMMAND, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN POINT.** `apps/rph-demo`'s `check` is `svelte-kit sync && svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json`, reading **1660 files** — a strict superset of tsc's 1640. Calling the script BY NAME means the gate cannot drift from what the app actually checks: change the app's checker and this follows with nothing to remember. **Copying the command into the harness would have re-created the very gap being closed**, the next time the app changed its own gate — which is how the gap arose in the first place.
- **SCOPED TO `.svelte` MUTANTS ONLY.** The other sixteen `apps/rph-demo` entries target `.ts` files that `tsc` genuinely loads, and `svelte-check` is the slower instrument; there is no reason to spend it where the cheaper one is already sufficient. The predicate is `m.file.endsWith('.svelte')` — a property of the mutated file, not a package allowlist that would rot.
- **COST, AND IT WILL BE READ FROM ITS OWN LEG (REG-F-174's rule).** The change adds a `svelte-check apps/rph-demo` leg and removes six calls from `tsc apps/rph-demo`; both are named lines in `printTimings`, so the price is a DIRECT reading rather than a difference of two totals whose noise floor is +16.3%. **No estimate is offered here** — the next full run reports it.
- **~~⚠ NOT YET DRIVEN THROUGH THE RUNNER.~~ ✅ DRIVEN.** `MU-FRESH-18-D-template-stops-carrying-the-revision` (victim `baselines.e2e.ts`, mutating `+page.svelte`) took the new branch: the timing table shows **`svelte-check apps/rph-demo 14.5s`** and **no `tsc apps/rph-demo` leg at all** for that mutant, and the verdict is unchanged — **KILLED**, with **NO_COMPILE 0** confirming the mutation compiles, so the guard is genuinely what caught it rather than the compiler. **Cost read from the leg itself (REG-F-174’s rule): 14.5 s of `svelte-check` replacing ~7.7 s of `tsc`, so ~+7 s per `.svelte` mutant and ~+41 s over the six** — a direct reading, not a difference of totals.
- **✅ CONFIRMED AT SCALE at `fe16e6a8`, and the CALL COUNTS are the structural proof that exactly the right six moved.** `tsc apps/rph-demo` fell from **22 calls to 16**, and `svelte-check apps/rph-demo` appeared at **6 calls, 90.0 s, avg 15.0 s** — 22 = 16 + 6, with no other leg gaining or losing a call. Measured net cost **+45 s** (90.0 s added, ~45 s of `tsc` removed) against the ~+41 s read from one mutant. All six kept their verdicts: **205 distinct, SURVIVED 0, UNANCHORED 0, NO_COMPILE 0, KILLED_UNNAMED 0, ABORTED_DIRTY 0, INCONCLUSIVE 0, CONTROL_HELD 9.**
- **⚠ AND THE TOTAL IS DELIBERATELY NOT QUOTED AS A DELTA (REG-F-174).** This run totalled 3043.2 s, but `tsc packages/rph-domain` — which this change cannot touch — moved 191.2 s → 239.8 s, **+25% on 64 identical calls**. Differencing the totals would attribute the machine to the change; the leg arithmetic above does not.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/run.ts`. **Safe default:** **when a harness checks someone else's code, invoke THEIR gate rather than reconstructing it** — a reconstruction is correct only until the owner changes it, and nothing announces the moment it stops being correct.

### REG-F-176 — the shell wrapper was erasing the evidence, and dropping it closes the last measured hole in the kill arm
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** THE ROOT CAUSE REG-F-168 IDENTIFIED, NOW REMOVED · **Status:** ~~BUILT and proven at the seam. The runner drive is owed.~~ **INSTALLED — driven through the full runner at `6642430c`; 205 distinct, exit 0.**
- **REG-F-168 MEASURED THE DEFECT AND NAMED THE CAUSE WITHOUT FIXING IT.** Under Bun, a child that **exited 0** having written more than 1,048,576 bytes was delivered to this runner as `{ status: 1, signal: null, error: undefined, stdout: '' }` — **a PASSING suite reported as a failure with its evidence emptied.** The kill arm scored that KILLED, and `timeoutEvidence` was blind to it because it scans the buffer that had just been emptied.
- **THE FIX IS THE REMOVAL OF `shell: true`, AND THE FOUR-WAY MEASUREMENT IS WHY.** REG-F-168 tried `maxBuffer` first and found it **inert**, then removed it rather than keep a knob that provably could not fire:

  | options | status | stdout | error |
  |---|---:|---:|---|
  | `shell:true` + no maxBuffer | 1 | 0 | none |
  | `shell:true` + maxBuffer 64M | **1** | **0** | none — the knob cannot reach it |
  | `shell:false` + no maxBuffer | null | 1,083,002 | **ENOBUFS** — `nonCompletion` catches this |
  | `shell:false` + maxBuffer 64M | **0** | 1,262,100 | none — correct |

  **The shell wrapper is what erases the evidence.** Without it the same overrun surfaces as a real `ENOBUFS`, which REG-F-168's `nonCompletion` already refuses; with `maxBuffer` restored on top, it does not overrun at all.
- **PROVEN AT THE SEAM WITH THE RUNNER'S OWN OPTIONS, both arms in one output:** the same `exit 0` child through the OLD seam returns `status 1, 0 bytes` — **which would have been scored KILLED for a suite that passed** — and through the NEW seam returns `status 0, 1,262,100 bytes`, scored SURVIVED. **Not a description of a fix; the before and after of the exact call the runner makes.**
- **⚠ SAFE ON WINDOWS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, WHICH WAS THE ONLY REASON TO KEEP THE SHELL.** `shell: true` existed so `bunx` would resolve. Both `bunx vitest --version` and `bun --version` return **status 0 with `shell: false`** here. And the failure mode if it ever stopped resolving is **loud** — `ENOENT` arrives as `error` and `nonCompletion` reports INCONCLUSIVE, which blocks — rather than the silent mis-scoring it replaces. Dropping the shell also removes an interpolation layer from every path this runner passes.
- **WHY THIS MATTERED EVEN THOUGH NO VICTIM CURRENTLY EMITS 1 MiB — AND THE INHERITED FIGURE WAS WRONG.** REG-F-168 recorded the mitigation from the audit as *"no victim file contains a `console.*` call and the largest is 43 KB"*. **I measured it myself rather than restate it, and half of it is off.** THE SEARCH: the 70 distinct `expectRed` paths were derived from the ledger and every one read from disk — **70 of 70 readable**, which independently re-confirms REG-F-162's victim-existence check — then matched against `/\bconsole\.(log|info|warn|error|debug)\s*\(/`. RESULT: **0 of 70 contain a `console.*` call**, and the largest victim is **81.7 KB** (`execrem-wp16-enforcement-observed.test.ts`), **not 43 KB**. **POSITIVE CONTROL:** the same regex over `scripts/mutants/run.ts` returns TRUE, so the search discriminates rather than being blind to everything. The mitigation HOLDS — 81.7 KB is still an order of magnitude under 1 MiB — but the number I was about to repeat was not mine and was not right. **But nothing guarded it, the threshold is one noisy suite away, and the failure is silent and in the WRONG direction** — a passing suite certified as a caught guard. A hole whose precondition is "someone adds logging" is not a hypothetical; it is a deadline.
- **~~⚠ NOT YET DRIVEN THROUGH THE RUNNER.~~ ✅ DRIVEN at `6642430c`, and the run EXITED 0.** **220 entries → 205 distinct measured**, every failure category empty — **SURVIVED 0, UNANCHORED 0, NO_COMPILE 0, KILLED_UNNAMED 0, ABORTED_DIRTY 0, INCONCLUSIVE 0** (DUPLICATE 10, RETIRED 5) — and **KILLED 193 · TYPE_PREVENTED 3 · CONTROL_HELD 9**.
- **⚠ THE KILLED COUNT IS NOT WHAT MAKES THAT EVIDENCE. IT IS THE PART A BROKEN SEAM WOULD ALSO PRODUCE.** A seam that reported EVERY child as failing yields exactly this kill arm — 193 of 193 KILLED, nothing surviving, a perfect-looking table — which is this programme’s own *a control that cannot fail* defect wearing a summary line. **What discriminates is the REQUIRED-GREEN population**, because two verdicts here are reachable ONLY through a child that PASSED: `gradeNamedVictim` returns INCONCLUSIVE unless the victim was observed GREEN *before* the mutation (REG-F-171), so **INCONCLUSIVE 0 across 193 kill-arm entries means every named victim was read as green through the new seam**; and `gradeControl` returns CONTROL_HELD only when `passed` is true, so **CONTROL_HELD 9 is nine runs read as PASSING**. Both reconcile to the leg table file-for-file: the ledger’s live entries name **70 distinct victims — 62 vitest + 8 `.e2e.` — and the run made exactly 62 `vitest victim BASELINE` and 8 `playwright BASELINE` calls**; of the 9 controls, **8 carry an empty `expectRed` and so run whole-suite — matching `vitest WHOLE-SUITE` 8 calls exactly** — while the ninth, `S3-CONTROL-e2e-victim-is-actually-run`, names an e2e victim and runs targeted through Playwright. **Seventy green reads and nine passing suites is the arm the old seam could not have produced**, and it is the same 70 this entry read from disk for the `console.*` search.
- **⚠ HOW KILLED AND TYPE_PREVENTED WERE RECOVERED, SINCE I DID NOT SEE THEM PRINTED.** The background task’s captured output was truncated to its last 30 lines, which begin at `RETIRED`; the two lines above it were lost. **They were DERIVED, by two routes that agree.** (a) ARITHMETIC: the surviving lines account for 9 of the 205, so `KILLED + TYPE_PREVENTED = 196`. (b) POPULATION: the ledger partitions the same 205 into **193 kill-arm + 3 `expectNoCompile` + 9 `expectSurvive`**, and TYPE_PREVENTED is reachable ONLY from an `expectNoCompile` entry — its branch dereferences that field — whose only alternative verdict is SURVIVED, measured 0. Both give **KILLED 193 / TYPE_PREVENTED 3**. Recorded this way because **a number I did not watch print is a number whose provenance has to travel with it.**
- **AND THE RUN SETTLED REG-F-175’S COST, read from the named legs rather than differenced (REG-F-174).** That entry’s single-mutant drive predicted **~+41 s over the six `.svelte` mutants**; the full run measures **`svelte-check apps/rph-demo` at 82.1 s / 6 calls** against **`tsc apps/rph-demo` at 112.9 s / 16 calls (avg 7.1 s)** — **~+39.5 s**, and the **6** and **16** are the two call counts REG-F-175 predicted for exactly the six files that moved. A prediction made from one mutant, confirmed at full scale.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/run.ts`. **Safe default:** **when a wrapper sits between you and your evidence, suspect the wrapper** — the buffer limit was the visible symptom and the shell was the cause, and the knob aimed at the symptom was inert precisely because it never reached the layer doing the damage.

### REG-F-177 — the compile leg re-typechecks a whole package to judge one line, and my first reading of what that costs was 4x wrong because I timed it outside the harness
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** COST, and a MEASUREMENT-METHOD finding that outranks it · **Status:** ~~BUILT. The cost reading through the runner is OWED.~~ **BUILT, COSTED THROUGH THE RUNNER, AND ITS CONTROL DRIVEN WARM.** The full-run leg is owed at the next gate.
- **THE COST BEING ATTACKED, read from the legs of the `6642430c` run (REG-F-174's rule).** `compileVerdict` runs `tsc --noEmit -p <pkg>/tsconfig.json` once per mutant, re-checking the ENTIRE package from scratch to judge a **one-line** edit. `tsc packages/rph-application` alone is **314.6 s over 78 calls** — and 78 is exactly the number of live ledger entries in that package, so it is one full re-check each. Across all nine packages the `tsc` legs total **685.6 s over 199 calls, 25.9 % of the run's 2 649.7 s**. It is the largest single addressable block in the table.
- **THE CHANGE.** `--incremental --tsBuildInfoFile node_modules/.cache/jpwb-mutants/<pkg>.tsbuildinfo`, on the **runner's** `tsc` invocation only. **The product's own `check-types` stays a cold full check on purpose:** a speed knob that lives in the harness can be judged by the harness, and one that lives in `base.json` would silently become the gate every developer and every CI job trusts. `base.json` keeps `"incremental": false`.
- **⚠ AND HERE IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OPTIMISATION: MY FIRST COST READING WAS 4x WRONG, BECAUSE I TIMED THE OPERATION OUTSIDE THE HARNESS THAT PAYS FOR IT.** Run from my shell, the *identical* command — `bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/rph-application/tsconfig.json` — took **16.5 s, 16.1 s, 20.5 s** on three consecutive calls. Driven through the runner over three mutants in that same package, its own instrument reports **12.3 s over 3 calls, avg 4.1 s** — agreeing with the full run's 78-call average of **4.0 s** to within 2.5 %. **Fixed invocation overhead is not the explanation and was measured rather than assumed:** `bunx tsc --version` is **0.18 s**, `bun --version` **0.09 s**.
- **⚠ WHICH WAY THAT ERROR RAN IS THE DANGEROUS PART.** The outside reading was **four times too EXPENSIVE**, so it would have made a modest optimisation look like a large one — and the "saving" would then have been reported as a fraction of a per-call cost the harness never actually pays. **REG-F-174 said: do not cost an operation by differencing two totals. This says: do not cost it outside the run either.** They are one error with two faces — *a number produced by an instrument other than the one whose cost is in question* — and the safe default is that **only the harness's own `printTimings` leg is admissible as a cost for that harness.**
- **⚠ THE CONTROL IS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER, AND IT CAN FAIL.** The failure mode of an incremental cache is precise: a changed file goes UNCHECKED, which turns `compileVerdict` into a leg that cannot fail — this repository's most-repeated defect. **Three live entries declare `expectNoCompile`, one each in three different packages** — `B6-unresolvable-fails-open` (`packages/rph-application`), `V2C-T1 PlanLiveness is a closed union` (`packages/rph-domain`), `F119-the-accountability-gate-is-handed-a-derived-set` (`verif`) — and each reports **SURVIVED, which BLOCKS**, the moment its mutation compiles. A cache that skipped a changed file flips all three. **PREDICTED RED, to be driven before this is believed:** run an `expectNoCompile` mutant *behind* another mutant in the same package, so its cache is WARM rather than cold, and it must still report **TYPE_PREVENTED**. A cold-cache pass would prove nothing, because a cold cache is the state that already works.
- **WHY THE CACHE IS KEPT BETWEEN RUNS, AND WHY IT LIVES IN `node_modules/.cache`.** TypeScript records a per-file version derived from the **text**, plus the options and the compiler version, and discards the whole `.tsbuildinfo` when any of the three disagree — so a cache left by a different commit does not make a changed file go unchecked, it makes it re-checked. Deleting it per run would throw away the cold-start cost on the first mutant of every package and buy no soundness. `node_modules/.cache` is gitignored by construction and destroyed by `bun install`, which is the right invalidation; **it also keeps the file out of the tree `treeIsClean` judges**, so the harness's cleanliness check does not come to depend on `git status --untracked-files=no` continuing to hide it.
- **~~⚠ NOT YET COSTED THROUGH THE RUNNER.~~ ✅ COSTED, with the runner’s own instrument, over four `packages/rph-application` mutants driven twice.** Every figure below is a `printTimings` leg, and the BEFORE arm is two independent readings of the same thing that agree:

  | arm | leg | calls | avg |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | BEFORE — full run `6642430c` | 314.6 s | 78 | **4.0 s** |
  | BEFORE — three mutants, driven today | 12.3 s | 3 | **4.1 s** |
  | AFTER — first run, cold cache included | 14.5 s | 4 | 3.6 s |
  | AFTER — second run, fully warm | 9.3 s | 4 | **2.3 s** |

  **Warm, the call costs 2.3 s against the 4.0 s the full run actually paid — about 43 % less.**
- **AND THE COLD CALL GOT DEARER, WHICH IS THE PART AN AVERAGE WOULD HAVE HIDDEN.** The two AFTER runs differ only in cache state, so their difference is the cold call’s surcharge: **14.5 − 9.3 = 5.2 s**, putting a cold incremental call at **~7.5 s against the old 4.0 s**. It is paid once per package per cache lifetime, and because the `.tsbuildinfo` is deliberately KEPT between runs it is paid **once ever** — until `bun install` clears `node_modules/.cache`, which is the invalidation this wants. A per-package cache that was cleared each run would have made the harness SLOWER on any package holding few mutants.
- **✅ THE PREDICTED-RED CONTROL WAS DRIVEN WARM, AND IT HELD.** The entry demanded an `expectNoCompile` mutant run BEHIND another in the same package, because a cold-cache pass proves nothing. `B6-unresolvable-fails-open` ran **fourth**, after three mutants in the same package **and in different files** — they mutate `handlers/pwu.ts` and its neighbours, it mutates `handlers/execution.ts` — so its cache was warm from other files when its own file changed. It reported **TYPE_PREVENTED**, with **NO_COMPILE 0 and SURVIVED 0** and the other three **KILLED**. That is the exact shape of the failure this control exists to catch: a warm cache letting a changed file go unchecked would have compiled, and compiling is SURVIVED, which blocks.
- **~~⚠ AND NO LEG TOTAL IS QUOTED HERE, DELIBERATELY.~~ ✅ THE FULL GATE HAS NOW MEASURED IT, AND THE PREDICTION LANDED ON THE NOSE.** The projection this entry refused to assert was ~190 s; the run at `8420c5e7` measures `tsc packages/rph-application` at **175.8 s over the same 78 calls — avg 2.3 s**, which is **exactly the per-call figure the 4-call sample predicted.** Every `tsc` leg, at identical call counts:

  | leg | calls | before | after | per call |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---|
  | `tsc packages/rph-application` | 78 | 314.6 s | **175.8 s** | 4.0 → **2.3** |
  | `tsc packages/rph-domain` | 64 | 166.4 s | **110.3 s** | 2.6 → **1.7** |
  | `tsc apps/rph-demo` | 16 | 112.9 s | **59.1 s** | 7.1 → **3.7** |
  | `tsc verif` | 16 | 34.8 s | 28.5 s | 2.2 → 1.8 |
  | `tsc packages/rph-projections` | 14 | 25.8 s | 21.4 s | 1.8 → 1.5 |
  | `tsc scripts` | 5 | 19.0 s | 10.1 s | 3.8 → 2.0 |
  | `tsc packages/rph-engine` | 3 | 5.8 s | 5.4 s | 1.9 → 1.8 |
  | `tsc packages/rph-contracts` | 1 | 3.5 s | 3.5 s | unchanged — one call is a COLD call |
  | `tsc packages/rph-product-realization-pwa` | 2 | 2.8 s | 2.8 s | 1.4 → 1.4 |

  **685.6 s → 416.9 s across the nine `tsc` legs**, and the NEXT run — `3ccbbc22`, with the `.tsbuildinfo` files surviving between runs exactly as this entry argued they should — takes `tsc packages/rph-application` down again to **151.2 s / 78 calls, avg 1.9 s**. The cold-start cost is now paid nowhere at all. And it answers this entry’s own open question: `apps/rph-demo` **does** benefit (7.1 → 3.7) — `svelte-kit sync` rewriting the generated tsconfig did not discard the cache.
- **⚠ AND THIS IS A CROSS-RUN COMPARISON, WHICH THIS PROGRAMME HAS ALREADY BEEN BURNED BY — SO HERE IS WHY IT IS BELIEVABLE ANYWAY.** The same table shows `vitest BASELINE` falling **175.6 s → 64.2 s** on one call, for reasons that have nothing to do with this change; the two runs were plainly not in the same machine state. What carries the reading is not the difference of two totals (REG-F-174 forbids exactly that) but four independent things agreeing: **identical call counts leg-for-leg**, **nine legs all moving the same direction**, **the one leg with a single call — therefore always cold — not moving at all**, and **a per-call figure predicted from 4 calls reproducing at 78.** Any one of those alone would be weak.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `scripts/mutants/run.ts`. **Safe default:** **time an operation with the instrument that pays for it.** An outside stopwatch and an inside leg disagreed by 4x on the same command, and the outside one was the flattering direction.

### REG-F-178 — batching the e2e baselines was carried on an impossible premise, and measuring it correctly is what showed the change should be DECLINED
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A PLANNED OPTIMISATION, MEASURED AND REFUSED · **Status:** DECLINED, with the numbers recorded so it is not re-proposed from the same premise. **No code changed.**
- **THE INHERITED PREMISE WAS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, AND NOBODY HAD CHECKED IT.** The plan item read: *"batch the 8 e2e baselines into ONE Playwright invocation — the `playwright BASELINE` leg 130–138 s would fall to ~70 s; the ~16 s boot dominates and would be paid once."* The `6642430c` leg measures that arm at **117.5 s over 8 calls, avg 14.7 s per call** — so the claimed **fixed** cost of 16 s is LARGER than the entire per-call cost it is supposed to be part of. **A component cannot exceed its total.** The figure was inherited, restated twice in planning, and refuted by one line of the leg table.
- **THE REAL SPLIT, MEASURED.** Eight separate invocations cost **117.5 s** (the harness's own leg); the same eight specs in **ONE** invocation cost **60.3 s**. The difference is seven avoided server boots: **57.2 s, so a boot is ~8.2 s and the spec work itself ~6.5 s.** The inherited boot figure was about **double** the truth, and the achievable saving is **57.2 s — 2.2 % of the 2 649.7 s run**, not the ~60 s-of-130 s the plan implied.
- **⚠ THE OUTSIDE INSTRUMENT WAS CALIBRATED BEFORE IT WAS MIXED WITH THE INSIDE ONE.** Comparing a shell reading (60.3 s) against a harness leg (117.5 s) is exactly the error REG-F-177 recorded — unless the two are first shown to agree **for this command**. They were: the identical single-spec command run from the shell reads **13.7 s and 20.0 s**, straddling the harness leg's 14.7 s average. **For `bunx tsc` they did NOT agree — 16–20 s against the harness's 4.0 s — so the calibration is not a formality**, it is the step that decides whether the second number may be believed at all.
- **⚠ AND IT IS DECLINED, BECAUSE THE PER-VICTIM BASELINE HAS A SECOND PROPERTY NOBODY IS PAYING FOR AND BATCHING WOULD SPEND.** A baseline exists to make a KILLED **attributable**: the victim was GREEN, then the mutation made it RED (REG-F-171). Today that green is measured **in the same execution mode the mutated run uses** — one spec, its own server boot, its own fresh engine, because `playwright.config.ts` sets `workers: 1` and `reuseExistingServer: false`. A batched baseline instead certifies *"green while sharing a boot with seven other specs"*, while the mutated run stays alone — **so a KILLED would rest on a premise measured under different conditions than the fact it is attributing.**
- **⚠ AND THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS THE QUIET ONE (REG-F-110).** A spec that drifts into order-dependence is caught **today** — red when run alone, so its baseline is red, so `gradeNamedVictim` reports INCONCLUSIVE and BLOCKS. Under batching it would be green-in-batch, red-alone, and scored **KILLED**: a guard credited for a kill it never made. **Note the empirical status honestly — all eight ARE green alone today**, which is precisely what the `6642430c` run's **INCONCLUSIVE 0** says. So this is not a present defect. It is the removal of a check that currently passes, **which is how most of the guards in this ledger died.**
- **WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER, so the next reader need not re-derive it.** If the e2e victim count grows enough for this leg to dominate, the symmetry can be bought back with batch-then-confirm — batch for the baseline, then re-run individually any victim a KILLED is about to rest on. But that confirmation is owed for **every killed e2e mutant**, which is most of them, so it recovers little of the 57.2 s. The cheaper wins are elsewhere and do not touch the attribution arm: REG-F-177's compile-leg change is measured at 43 % off a leg **2.7x larger** than this one.
- **Merge target:** none — this entry IS the artifact. **Safe default:** **a measurement taken for ATTRIBUTION must be taken in the same mode as the thing it attributes**; and before mixing an outside reading with a harness leg, calibrate the outside one against a known leg, because for one of the two commands checked today it disagreed by 4x.

### REG-F-179 — the filed remedy said seven, the derivation said eight, and the authority for the right spelling was already in the vocab
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** REG-F-167'S FILED REPAIR, VERIFIED THEN PERFORMED · **Status:** REPAIRED and GATED. The enumeration REG-F-167 pinned is replaced by a closed predicate, not updated.
- **THE FILED REMEDY WAS A HYPOTHESIS, AND CHECKING IT FIRST IS WHAT FOUND THE EIGHTH.** REG-F-167 filed *"seven aggregates are spelled two ways, splitting 54 commands"* — and re-derived at HEAD that is exactly right: **7 split groups, 54 commands**. But *"spelled two ways"* is a property of a COINCIDENCE — that a stray spelling happens to have a canonical twin. Deriving the population a different way returns **8 spellings over 24 declarations**: `DecompositionContract` ×3 has **no** SCREAMING_SNAKE counterpart, so it is invisible to a dual-spelling test while being the identical defect, one new command away from joining the list. **Said 7, was 8** — the same shape as every other hand-listed population in this register.
- **AND THE CANONICAL SPELLING WAS NEVER MINE TO CHOOSE.** `canonicalEnums[0]` in `canonical-vocabulary.json` is **`ProfessionalWorkObjectType`**, and its own `appliesTo` reads *"ObjectEnvelope.objectType (all Professional Work Objects)"* — 23 SCREAMING_SNAKE values. A `targetAggregateType` names one of those, so the question is **membership**, not house style. **MEASURED BEFORE THE REPAIR: 22 of 30 spellings (77 declarations) were members; 8 spellings (24 declarations) were not, and every one mapped letter-for-letter onto exactly one member.** The repair script derives that mapping **from the enum** rather than listing eight renames — a hand-typed mapping would have been a second copy of a derivable value inside the fix for a defect caused by an unchecked copy.
- **⚠ PREDICTED RED, NAMED BEFORE IT WAS RUN, AND IT NAMED THE RIGHT TWENTY-FOUR.** The gate was written and driven BEFORE the vocab was touched: it failed listing **24 commands** — `AbandonPwu -> ProfessionalWorkUnit`, `ProposeDecomposition -> DecompositionContract`, and 22 more — which is precisely the population the derivation predicted, command for command. The other five assertions in that file passed throughout, so the red is attributable to the new predicate rather than to the edit.
- **THE PIN WAS REPLACED, NOT UPDATED, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** REG-F-167's pin listed the seven groups with counts; keeping it would have meant re-typing seven literals to say "now zero". The replacement asserts **no command declares a `targetAggregateType` outside `ProfessionalWorkObjectType`** — one assertion, no literal to keep current, and it **strictly subsumes** what it replaces: enum members are distinct SCREAMING_SNAKE names, so no two can normalise alike, so membership forbids dual spelling as a corollary. **A closed predicate beats an open enumeration**, and here the enumeration was demonstrably one short.
- **⚠ WITH A CONTROL THAT CAN FAIL, BECAUSE AN EMPTY STRAY LIST IS ALSO WHAT A BROKEN READER RETURNS.** The control asserts three separate things: the registry is real (>100 declarations), the enum **ACCEPTS** `PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT`, and the enum **REJECTS** `ProfessionalWorkUnit`. The third is the load-bearing one — without it, a `members` set built from the wrong source, or from everything, would pass the main assertion silently.
- **THE REGENERATION WAS REVIEWED ON ITS OWN TERMS, AND THE REVIEW WAS CHEAP BECAUSE THE GENERATOR WAS PROVED TO BE AT A FIXED POINT FIRST.** `bun run gen` on the CLEAN tree produced **zero diff**, so every line of the subsequent generated diff is attributable to the 24 vocab edits. It is: `messages.ts` changed **50 diff lines, of which the number that are not a `targetAggregateType` line is ZERO** — counted, not eyeballed. `schemas/`, `enums.ts` and `objects.ts` did not move.
- **⚠ AND THAT CORRECTS AN INHERITED PLANNING PREMISE THAT WOULD HAVE DETERRED THIS REPAIR.** A standing plan note held that *"committed generated files are stale vs their generators (pre-existing drift); `bun run gen` produces a large unrelated diff"*, and REG-F-167 deferred the repair partly on that basis — *"a regeneration with a large diff"*. **At this HEAD it is false, measured: zero.** The deferral was reasonable when written and simply stopped being true; what makes it worth recording is that a premise about how expensive a change is can silently outlive the condition that made it expensive.
- **AFTER: 101 declarations over 23 distinct spellings — every one of the enum's 23 values is now used by at least one command**, and the repair script asserts that post-condition itself rather than leaving it to the gate to discover.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `packages/rph-contracts/vocab/m3-commands-events.json` (24 lines), `packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts` (generated), `verif/observation-command-surface.test.ts`. **Safe default:** **when a defect is filed as a list of exceptions, ask what PREDICATE the list is an instance of** — the predicate was already written down as an enum, and the list was one short.

- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** RETIREMENT-PRECONDITION AUDIT, PARTIAL AND SAYING WHICH PART · **Status:** RECORDED. Precondition 3 NOT discharged and carrying a design conflict; precondition 4 NOT discharged; **preconditions 1 and 2 NOT AUDITED HERE, and this entry claims nothing about them.**
- **⚠ READ THIS ENTRY WITH REG-F-184 BESIDE IT: THE ACT THESE PRECONDITIONS GATE WAS REVERSED BY THE SPONSOR SIX DAYS BEFORE I AUDITED THEM.** REG-D-034 (2026-08-09) abandoned the wholesale retirement and admitted the source corpora as SOURCE OF RECORD. **The questions below outlive the act and are worth answering; the obligation does not bind.** Everything measured here stands; only the framing — *"held until retirement"* — is stale.
- **WHY THIS WAS CHECKED AT ALL.** Ratify Sheet R1 was executed wholesale (REG-D-010, 2026-07-24) and its one outstanding item is **Part 4 — the retirement decision**, held behind four preconditions. Approving retirement is a sponsor act and is not mine. **Verifying whether the four preconditions HOLD is not a sponsor act, and it had never been done** — so the sheet has been waiting on a question nobody had answered rather than on a judgment only the sponsor can make.
- **⚠ PRECONDITION 3 (REG-E-020) IS NOT DISCHARGED, AND WHAT LOOKS LIKE ITS DISCHARGE IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT.** REG-E-020 cedes the numeric floors — **100 % guard-logic / 90 % projection / risk-based UI** — to repository gate configuration, warning *"confirm they are encoded there before retirement, or the numbers are lost."* The repository DOES encode coverage numbers: `vitest.config.ts:166`, **statements 95 / branches 83 / functions 96.5 / lines 97**. But those are **global**, not per-concern, and they are derived from **MEASUREMENT** — the V-2c ratchet, set from measured merged figures and rounded down — not from REG-E-020's floors. **A global 95 % does not entail 100 % on guard logic.** The two instruments answer different questions, and only one of them is the one the precondition names.
- **⚠ AND IT IS WORSE THAN AN OMISSION: THE REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY DECIDED AGAINST THE FORM THOSE FLOORS REQUIRE, WITHOUT REFERENCE TO THEM.** A per-concern floor needs per-file or per-area thresholds, and `vitest.config.ts` rejects `perFile` **explicitly**, with its reason recorded: it *"would fail on day one — `sqlite-storage-adapter.ts` sits at 62 % because most of it is error paths behind a driver this suite fakes — and a day-one failure is a day-one disablement."* **That rationale is sound, and it is in direct tension with REG-E-020.** So discharging precondition 3 is not a matter of typing two numbers into a config: it is choosing between a ratified floor and a ratchet whose own argument predicts the floor will be switched off. **Recorded as the open decision it is, rather than settled by whichever side was nearer to hand.**
- **THE MUTATION HALF IS DIFFERENT, AND MUST NOT BE READ AS WEAKER OR AS EQUIVALENT.** REG-E-020 also cedes a *"mutation floor"*, and **no numeric mutation percentage is encoded anywhere**. What is encoded is categorical and, on its own population, stronger: `scripts/mutants/run.ts` fails the build on **ABORTED_DIRTY, SURVIVED, UNANCHORED, NO_COMPILE, INCONCLUSIVE or KILLED_UNNAMED** — a **100 % kill requirement over the 205 declared mutants**. ⚠ But that population is **AUTHORED, not generated**: it is a stronger claim about a smaller set. A reader who sees "no mutation percentage" and files a gap is wrong; a reader who sees "0 survivors" and reads it as a 100 % mutation score over generated mutants is **also** wrong. ### REG-F-181 — minting `RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`: the category is derivable from two precedents, and the predicted red had to be manufactured because nothing asserts the code
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A FILED CONTRACT CHANGE, DESIGNED WITH ITS PREDICTED RED NAMED FIRST · **Status:** ~~DESIGNED.~~ **BUILT AND DRIVEN.** All three couplings were observed FIRING, and the manufactured red went red before it went green.
- **WHAT IS BLOCKED, AND FOR HOW LONG.** `command-bus.ts:411-438` refuses an idempotency-key reuse with `RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED` and carries `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` in the message. The comment there records why: minting `RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` was believed to be **a sponsor act**. **REG-D-027/REG-F-057 settled on 2026-08-07 that it is not** — minting is a repository shape change through the contract procedure, since REG-D-004 makes the repository authoritative for *"error codes"* by name and DOC-004 §5 routes enum extension through that procedure. REG-F-144/148 recorded that the correction reached `errors.ts` **and never reached this consumer.** The workaround has stood on removed ground for eight days.
- **⚠ THE CATEGORY IS NOT MINE TO CHOOSE EITHER, AND TWO INDEPENDENT PRECEDENTS AGREE.** `ERROR_CODE_CATEGORY` already maps **`RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_DUPLICATE: 'CONCURRENCY'`** — the sibling code for the same domain concept — and **`RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT: 'CONCURRENCY'`**, the only other `*_CONFLICT` code in the set. Same concept and same suffix, independently, both CONCURRENCY. **So `RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` is CONCURRENCY by derivation, not by taste** — the same move REG-F-179 made against the object-type enum.
- **⚠ AND THAT MOVES THE CATEGORY THIS REFUSAL REPORTS, FROM VALIDATION TO CONCURRENCY — DISCLOSED, NOT DISCOVERED.** `makeRphError` derives `category` from the map, so anything routing on category sees this refusal change buckets. It is the correct move — the current bucket is an artifact of a **borrowed** code rather than a judgment about the condition — but it is a behaviour change and is named here rather than found later.
- **⚠ THE MECHANISM, CORRECTED BEFORE IT SHIPPED — MY FIRST DRAFT OF THIS BULLET DESCRIBED A GENERATOR THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** It said the path was *"`vocab` → `bun run gen` → `enums.ts` + `schemas/`"*. **`errors.ts` IS HAND-WRITTEN**, and `grep -rn "errorCodes" packages/rph-contracts/src/gen/*.ts` returns **nothing** — no generator reads that vocab list at all. The real chain has **three** couplings, each already enforced by something that fails:

  1. **vocab ↔ enum, by TEST.** `errors.test.ts:22` — *"exposes exactly the RPH_\* error codes the vocabulary declares — no more, no fewer"* — reads `canonical-vocabulary.json` directly and filters `RPH_*`. **Adding the code to either side alone reddens it.**
  2. **enum ↔ category, by COMPILER.** `ERROR_CODE_CATEGORY` is `Readonly<Record<RphErrorCode, RphErrorCategory>>` — **TOTAL** over the enum — so a new member without a category **does not compile**; `errors.test.ts:27` then checks the value is a real category.
  3. **Zod ↔ committed schema, by DRIFT TEST.** The codes DO reach the emitted artifacts — `schemas/objects/RphError.json` and `schemas/objects/CommandResult.json` both contain them — and `json-schema.test.ts` asserts every committed schema is undrifted from its Zod source, with a plausible-count control and a stale-file check beside it. **So `bun run gen` IS still required**, for the emission step rather than for `errors.ts`.

  **This corrects my own draft, not the register’s:** REG-F-144’s description of the `RPH_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` precedent — *"vocabulary, enum, total category map, regenerated schemas, with the JSON-schema drift test enforcing the coupling"* — **is accurate in every limb**; I paraphrased it into a generator step it never claimed. Checked because a remedy recorded by someone else is a hypothesis — and so, it turns out, is one recorded by me an hour earlier.
- **⚠ AND THE PREDICTED RED HAD TO BE MANUFACTURED FOR THE *REFUSAL* HALF — the three couplings above cover the CONTRACT half and nothing covers this one.** `idempotency-key-reuse.test.ts` asserts the **MESSAGE** — `toContain('IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED')` at four sites — and **nothing anywhere asserts this refusal's CODE**. So minting the code while keeping the label would leave the entire suite green: **a contract change no test could notice.** The increment therefore adds the code assertion FIRST and drives it RED before the vocab is touched, as REG-F-179 did. A green that was never at risk is not evidence.
- **THE MESSAGE LABEL IS RETAINED, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN INERTIA.** Once the code exists the label duplicates it. It stays because it is human-facing prose emitted from the same refusal (no drift surface between them), four assertions and any operator grep depend on it, and **removing it is a separable call that would otherwise ride in on a mint.** Recorded so that its removal is a decision someone takes rather than a tidy-up someone performs.
- **A DISCREPANCY CHECKED AND DISSOLVED, recorded because the checking is the point.** The vocab lists **17** `errorCodes` while the emitted enum has **16**. The extra is `VALIDATOR_FAILED`, and `errors.ts:3` already says it *"is intentionally NOT an RphError code"* — DOC-004 §34.1 makes it a validator **execution** failure and a state-machine state, not an assurance rejection. **Already adjudicated at the source; no finding.** Noted so the next reader who counts does not re-open it.
- **✅ DRIVEN, AND EACH OF THE FOUR CHECKS WAS WATCHED FAILING BEFORE IT PASSED — which is the only reason any of them is evidence.**
  1. **The manufactured red (REFUSAL half).** The code assertion was added FIRST and run: *"expected 'RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED' to be 'RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT'"*, **1 failed / 10 passed**. The ten that passed are the message assertions — exactly the suite that would have stayed green through this whole change.
  2. **vocab ↔ enum, by TEST.** Adding the vocab entry alone leaves `errors.test.ts:22` unsatisfied by construction; both sides now agree at **17 `RPH_*` codes** (18 `errorCodes` entries, `VALIDATOR_FAILED` still correctly excluded).
  3. **enum ↔ category, by COMPILER — observed, not assumed.** With the member added and the map untouched, `tsc` refused: *"error TS2741: Property 'RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT' is missing in type … but required in type `Readonly<Record<…>>`"*. **A half-done mint does not compile.**
  4. **Zod ↔ committed schema, by DRIFT TEST.** `bun run gen` moved **`schemas/objects/RphError.json`** and **`schemas/objects/CommandResult.json`** by three lines each, and `json-schema.test.ts` passes against them.
- **THE DIFF IS THE SIZE THE ARGUMENT SAYS IT SHOULD BE:** vocab **+5**, `errors.ts` **+27**, `command-bus.ts` **+15**, the test **+16**, two generated schemas **+3 each**. ⚠ And the vocab file is **CRLF while its sibling `m3-commands-events.json` is LF** — measured (2 770 CRLF / 0 bare LF against 0 / 8 320) before writing, because writing LF into it would have turned a five-line insertion into a 2 770-line diff.
- **GATES:** `check-types` 22/22 (svelte-check 0 errors), lint clean, boundary 0 violations, build, `vitest` **310 of 311 files** — the one failure being the pre-existing CSAA `scripts/tsconfig` population pin — and Playwright **73 passed, 1 flaky**.
- **⚠ AND THE COLLATERAL NOBODY WOULD HAVE CAUGHT WAS CHECKED BY HAND, BECAUSE NOTHING CHECKS IT.** `EnforcementDisposition.declaredMutations` holds **107 prose mutation instructions across 31 rows**, and REG-F-134 established that this field is validated for **LENGTH ONLY** — a string naming a function that was never written survives every gate. So an instruction reading *"swap the guard’s refusal code to `RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED`"* would go stale **silently** if this mint had landed on its guard. **Three rows name that code** — `RPH-EVD-002` (`recordClaimAssessment`), `RPH-EVD-007` (`admitEvidence`, where the point is that `loadOrReject` refuses with the SAME code and masks a code-only probe) and `RPH-INT-003` (`approveIntent`’s FROM_STATES arm) — and **none of them is the idempotency guard**, so all three instructions remain performable exactly as written. **Checked rather than assumed, and recorded rather than left as a silence**, because the next mint against one of those three guards WILL invalidate a declared mutation and the register will not say so.
- **AND REG-F-151’S RATIO WAS RE-DERIVED WHILE I WAS IN THERE, because a decision resting on a ratio is only as good as the ratio still being true.** That entry declined to build a `mutantId` gate on the measured ground that it would watch **1 row of 107**. Re-derived at this head: **112 register rows, 31 carrying `declaredMutations`, 107 strings, exactly ONE resolving to a ledger id** — unchanged. **The item stays closed**; it was on my working list as *"the additive `mutantId` migration"*, which reads like a task, and REG-F-151’s actual disposition is *"nothing built, deliberately"* with the additive field named only as what a FUTURE attempt should do incidentally. Re-listing a settled decision as pending work is how a deliberate refusal quietly becomes a backlog item.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `packages/rph-contracts/vocab/canonical-vocabulary.json`, `packages/rph-contracts/src/errors.ts` (category map + the AUTHORED disclosure), `packages/rph-application/src/command-bus.ts`, a new code assertion in `idempotency-key-reuse.test.ts`, regenerated `enums.ts`/`schemas/`. **Safe default:** **a correction recorded at the source is not a correction delivered** — REG-F-144 found this workaround still standing on ground removed a week earlier, and it takes a second entry to actually remove it.

### REG-F-182 — the gate BLOCKED on an INCONCLUSIVE that re-drove to KILLED, and the artifact that would have explained it was destroyed by the run I used to look for it
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A BLOCKING VERDICT, RESOLVED WITHOUT EDITING THE ORACLE · **Status:** the mutant is **KILLED**; the gate is **GREEN at `3ccbbc22`**; and the contention hypothesis this entry declined to assert is now **SUPPORTED** by a third run — see the last bullet.
- **WHAT THE GATE SAID.** The full run at `8420c5e7` reported **INCONCLUSIVE 1** and **BLOCKED** (exit 1). The entry is `B3-rejection-stops-checking-the-subject`, victim `apps/rph-demo/e2e/pwu-rejection.e2e.ts`, detail *"the run TIMED OUT (Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded)"*. Re-driven **alone on an idle machine it reports KILLED**. So the mutation is caught, and the run that failed to say so **did not measure it** — which is precisely what INCONCLUSIVE means and why REG-F-116/169 made a timeout refuse a verdict rather than manufacture one. **The harness behaved correctly; that is not in question here.**
- **⚠ A NOTE ON THE EXIT CODE, BECAUSE I NEARLY REPORTED THIS AS A PASS.** The run was launched as `bun run mutants 2>&1 | tail -60`, and the task notification reported **"exit code 0"** — which is `tail`'s status, not the runner's. The runner's own last line reads `error: script "mutants" exited with code 1`. **A pipeline reports the exit code of its LAST stage**, and a gate observed through a pipe is a gate whose verdict you are not reading.
- **⚠ MY FIRST EXPLANATION WAS CONTENTION, AND THE LEG TABLE DOES NOT SUPPORT IT.** I ran read-only analysis — `bun -e` over the ledger, python, git, greps — throughout that 40-minute run, so load was the obvious suspect, and the mutated `playwright` leg did rise **28.5 s → 33.8 s**. But checking the rest of the table refutes the simple story: `vitest BASELINE` **fell** 175.6 → 64.2 and `playwright BASELINE` **fell** 14.7 → 13.9, while `vitest targeted` (2.9 → 3.1) and `vitest WHOLE-SUITE` (54.7 → 58.3) rose slightly. **Legs moved in both directions.** Worse, the rise I wanted to cite as evidence is partly *caused by the event it was meant to explain*: a timed-out Playwright test burns its full 30 s ceiling and then **retries**, so one timeout inflates that leg's average by itself. **Circular.** So: my concurrent activity is a plausible contributor and is **not established**, and this entry does not claim it.
- **⚠ AND THE SAME TEST FLAKED WITH THE MACHINE IDLE, WHICH IS THE PART NOTHING EXPLAINS.** In the clean e2e gate earlier at this head, `pwu-rejection.e2e.ts:129` — **the CONTROL** — was reported **flaky** (green on retry) with nothing else running. Two occurrences, two different conditions.
- **⚠ AND I DESTROYED THE EVIDENCE LOOKING FOR IT — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` had written a trace for that flake. **A Playwright run clears `outputDir` at start**, so the next thing I ran deleted it. I did not take that on trust: I planted `PROBE-does-a-run-clear-this.txt` in `e2e-results/artifacts/`, ran one unrelated spec, and **the probe was gone**. The rule it teaches is **capture the trace before running anything else**, and it is now the first step if this recurs.
- **REPRODUCTION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED — RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE RESULT, NOT AS A CLEARANCE.** The spec alone: **2 tests, 16.3 s, both green**, so neither test is anywhere near its 30 s ceiling when idle. The full suite re-run at this head: **74 passed, 0 flaky, 4.2 m**. One clean pass is one sample of a rare event, and calling that "fixed" is the shape this register has recorded too often to repeat.
- **⚠ AND THE NEXT RUN FLAKED IN A DIFFERENT SPEC ENTIRELY, WHICH SETTLES THE QUESTION THIS ENTRY WAS CIRCLING.** A later full e2e gate at this head reported **73 passed, 1 flaky** — `pwu-lifecycle.e2e.ts:17`, **not** the rejection control. So across three full e2e runs today the flake moved: `pwu-rejection` once, none once, `pwu-lifecycle` once. **A defect in one control does not migrate between specs.** That is evidence for a timing property of the harness and against the reading that the control I declined to edit is itself broken — and it arrived AFTER the decision not to edit it, which is the order that makes it worth anything.
- **⚠ AND A THIRD SUITE DID THE SAME THING, IN A DIFFERENT TOOL.** In one `bun run test` run, `csaa/src/semantic/build-static-semantic-snapshot.test.ts` — *"refuses replay drift and downstream normalization or validation disagreement"*, a 35 s test — **failed**; run alone it is **29 passed**, and the very next full run was green. So today produced **three** load-sensitive failures across **two** independent expensive suites (Playwright, CSAA), none reproducible in isolation. **This bears directly on the mutation gate, which drives those suites 200+ times per run**, and it is the reason a single INCONCLUSIVE is now expected rather than surprising.
- **⚠ THE ORACLE IS NOT BEING EDITED ON A SUSPICION, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DISCIPLINE HERE.** `pwu-rejection.e2e.ts:129` is a **CONTROL**, and its own comments record **three prior rounds** in which it passed for the wrong reason and `B3-…` SURVIVED against it. DOC-004 §7.6's oracle rule — *"the oracle stream is never edited to make the implementation stream pass"* — binds hardest exactly here: from the outside, adding a wait to "settle the flake" is indistinguishable from weakening the fourth version of a control that has already been weakened three times. **A green bought with an oracle's credibility costs more than the red.**
- **WHAT IS OWED, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE RUNNER'S MESSAGE SUGGESTS.** The runner prints *"Fix the slow test; do not raise the timeout"*, which presumes slowness; the measurement says the whole spec is **16.3 s for two tests** idle. So the owed work is **diagnosis from a trace**, triggered by the next occurrence. ⚠ And the harness cannot help with this one: a Playwright timeout writes **no vitest JSON report**, so `MUTANTS_HARVEST=1` — the runner's own advice in that very message — **cannot recover it.** That advice is sound for a vitest victim and inapplicable to a Playwright one, and the message does not distinguish them.
- **✅ A THIRD RUN SETTLES IT, AND IT REVERSES THE CAUTION ABOVE — THE CONFOUNDER WAS A COLD CACHE.** The gate at `3ccbbc22`, run with **nothing else executing** and NOT through a pipe, is **GREEN: 205 distinct, KILLED 193 · TYPE_PREVENTED 3 · CONTROL_HELD 9, and 0 in every failure category including INCONCLUSIVE**, exit 0 from the runner itself. That gives three runs to compare, and the comparison I made earlier used the wrong pair:

  | leg (avg per call) | **A** `6642430c` — COLD, idle | **B** `8420c5e7` — warm, **BUSY** | **C** `3ccbbc22` — warm, **IDLE** |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | `playwright` | 28.5 s | 33.8 s | **26.8 s** |
  | `vitest targeted` | 2.9 s | 3.1 s | **2.8 s** |
  | `vitest WHOLE-SUITE` | 54.7 s | 58.3 s | **52.8 s** |
  | `vitest victim BASELINE` | 2.9 s | 3.0 s | **2.7 s** |
  | `playwright BASELINE` | 14.7 s | 13.9 s | **13.4 s** |
  | `svelte-check apps/rph-demo` | 13.7 s | 13.7 s | **13.1 s** |
  | `vitest BASELINE` (1 call) | **175.6 s** | 64.2 s | 60.6 s |

  **A is the cold-cache run** — its single-call `vitest BASELINE` leg is 175.6 s against ~62 s in both later runs, which is the confounder wearing a label. So **A vs B was never the controlled comparison; B vs C is** — both warm, differing in one increment and in whether I was running anything alongside. **C is faster than B on every one of the seven legs**, `playwright BASELINE` included, which was the very leg I cited as counter-evidence. **The contention reading is therefore supported**, and my earlier refusal to assert it was right for the evidence I had and wrong about the world.
- **⚠ WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW, STATED SO THE CORRECTION IS NOT OVER-READ.** Uniformly slower legs make contention a plausible CAUSE of the timeout; they do not make it the proven one, and they explain nothing about the two e2e flakes that happened with the machine idle or the CSAA suite that failed once and passed twice. **The operating rule stands on the weaker claim, which is enough:** do not run anything alongside the mutation gate. It cost a 40-minute run and a BLOCKING verdict to learn, and the harness cannot enforce it — `treeIsClean` guards a dirty TREE and says nothing about a busy MACHINE.
- **Merge target:** none — the ledger is unchanged and the verdict stands as KILLED on the isolated drive. **Safe default:** **when a verdict says the INSTRUMENT did not measure, re-drive it in isolation before touching anything it points at** — and read a gate's exit code from the gate, not through a pipe.

### REG-F-183 — retirement precondition 1 audited: NOTHING is missing from the seed, and my own first pass would have reported eleven items missing
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** RETIREMENT-PRECONDITION AUDIT (REG-F-180's precondition 1, now performed) · **Status:** **Every item REG-Q-045 names is CARRIED.** The precondition is not thereby discharged, and the reason is a distinction the word *"losslessly"* turns on — see the carriage table.
- **THE HOLD IS CHECKABLE, WHICH NOBODY HAD NOTICED.** Ratify Sheet Part 4's first precondition reads as a judgment call — *"carries their type hierarchy, policy catalog, profiles, and taxonomies losslessly"* — but **REG-Q-045 enumerates the populations with line references**: the seven-branch PWU Type hierarchy (RPH-DOC-003 L371-380), three conformance profiles with five selection criteria (L129-195), the Intent Discovery six-class epistemic taxonomy (L535-542), six validator-hunted failure modes (L548-555), the eight minimum scenario classes (L633-644), and RPH-DOC-004's twelve mandatory core policies. **That is ~~39~~ 58 named items over six populations, and each one either appears in the repository or does not.** ⚠ **The 39 was mine and it was wrong twice over — corrected the same day, from the source.** It omitted the three conformance profiles as entities *and* their selection criteria, while the table below counted the profiles in its numerator: **22 of 39 was 22 of 42 at best, and is 22 of 58 once the criteria are counted.** A denominator that excludes what the numerator includes is the arithmetic this register exists to catch, and it survived my own reading of the entry before commit.
- **⚠ AND MY FIRST PASS WOULD HAVE FILED ELEVEN FALSE ABSENCES.** I transcribed the four RPH-DOC-003 populations byte-exact from the source and searched **736 `.ts`/`.json`/`.svelte` files** under `packages/` and `apps/` for each phrase. Result: failure modes **3 of 6**, scenario classes **0 of 8** — eleven items apparently gone, with a working positive control (a fabricated phrase returned 0 carriers, a known one returned 5). **All eleven are present.** The repository carries them **ABBREVIATED**: *"omission of inconvenient constraints"* is stored as *"omitted constraints"*, *"conversion of preferences into requirements"* as *"preference-as-requirement"*, and all eight scenario classes appear as *"(normal, alternate valid, user-error, system-failure, permission-denied, interrupted/resumed, data-unavailable, cancellation)"* — the source's words shortened by the author who transcribed them. **An exact-phrase search over a paraphrasing corpus measures the paraphrase, not the content**, and the only thing that caught it was checking the absence in the other direction.
- **THE ACTUAL RESULT, AND THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS IS *HOW* EACH POPULATION IS CARRIED, NOT WHETHER:**

  | population | items | carried | carriage | gated by |
  |---|---:|---:|---|---|
  | PWU Type hierarchy | 7 | **7** | STRUCTURED — `pwuTemplates[].pwuKind` | `pwu-kind-vocabulary-census.test.ts` — *"the seeded root tree speaks the corpus vocabulary, name for name"* |
  | Twelve core policies | 12 | **12** | STRUCTURED — `seedPolicies` | `doc004-conformance.test.ts` — criteria text verbatim, finding codes in document order, evidence per §-heading |
  | Conformance profiles (as entities) | 3 | **3** | STRUCTURED — `conformanceProfiles` | `ontology.test.ts` — count + reference resolution |
  | **Profile selection criteria** | **16** | **16** | **PROSE** — semicolon-separated inside each profile’s `appliesToRisk` string | *nothing* |
  | Epistemic taxonomy | 6 | **6** | **PROSE** — one `purpose` sentence, verbatim | *nothing* |
  | Validator failure modes | 6 | **6** | **PROSE, ABBREVIATED** — inside a `sourceSection` **provenance** string | *nothing* |
  | Minimum scenario classes | 8 | **8** | **PROSE, ABBREVIATED** — inside one `completionClaims` string | *nothing* |

- **SO THE HONEST ANSWER TO THE PRECONDITION IS: THE CONTENT SURVIVED, AND MOST OF IT SURVIVED SOMEWHERE NOTHING CAN CHECK.** ~~22 of 39 items are structured and gated; 20 of 39 live inside four prose strings~~ — **22 of 58 are structured and gated; 36 of 58 live inside ~~SEVEN~~ **SIX** prose strings** (one `purpose`, one `sourceSection`, one `completionClaims` entry, and the three profiles’ `appliesToRisk`), and a single careless edit to any of them drops a ratified distinction with no test reddening. **Correcting the arithmetic made the finding bigger, not smaller: it is not half, it is nearly two thirds.** That is not a hypothetical failure mode in this repository — **it is REG-F-001, the hollow-seed finding, which is the very reason REG-Q-045 says carriage cannot be assumed.** The seed is no longer hollow; part of it is now *unenumerable*, which is the next shape along.
- **WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE IT. ⚠ CORRECTED — AS FIRST WRITTEN IT UNDER-COVERED THIS ENTRY’S OWN FINDING BY SIXTEEN ITEMS (REG-F-184).** It named `purpose`/`sourceSection`/`completionClaims`, **all three on `PwuTemplate`** — but the sixteen profile selection criteria live in `appliesToRisk`, which `ontology.types.ts:184-189` declares on **`ConformanceProfile`**, a different interface that edit cannot reach. **All FOUR prose carriers are in scope.** The policies show the pattern already: transcribe, then machine-check the transcription against the ratified text. Doing the same for the prose populations — lifting them into enumerable fields and pinning them against RPH-DOC-003 §4/§10/§12 the way `doc004-conformance.test.ts` pins §15-§26 — converts *"a reader can see the words are there"* into *"a test fails when they are not"*. **That is what the precondition is actually asking for**, and it is one increment, not a programme.
- **✅ THE PROFILE-CRITERIA CAVEAT IS NOW CLOSED, AND CLOSING IT FOUND AN OFF-BY-ONE IN REG-Q-045 ITSELF.** All three profiles were extracted from the source **by ANCHOR TEXT, never by line number** — this register forbids inferring a section from a line, and the extractor instead finds each `Appropriate for:` run and then CHECKS where it landed. Result: **Lightweight 5, Standard 5, High-Assurance 6 — sixteen, not fifteen.** REG-Q-045 describes the population as *"three conformance profiles with five selection criteria"*, which is right for two of the three. All sixteen are CARRIED, in the `appliesToRisk` prose (lightly abbreviated — *"database/API changes"* for *"database or API changes"*). ⚠ **That is the second hand-written population count this session to come up one short** (REG-F-179’s filed *"seven"* was eight), and both were found the same way: by deriving the population instead of reading its description.
- **⚠ WHAT THIS ENTRY STILL DOES NOT CLAIM.** The three RPH-DOC-003 populations were also extracted by anchor and their landing checked against the citations — the taxonomy anchor lands at **L535** (cited L535-542), the failure modes at **L548** (cited L548-555), the scenario classes at **L635** (cited L633-644) — so the citations hold. RPH-DOC-004's **per-policy semantics** are counted here and machine-checked by `doc004-conformance.test.ts`, not re-derived by me. And **precondition 2 — REG-D-008's shape-survivorship audit over six source documents — remains unaudited**, exactly as REG-F-180 said.
- **Merge target:** none yet — this entry is the audit; the remedy above is a repository increment awaiting its own. **Safe default:** **when a survivorship question asks "losslessly", ask WHERE the content landed, not just WHETHER** — content in a prose field is preserved from deletion and unprotected from erosion, and the difference is invisible to the search that finds it.

### REG-F-184 — the Ratify Sheet asks the sponsor to approve a retirement its own table records as REVERSED, and I audited its preconditions twice without noticing
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A GOVERNANCE CONTRADICTION INSIDE ONE DOCUMENT, plus the design it unblocks · **Status:** the contradiction is RECORDED and its remedy is the SPONSOR's (strike, do not delete); the design is GROUNDED and its predicted red already exists.
- **THE CONTRADICTION, IN ONE DOCUMENT, VERIFIED BY READING BOTH HALVES.** `JPWB Canon Ratify Sheet (R1).md` **line 139** still reads *"☐ **APPROVE RETIREMENT** of the pre-canon corpus (everything under `docs/` except `canon/`) to an archive outside the agent-visible tree"*. **Rows 22 and 29 of the same sheet** record the opposite: *"AMENDED 2026-08-09 (REG-D-034): REG-D-006's wholesale retirement REVERSED; retirement now applies only to individually named documents."* REG-D-034 is a **sponsor ruling given directly**, and its own words are *"abandon the retirement; keep the sources visible with a declared role"* — the corpora enter CON-000 B1's registry as **SOURCE OF RECORD**, authoritative for DETAIL. **The sheet asks for an approval its own clause-level table already reversed.**
- **⚠ AND I AUDITED ITS PRECONDITIONS TWICE THIS MORNING WITHOUT NOTICING.** REG-F-180 reported preconditions 3 and 4 *"NOT discharged"*; REG-F-183 audited precondition 1 in full. **Both were framed as gating a retirement abandoned six days earlier.** Worse: I derived REG-D-006's own status line — *"REVERSED AND SUPERSEDED BY REG-D-034"* — from this register **the same morning**, while scanning statuses, and did not connect it to the sheet I was auditing an hour later. **A fact read and a fact used are different things**, and this one lived in the gap.
- **WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS MOST OF IT.** The preconditions were conditions on an *archive move*; **the questions they ask outlive the act.** REG-Q-045 asks whether the repository carries the ontology content, and SOURCE OF RECORD status makes that **more** answerable, not less: the source stays readable, so a conformance test may read it **at runtime** — exactly what `doc004-conformance.test.ts` already does for the twelve policies. **What changes is the urgency claim.** REG-F-183's finding is no longer *"fix it before the source disappears"* but *"the source is operative and nothing checks the copy against it"* — a standing divergence rather than a deadline, and the second is the honest description.
- **⚠ THE THIRD ARITHMETIC SLIP IN THE SAME ENTRY, AND IT WAS INSIDE THE CORRECTION.** REG-F-183 now says *"36 of 58 live inside SEVEN prose strings"* and then enumerates **six**: one `purpose`, one `sourceSection`, one `completionClaims`, three `appliesToRisk`. Struck to SIX. **The first slip was a denominator that excluded what its numerator included, the second was a population one short, and the third was in the sentence written to fix the first two.** Three of a kind is not a slip — it is evidence for the entry's own safe default, that a hand-counted population is the defect rather than the report of one.
- **THE REMEDY UNDER-COVERED ITS OWN FINDING BY SIXTEEN ITEMS, ON AN INTERFACE IT COULD NOT REACH.** REG-F-183's remedy named `purpose`/`sourceSection`/`completionClaims` — all on **`PwuTemplate`**. The sixteen profile selection criteria live in `appliesToRisk`, declared on **`ConformanceProfile`** (`ontology.types.ts:184-189`). Corrected in place there; **all four prose carriers are in scope.**
- **✅ AND THE PREDICTED RED ALREADY EXISTS — I NEITHER DESIGNED IT NOR KNEW OF IT.** `packages/rph-engine/src/ontology-delivery-census.test.ts` derives the authored key set **from the data itself** (`for (const t of ontology.pwuTemplates) for (const k of Object.keys(t))`) and fails for any key neither delivered into the seeder payload nor carried by a `TEMPLATE_ACCOUNTED_FOR` row — with a **companion test rejecting stale rows**, so the exemption cannot rot into an allowlist. **A new template field reddens it by construction.** That is a better predicted red than one I would have written, precisely because it was authored against a different concern and cannot have been shaped to fit this change.
- **AND THE PARSE MECHANISM MUST BE EXTRACTED, NOT COPIED.** `doc004-conformance.test.ts` has **zero `export` statements**: `normalize`, `sectionLines`, `subsection` and `bulletItems` are file-local. Reuse therefore means lifting them into a shared module — **copying them would be REG-F-175's defect again**, a second implementation of a checker free to drift from the first. ⚠ And the drift has already begun *inside the exemplar*: that file carries **four inline re-implementations** of section extraction, one of which omits the `start < 0` guard the real `sectionLines` has, so a missing section would slice from `-1` instead of throwing.
- **⚠ ITS `subsection` LOOKUP IS BY TITLE, NEVER BY NUMBER, AND THE REASON IS RECORDED IN THE FILE** — subsection numbering is not uniform across the twelve policies (`Purpose` is §15.2 but §16.1), and *"assuming a number is the single most reliable way to read the wrong subsection and report it as ratified"*. **The same discipline is why this session's extractor keyed on anchor text and then checked where it landed.** The new reader must inherit it: RPH-DOC-003's subsections are **unnumbered** (`## Blocking conditions`), a third shape again.
- **⚠ AND ONE ADVERSARIAL CLAIM WAS CHECKED, WHICH TOOK TWO ATTEMPTS BECAUSE MY FIRST INSTRUMENT HAD NO DISCRIMINATING POWER.** A lens argued the plan would miss *"§12’s required fields"*, so I walked every `# N. PWU Type:` section — **thirteen of them** — for a `## Required fields` run. The first pass reported **§12 with 15 and the other twelve with ZERO**, which is a parser artifact: **§12 is the only section using that exact heading.** The others use entirely different titles — `Required evidence`, `Required outputs`, `Required inputs`, `Expected outputs`, `Principal completion claim`, `Standard child PWU Types`, `Recomposition rule`, `Candidate child PWU Types`, `Principal claims`, `Key assurance policies`, `Required behavior`, `Assurance considerations`.
- **⚠ AND THAT RUN’S CONTROL FAILED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** It had two arms: a fabricated phrase (expected absent) and a known-present phrase (expected present). **The fabricated arm passed and the known arm FAILED** — because the phrase I picked as "known present" was itself one of the items the run was reporting absent. So the reassuring arm was the one that proved nothing, and the run had no power to distinguish "not carried" from "my search cannot see anything". **Its numbers were discarded, not reported.** Re-run with a control verified present earlier in this session (`user-stated facts` → true; fabricated → false), §12 carries **9 of its 15 required fields** as exact phrases; the six that are not are `journey identity`, `primary actor`, `exceptional paths`, `completion condition`, `failure condition`, `evidence of success`.
- **⚠ THOSE SIX ARE CANDIDATE GAPS, NOT CONFIRMED ONES, AND THIS ENTRY’S OWN PARENT SAYS WHY.** REG-F-183 established that this repository **abbreviates** when it transcribes — which is how an exact search there scored eleven present items as absent. Each of these six needs the same both-directions check before anyone calls it missing. **What is established is narrower and still useful: the carriage question is LARGER than REG-Q-045 enumerates**, and REG-F-183’s *"every item carried"* is true of the population it audited and silent about this one.
- **WHAT THAT DOES TO THE DESIGN.** The reader must walk subsections **BY TITLE** across every `# N. PWU Type:` section rather than assume a fixed heading — the exact discipline `doc004-conformance.test.ts` records for its own by-title lookup (*"assuming a number is the single most reliable way to read the wrong subsection and report it as ratified"*), with the extra wrinkle that DOC-003’s subsections are **unnumbered**, a third shape again. **The narrow lift REG-F-183 named remains correct and is now known to be a floor rather than the whole job.**
- **Merge target:** Part 4 of the Ratify Sheet is the **sponsor's** to strike; the two register corrections are made here; the design lands as its own increment. **Safe default:** **before auditing a document's conditions, check whether its act is still live** — and **a control that cannot distinguish is worse than no control, because it is reported as one**: mine passed its fabricated arm and failed its known-present arm, and only the second was load-bearing — a precondition to a reversed act is a question worth answering and an obligation that no longer binds, and reporting it as the second gives a register urgency it has not earned.
