### REG-F-185 — the seed had MERGED two ratified criteria into one, and only a test demanding the ratified WORDING could find it
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** THE REMEDY REG-F-183 NAMED, BUILT AND DRIVEN · **Status:** BUILT. Predicted red watched first; full gate green but for the pre-existing CSAA pin.
- **WHAT WAS BUILT.** `packages/rph-product-realization-pwa/src/doc003-carriage.test.ts` reads RPH-DOC-003 **at runtime** and asserts that every item of four ratified populations — the six-class epistemic taxonomy, the six validator-hunted failure modes, the eight minimum scenario classes, and the sixteen conformance-profile selection criteria — is carried by the seeded ontology **in the ratified wording**. ⚠ **What it is NOT:** it does not move content out of prose into structured fields, and it does not fix that §10's failure modes sit inside a `sourceSection` **provenance** string. It pins the WORDS. That is less than *"the taxonomy is modelled"* and more than nothing, which is what was there.
- **⚠ AND IT ADDS NO ONTOLOGY FIELD — A DEPARTURE FROM REG-F-183's REMEDY, WITH A MEASURED REASON.** That entry said *"lift them into enumerable fields"*. `packages/rph-engine/src/ontology-delivery-census.test.ts` fails for any authored `pwuTemplates` key neither delivered into the seeder payload nor carried by a `TEMPLATE_ACCOUNTED_FOR` row — and ~~that list has been EMPTY since 2026-08-06, its own comment recording that "an exemption nobody checks is how this table rots into an allowlist". A new field would therefore have reopened the allowlist~~ **⚠ THAT REASON IS WRONG — SEE REG-F-188. `TEMPLATE_ACCOUNTED_FOR` holds SEVEN live rows**, and the "EMPTY SINCE" comment I read describes the ASSERTION’S empty result, not the map above it. **The decision stands on its other ground** — the content was already in the dataset and what was missing was the check — but adding a row would have been ordinary use of a live mechanism, not the reopening of an emptied allowlist. A contracts cascade through `DefinePwuType` remains a real cost. **The content was already in the dataset; what was missing was the check.** So this increment builds the check and leaves the schema alone. `completionRule` is derived (`'All of: ' + completionClaims.join(' ')`), so editing a claim flows through without touching the seeder.
- **✅ PREDICTED RED, WATCHED FIRST, AND EXACTLY AS FORECAST.** Run before any data change: **3 failed / 7 passed**. The three failures are precisely the populations REG-F-183's hand audit had identified as abbreviated — failure modes, scenario classes, profile criteria — while **the epistemic taxonomy passed, because it is carried verbatim**. A prediction made by hand two hours earlier, reproduced by an independent instrument.
- **⚠ AND THE FIX FOUND SOMETHING THE AUDIT HAD NOT: A MERGED CRITERION.** Fourteen items needed their ratified wording restored. **Thirteen were shortenings** — `omitted constraints` for *"omission of inconvenient constraints"*, the eight scenario classes each missing the word `path`, `database/API changes` for *"database or API changes"*. **The fourteenth is different in kind.** §4.1 ratifies *"small, reversible changes"* and *"well-understood internal features"* as **two separate selection criteria**; the seed carried the single phrase *"Small, reversible, well-understood changes"*. **That is not an abbreviation but a LOST DISTINCTION** — one criterion offered where the corpus ratifies two — and nothing would have caught it: the phrase reads naturally, a count of the profile's criteria was never taken, and REG-F-183's content search scored both items CARRIED because their words all appear. **Only demanding the ratified wording exposed it.**
- **THE CONTROLS, ONE OF WHICH EXISTS BECAUSE OF THIS SESSION'S OWN FAILURE.** Three. (1) The reader must resolve a real document — >1000 lines, and 20 items across the three bullet populations. (2) `carries` must **REJECT** a fabricated phrase **AND accept a known one** — *both arms*, because REG-F-184 records a control of mine whose fabricated arm passed while its known-present arm failed, leaving it no power to discriminate at all. (3) A missing anchor must **THROW** rather than return an empty population, since `expect(missing).toEqual([])` is exactly what a reader that finds nothing also produces.
- **AND THE POPULATION SIZES ARE PINNED, NOT ONLY MEMBERSHIP** — 6, 6, 8, and 5/5/6 for the profiles. A corpus edit deleting five of six bullets would otherwise leave a green run over the single survivor: REG-F-121's shrinking-denominator shape, where a smaller population reports as success.
- **IT KEYS ON ANCHOR TEXT, NEVER ON NUMBER OR LINE.** RPH-DOC-003's subsections are **unnumbered** (`## Minimum scenario classes`) — a third shape beside DOC-004's `## N.M Title` and DOC-003's own `## 4.1 Lightweight Profile`. `doc004-conformance.test.ts` records the reason: *"assuming a number is the single most reliable way to read the wrong subsection and report it as ratified"*. Line numbers are worse — REG-Q-045 cites L535-542, and one edit above them moves every citation.
- **⚠ AND ITS ORACLE IS SOUND FOR A REASON ONLY SIX DAYS OLD.** Reading the corpus at runtime would have been a liability under Ratify Sheet Part 4's archive proposal. **REG-D-034 abandoned that retirement and admitted these documents as SOURCE OF RECORD** (REG-F-184), so the oracle stays readable by ruling rather than by luck. Had that ruling gone the other way, this test would have been built to break.

### REG-F-186 — the merged criterion has a general form, and deriving it shows REG-Q-045 enumerates 58 of the 315 items those sections ratify
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** THE GENERAL FORM OF REG-F-185, DERIVED · **Status:** SIZED, not remedied. **Three merges are CONFIRMED by reading; the rest of the output is candidates and is labelled so.**
- **THE GENERAL FORM, ASKED BECAUSE THE FINDING WAS CLOSED.** REG-F-185 found §4.1's *"small, reversible changes"* and *"well-understood internal features"* carried as the single phrase *"Small, reversible, well-understood changes"*. The general form is not *"that phrase was wrong"* but **the seed compresses a ratified ENUMERATION into a CONJUNCTIVE PHRASE** — and every content-level check scores that as carried, because all the words are present. So it was derived rather than enumerated: over every `# N. PWU Type:` section's `## <title>` bullet runs, an item is a merge candidate when no seeded string carries it standalone but some string carries all its content words.
- **THE POPULATION IS FAR LARGER THAN THE ONE THE PRECONDITION NAMES.** Those thirteen sections carry **36 bullet runs and 315 ratified items**. **REG-Q-045 enumerates 58 — about 18 %.** Measured against the seeded ontology: **standalone 235 · merge candidates 34 · no carrier 46.** REG-F-183's *"every item carried"* is true of the 58 it audited and says nothing about the other 257 — which is exactly what that entry claimed, and is worth stating in numbers now that they exist.
- **⚠ NEITHER LIST IS A DEFECT LIST, AND BOTH OF THIS SESSION'S HAZARDS APPLY TO IT.** The 46 "no carrier" can be **paraphrases** — the error that scored eleven present items absent in REG-F-183 — and the 34 "merge candidates" are matched by word-bag, which **false-positives** on long provenance strings that happen to contain each word separately. Reporting either as a gap would repeat a mistake made twice today. **What the numbers establish is a SIZE, not a set.**
- **⚠ AND THE FIRST RUN OF THIS INSTRUMENT WAS ITSELF WRONG, CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS REPORTED.** It searched only `pwuTemplates`, so every §17 *"Assurance policies"* item reported NO CARRIER **by construction** — those names live in `seedPolicies`. **70 apparent absences became 46** once the search corpus matched the population, moving 35 items. **A search corpus narrower than the population under test is a false-negative machine**, and the thing that caught it was adding the two-armed control REG-F-184 demanded: a known-present phrase must match AND a fabricated one must not, with the script throwing if either fails.
- **⚠ CORRECTED BY REG-F-187 — THE TWO §12 "MERGES" BELOW ARE NOT THE §4.1 DEFECT, AND CALLING THEM CONFIRMED WAS WRONG.** §4.1's was a **corrupted transcription of a ratified list**. **§12 provides no inputs list at all** — its four subsections are `Purpose`, `Required fields`, `Minimum scenario classes`, `Assurance policies` — so the Journey template's `inputs` are **AUTHORED**, as they are for eight of the thirteen sections. The seed's actual convention is `inputs` ← a section's `Required inputs`/`Inputs` run, **verbatim**, and §12 has no such run to violate. **What survives: the general form is real** — §4.1 proved it, and REG-F-187 found two further divergences of neighbouring kinds. **What falls: these two instances do not demonstrate it.** The original text follows.
- **✅ CONFIRMED BY READING RATHER THAN BY HEURISTIC — THREE MERGES, TWO STILL PRESENT.** §4.1's was fixed in REG-F-185. **The Journey template's `inputs` carries *"primary and supporting actors"* and *"trigger and preconditions"*, against §12's four separately ratified fields** — `primary actor`, `supporting actors`, `trigger`, `preconditions`. Same shape, same invisibility to a content check, and **they close the question REG-F-184 left open**: §12's six items that an exact search called absent were not simply absent, and not simply carried — **two pairs were merged and the search saw the halves it happened to match.** Neither reading was right.
- **WHAT IS OWED, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Owed: extend `doc003-carriage.test.ts` to §12's required fields once the merges are decided, since the reader is already in place. **Not owed:** a sweep of the 46 and 34 as though they were findings — each needs a reading, and this repository has recorded twice today what happens when a heuristic's output is treated as a verdict.
- **Merge target:** none — this entry is the measurement; the remedy is a later increment. **Safe default:** **a search corpus narrower than the population under test cannot return a true absence** — and the shape to watch for is a ratified enumeration compressed into a conjunctive phrase, which reads naturally and which every check for CONTENT will pass.

- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A CONVENTION DERIVED, GATED, AND TWO DIVERGENCES REPAIRED · **Status:** BUILT and DRIVEN; predicted red named before the test existed.
- **THE CONVENTION WAS DERIVED, NOT IMPOSED — WHICH IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A CHECK AND A NEW REQUIREMENT.** Five of the thirteen `# N. PWU Type:` sections give an inputs list (`## Required inputs`; `## Inputs` in §8). Measured **before** anything was written: where one exists the seed transcribes it **verbatim and in order** — §10 **5/5**, §14 **8/8**, §20 **10/10**. The gate therefore asserts a rule the authors were already keeping. The other eight sections provide no such list and their templates' `inputs` are authored; they are explicitly out of scope.

Every content search, substring search and word-bag test scores that as identical; REG-F-186's own merge heuristic classified it as standalone-carried. **§18:** *"approved PWU Instance shape"* had become *"approved PWU shape"* — **one word dropped** from an otherwise exact eight-item transcription. Neither is a merge: they are a **third and fourth divergence class**, and both were invisible to every instrument this session has built.

PWU Type:` section and collects **every** `## <title>` bullet run — it does not look for a fixed heading, because the titles genuinely vary (`Required inputs`, `Inputs`, `Required fields`, `Required outputs`, `Expected outputs`, `Principal claims`, `Assurance considerations`, and more). **POSITIVE CONTROL:** that same walk FINDS `Required inputs` in §§10/14/18/20 and `Inputs` in §8, so it is not blind to inputs-like subsections — it reports their absence only where they are absent. ⚠ An earlier pass that searched for the single fixed heading `## Required fields` reported **twelve of thirteen sections as having none**, which is what a fixed-heading search does to a document that names things differently (REG-F-184). **(2) *"the ROOT template carries no `Spec §` citation"*:** every one of the 15 seeded templates’ `sourceSection` was enumerated and matched against `/Spec §\d+/`. **POSITIVE CONTROL: 13 of 15 matched** — so the pattern works, and the two that did not (`PRODUCT_REALIZATION`, `ARCHITECTURE_CONCERN`) are genuinely uncited rather than unmatched.

### REG-F-188 — a whole CLASS of ratified list has no home in the repository, and the reason I gave for not building one was a misread comment
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A CORRECTION TO REG-F-185 + the structural finding underneath it · **Status:** RECORDED. **The design question belongs to the sponsor; no repair is made here.**
- **⚠ FIRST, THE CORRECTION, BECAUSE IT IS MINE AND IT IS THREE COMMITS OLD.** REG-F-185 declined to add an ontology field partly because *"`TEMPLATE_ACCOUNTED_FOR` has been EMPTY since 2026-08-06 … a new field would have reopened the allowlist"*. **It holds SEVEN live rows** — `candidateChildren`, `inputs`, `outputArtifactTypes`, `completionClaims`, `requiredEvidenceTypes`, `defaultPolicyIds`, `sourceSection` — each naming a real delivery route. **What I actually read was a comment sitting BELOW `expect(unexplained).toEqual([])`, describing the ASSERTION'S empty result**, and I attributed it to the map declared above. The two are adjacent and mean opposite things. **The decision survives on its other ground** — the content was already in the dataset, so what was missing was the check — but *"adding a row reopens an emptied allowlist"* was false: it would have been ordinary use of a live mechanism. **Safe default learned: do not infer a comment's subject from its proximity**, which is the same rule this register already carries for spec sections and line numbers.
- **AND THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, WHICH IS LARGER THAN THE INCREMENT THAT FOUND IT.** RPH-DOC-003 carries **two different kinds of bullet run**, and the repository models exactly one. **(a) Runs naming DELIVERABLES** — `Required inputs`, `Expected outputs`, `Required outputs` — land in `PwuTemplate.inputs`/`outputArtifactTypes`, are delivered as `PWU_TYPE.requiredInputs`/`requiredOutputs`, and are machine-checked by the delivery census and now by REG-F-187's verbatim gate. **(b) Runs naming the CONTENT FIELDS OF ONE ARTIFACT** — §12 `Required fields` (15), §13 `Required properties` (11), §15 `Required content` — **have nowhere to go at all.**
- **✅ ESTABLISHED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY COUNTING, WHICH IS THE ONLY WAY IT COULD BE ESTABLISHED.** Verified by reading the contracts directly: **`ArtifactObjectSchema` is a `z.strictObject`** whose eleven fields beyond the envelope are `artifactType, mediaType, storageProvider, storageKey, contentHash, byteSize, producingPwuId, producingExecutionAttemptId, securityClassification, retentionClass, status` — **not one of them is content.** An Artifact is a content-addressed POINTER, and `strictObject` forbids smuggling fields in. And **`ProfessionalWorkObjectType` has 23 members, of which USER_JOURNEY, REQUIREMENT, SCENARIO, ACTOR, DOMAIN_ENTITY and CAPABILITY are none** — every member is a HARNESS object. **There is no product-content plane for these fields to live in**, so their absence is not drift.
- **⚠ AND TWO COUNTS WERE REFUSED ALONG THE WAY, INCLUDING MY OWN.** A subagent reported §13's eleven properties as **"zero of eleven present anywhere"**; my own measurement over the vocab returned **7 of 11** with a working two-armed control. **Neither number is admissible.** §13's properties are words like `statement`, `authority`, `rationale`, `dependencies`, `lifecycle` — **generic single words that match anywhere in a 3,600-line file**, so the substring search cannot distinguish "this Requirement property is carried" from "this word appears". **A generic single word cannot be searched for**, in either direction, and the structural argument above is what settles the question instead.
- **WHAT THIS DOES TO REG-F-186's OPEN LISTS.** That entry sized 46 items as "no carrier" and refused to call them gaps. **A share of them are this class** — ratified artifact-content fields with no plane to land on — and those are not drift, not a transcription defect, and **not mine to fix by inventing a schema**. Deciding whether the repository should model product-domain artifact content is a shape question of exactly the kind REG-D-004 assigns to the repository and DOC-004 §5 routes through the contract procedure — **but inventing eleven Requirement properties nobody ratified as fields is the fabrication `m1-object-fields.json` already refuses in its own words.** Recorded as a question, deliberately unanswered.
- **⚠ THE ESCALATION IN THIS ENTRY WAS TOO BIG, AND THE SPONSOR SUPPLIED THE CONTEXT THAT SHRANK IT.** This entry put *"should the repository model product-domain artifact content?"* to the sponsor as a shape question. **CON-000 AX-11 already answers it:** *"The Professional Work Unit is the common primitive… professional domains compose it into different work topologies… A domain product is a specialization of JPWB containing multiple PWAs."* The harness is domain-agnostic **by axiom**; `USER_JOURNEY` is a Product Realization PWA concept, and the vocab says so in its own words — *"pwuKind/artifactType are ontology-defined data (M8), not global enums"*. **`artifact.test.ts` already LOCKS that openness**, recording a value of `'anything-at-all'` as ACCEPTED *"to LOCK the absence of invented enums: if someone later narrows these to a made-up enum, this fails and sends them to the corpus first"*. **The repository had already built the guard against the repair I was contemplating.**
- **✅ BUT THE STRUCTURAL FINDING SURVIVES, AND IS NOW BETTER GROUNDED THAN WHEN IT WAS FILED.** Four independent readings agree that there is no product-content plane: (1) `ArtifactObjectSchema` is envelope-only; (2) `ProfessionalWorkObjectType`’s 23 members contain no product-domain concept; (3) **RPH-DOC-003 §21 — the section that actually specifies artifacts — specifies them by ENVELOPE**: *"Artifacts must have: identity; provenance; content hash where applicable; semantic version; producing PWU Instance; applicable claims; status; supersession history"*, a catalog of TYPE NAMES and never of content; and (4) **DOC-009 ratifies 56 `create table` statements and NOT ONE is a product-domain content table** — no `user_journeys`, `requirements`, `scenarios`, `actors`, `domain_entities` or `capabilities`. Six of §21’s eight envelope requirements map to fields directly and *applicable claims* maps relationally through `ClaimObject.subjectObjectIds`.
- **⚠ AND I REACHED THAT FOURTH READING BY LUCK RATHER THAN BY METHOD, WHICH IS THE PART TO KEEP.** `m1-object-fields.json` carries a note recording this exact blind spot from a previous occurrence: *"the search stopped at the meaning doc and the wire doc and never opened the STORAGE doc… **GENERALIZE THIS: ‘unspecified — do not fabricate’ notes in this vocab were written against DOC-002+DOC-007 only. DOC-009 is a ratified source and must be checked before any such note is trusted**; the same blind spot produced a false blocker on §16 item 23."* **I filed this entry having read the meaning doc and the wire doc and not the storage doc — the same three-document scope, the same omission** — and only found DOC-009 because that note happened to sit beside something else I was checking. **The check confirmed the finding; the method did not produce the check.**
- **AND ONE OBSERVATION IS WITHDRAWN AS ALREADY-RECORDED.** While reading, I found no `SupersedeArtifact` command and no `ArtifactSuperseded` event, against §21’s *"supersession history"*. **That is not new:** `m1-object-fields.json`’s open item states it — *"no ARTIFACT interface, no §5.2 id prefix, no command, no event"* — and DOC-009 §18.3 ratifies the mechanism as *"new artifact; new semantic version; supersession link"* rather than a mutable field. **Filed nowhere, because it is filed already.**
- **Merge target:** none — the correction is applied to REG-F-185 in place; the design question is the sponsor's. **Safe default:** **when a ratified list has no home, say so structurally rather than counting how many of its words appear somewhere** — the count will be wrong in whichever direction the searcher's phrasing happens to favour, and both directions were produced today.

### REG-F-189 — my reading was REFUTED by the document's own §44, the population was 8 runs not 3, and the repository is §45-VALID while being §44-INCOMPLETE
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** A READING PROPOSED, ATTACKED, AND OVERTURNED · **Status:** SETTLED as a reading; the remaining gap is stated and deliberately NOT built.
- **⚠ MY READING WAS WRONG, AND THE LENS I POINTED AT MY OWN HYPOTHESIS IS WHAT FOUND THE EVIDENCE.** I proposed that §12's fifteen *"Required fields"* were **completion-claim material** — assertions the PWU must satisfy — rather than schema the PWA ontology owes. **RPH-DOC-003 §44 refutes it directly.** That section is headed **`## Artifact schemas`** and lists thirteen: *Product Intent, **User Journey**, **Requirement**, Domain Entity, Integration Definition, Architecture Description, **Architecture Decision**, Execution Plan, Test Strategy, Product Artifact, Assurance Assessment, Evidence Package, Baseline.* **Three of those thirteen are exactly the three sections carrying content runs.** The document has a name for what those runs are, and it is *schema* — not claims.
- **✅ BUT §45 — THE DOCUMENT'S OWN VALIDITY TEST — DOES NOT REQUIRE THEM, AND THAT IS THE RESOLUTION.** *"A Product Realization PWA package is valid only if:"* rule **1** is *"Every PWU Type defines purpose, inputs, outputs, claims, evidence, and assurance defaults"* — **six limbs, and fields/properties/content is not among them** — and rule **2** is *"Every artifact type has identity, provenance, versioning, and producing relationships"*, envelope only. **So the seeded PWA is §45-VALID and §44-INCOMPLETE at the same time**, and both statements are the document's own. That is a far more precise account than *"a class of ratified list has no home"*: it has a NAME (§44) and no VALIDITY CONSEQUENCE (§45).
- **⚠ AND THE POPULATION WAS 8 RUNS, NOT 3 — MY THREE WERE MERELY THE ONES UNDER A `Required` HEADING.** Derived rather than listed: five more declare the parts of one typed object in **trailing prose with no heading at all** — §21 *"Artifacts must have"* (8, envelope), §23 *"Every evidence item must declare"* (6), §24 *"Every assurance policy … must define"* (16), §38.2 *"Every child must inherit or reference"* (6), §42 *"Each governance point must define"* (7). **I verified §23 and §38.2 by reading them.** **A heading scan found three of eight** — the identical instrument defect REG-F-184 recorded one level down, where searching for the fixed heading `## Required fields` reported twelve of thirteen sections as having none. **The same mistake, at the level of the search rather than the section.**
- **AND MOST OF THE EIGHT DO HAVE HOMES, WHICH SHARPENS THE GAP RATHER THAN WIDENING IT.** §24's sixteen assurance-policy fields are the twelve seeded policies with their criteria and evidence, machine-checked by `doc004-conformance.test.ts`; §23's evidence declarations correspond to the EVIDENCE object; §38.2's child-inheritance items are decomposition contract material; §21's envelope is implemented (REG-F-188). **The unmodelled remainder is precisely §§12/13/15 — the three PRODUCT-DOMAIN artifact schemas** — which is the same boundary AX-11 draws and the same one DOC-009's 56 tables draw. **Four independent lines now agree on where the edge is.**
- **NOT BUILT, AND THE REASON IS NOT TIMIDITY.** Authoring User Journey / Requirement / Architecture Decision schemas is a real increment in the PWA package — consistent with AX-11, since it is PWA data and not harness shape — but **§45 does not require it, no assurance policy evaluates it, and nothing in the repository reads such a schema today.** Building it now would produce authored content with no consumer, which is this register's most-recorded defect (*"a field that is authored and unread is this grant failing, not this grant used"*). **The evidence is assembled and the decision is a scheduling one, not a governance one.**
- **THE SEARCHES BEHIND THIS ENTRY’S TWO ABSENCE CLAIMS — *"nothing reads such a schema"* and *"no assurance policy evaluates it"* — stated because the absence gate refused the entry without them (P-3), for the fourth time today.** **THE SEARCH:** `packages/` and `apps/`, excluding `node_modules` and `dist`, for a declared type or schema bearing the three §44 names. ⚠ **AND THE FIRST PASS RETURNED A FALSE POSITIVE I HAD TO CHASE DOWN** — a loose alternation matched three files, and the symbols were `ArtifactRequirementSchema`, `EvidenceRequirementSchema` and `IndependenceRequirementSchema`: **substrings of longer, unrelated names, none of them §44’s Requirement schema.** Tightened, there is **no `UserJourneySchema`, no `ArchitectureDecisionSchema` and no standalone `RequirementSchema`** anywhere. **POSITIVE CONTROL:** the same search style DOES resolve `BaselineObjectSchema` and `AssuranceAssessmentSchema` — two other §44 entries — in `packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts`, so it finds a §44 name that IS modelled and reports absence only for those that are not. **This is the exact mirror of the failure mode this session kept hitting from the other side:** the abbreviation searches produced false ABSENCES, and this one produced a false PRESENCE, from the same cause — matching words instead of symbols.
- **Merge target:** none — this entry is the reading. **Safe default:** **when a document seems to leave a list homeless, look for the section that NAMES the home before concluding there is none** — §44 sat 1,600 lines from §12 and answered it in two words, and my reading survived three earlier checks only because none of them had gone looking for it.

### REG-F-190 — the "deeper issue" REG-F-185 left standing is not one: all six failure modes ARE modelled, in the policies, and my probe for the last one asked for the wrong word
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** AN OWED ITEM CLOSED AS A NON-ISSUE · **Status:** CLOSED. **No code changed; a recorded debt is removed rather than carried.**
- **WHAT WAS LEFT STANDING.** REG-F-185 declined to fix one thing and said so plainly: *"§10's failure modes are carried inside a `sourceSection` PROVENANCE string rather than as content. Pinning the words is a floor, not the fix."* It has sat as an owed item since. **It is not owed.**
- **✅ ALL SIX HAVE FINDING-CODE COVERAGE, ACROSS THE SEEDED POLICY SET.** §10 says *"The applicable Assurance Policy, through a conforming validator implementation, should specifically check for: …"* — so the place to look is the POLICIES, and there they are, among **99 finding codes over twelve policies**: *solution substitution* → `SOLUTION_SUBSTITUTION`; *scope expansion disguised as helpfulness* → `UNAUTHORIZED_SCOPE_EXPANSION`; *omission of inconvenient constraints* → `MISSING_USER_CONSTRAINT` (all three in `pol_intent_fidelity`); *premature architecture* → `PREMATURE_DOWNSTREAM_SHAPING` in **`pol_intent_completeness`**; *unsupported assumptions* → seven codes in **`pol_assumption_disclosure`**; *conversion of preferences into requirements* → **`UNAUTHORIZED_REQUIREMENT`** in **`pol_requirement_coverage`**.
- **SO THE `sourceSection` STRING IS A CITATION, NOT THE CARRIER, AND REG-F-185 DREW THE WRONG CONSEQUENCE FROM A CORRECT OBSERVATION.** It was right that the words sit in a provenance field and right that nothing gated them — REG-F-185 then gated them. It was wrong to infer that the CONTENT was therefore unmodelled: the modelling lives where §10 points, in the applicable policies, and three of the six are deliberately carried by **sibling** policies rather than by the one the section names. **A finding that says "this content has no home" must look where the document sends it before concluding.**
- **⚠ AND MY PROBE FOR THE LAST ONE RETURNED THE OPPOSITE ANSWER.** A regex over all 99 codes for `/PREFERENCE|REQUIREMENT_FROM|WANT/` reported **"NO CODE ANYWHERE"**, and I nearly recorded a one-item assurance gap on it. **Reading the 99 codes found it in seconds.** The cause is specific and new: **I guessed the vocabulary the corpus would use.** DOC-004 frames the defect as **AUTHORITY** — a requirement nobody authorised — where DOC-003 frames it as **PREFERENCE**. Same defect, two framings, and a regex can only carry one. **CONTROL, both arms:** the same probe style correctly resolved `SOLUTION_SUBSTITUTION` (2 codes) and correctly returned nothing for a fabricated concept, so it discriminates — it was simply asking for the wrong word.
- **THIS IS THE FIFTH SEARCH-VERSUS-READING DISAGREEMENT TODAY AND THE FIRST OF ITS KIND.** The others were abbreviation (false absence), narrow corpus (false absence), generic single words (untrustworthy both ways), and substring-inside-a-longer-symbol (false presence). **This one is SYNONYMY across two ratified documents**, and no amount of care with the regex would have caught it — only reading the population does.
- **Merge target:** none — an owed item is struck from REG-F-185 rather than carried. **Safe default:** **when probing whether a concept is modelled, read the population rather than pattern-match it** — a regex encodes YOUR name for the concept, and the corpus is entitled to have chosen its own.

### REG-F-191 — the corpus does not forbid recovery from BLOCKED; it ratifies a mapping that would define it and never writes the mapping down
- **Date:** 2026-08-15 · **Type:** CORPUS EVIDENCE FOR AN OPEN SPONSOR DECISION (REG-F-083 / REG-Q-034) · **Status:** the decision remains the sponsor's; **what changes is that it is no longer a choice between two ratified readings.**
- **⚠ FIRST: I RAN A SIX-AGENT CORPUS SEARCH FOR SOMETHING THIS REGISTER HAD ALREADY SEARCHED AND RECORDED.** **REG-Q-034** already carries it, with positive controls: *"no ratified transition anywhere gives `RESHAPING`, `CHALLENGED`, `BLOCKED` or `ESCALATED` any out-arrow other than `ABANDONED`/`SUPERSEDED`."* And **REG-F-093** already records REG-F-083 as **MIS-FRAMED** — *"the ratified Canonical Domain Model contains the word 'terminal' ZERO times; `terminalStates` is wholly a repository shape"*. **The rule that would have saved the run is this register's own — grep the register before searching, filing or escalating — and it has paid four separate times today.** Recorded because a rule I keep citing and keep not applying is worth more as a recorded failure than as a maxim.
- **WHAT THE RATIFIED MACHINE ACTUALLY SAYS, read directly from RPH-DOC-002 §8.** §8.2 *Exception transitions* ratifies **entry only**: `SHAPING | Missing information | BLOCKED`, `PLANNED/EXECUTING | Runtime dependency unavailable | BLOCKED`, and `EVIDENCE_PENDING | Evidence impossible to obtain | ESCALATED`. Neither state appears as a SOURCE anywhere in §8.1 or §8.2; the only exits are the umbrella rows `Any active → ABANDONED` and `Any non-baselined → SUPERSEDED`.
- **✅ AND §8.3 IS THE ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS.** *"The following must be rejected"* lists **nine** illegal transitions — including `ABANDONED → READY` and `SUPERSEDED → EXECUTING`, the two genuinely closed doors — and **names neither BLOCKED nor ESCALATED.** **The document demonstrably knows how to forbid a recovery arrow, does so for the states it means to close, and does not do so here.** So the repository's one-way behaviour is an ABSENCE of a specified arrow, not a ratified prohibition; those are different things and REG-F-083's headline reads as the second.
- **✅ AND BLOCKED IS NOT THE BLOCKING-FINDING STATE — a reading REG-F-083's own name invites.** A blocking finding sends `UNDER_ASSURANCE → REJECTED or RESHAPING` (§8.2). BLOCKED's two ratified triggers are **"Missing information"** and **"Runtime dependency unavailable"** — **both transient conditions by their own wording.** A state entered because information is missing, which cannot be left when the information arrives, is incoherent on its face; the corpus never says it cannot be left.
- **✅ THE NEW FINDING, AND IT IS NOT SILENCE BUT AN UNFULFILLED OBLIGATION.** RPH-DOC-002 **§36.5 ratifies**: *"Each failure class must map to permitted control actions."* **§37** then ratifies the vocabulary that mapping would use — `ControlAction` includes **`CONTINUE`, `WAIT`, `RETRY`, `CHANGE_TACTIC`, `RESHAPE_PWU`, `REPLAN_EXECUTION`** alongside `ESCALATE`, `WAIVE`, `REJECT`, `ABANDON`. **The mapping itself is written nowhere.** So the corpus does not merely fail to grant a recovery arrow: **it states that a mapping MUST exist, supplies the recovery-shaped vocabulary it would draw on, and then never writes it** — and that missing mapping is precisely where a recovery arrow would be specified. **A ratified `must` with no fulfilment is a corpus defect, not a design decision**, and it is stronger evidence for "recovery is owed" than any absence could be.
- **WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE.** It does **not** create an arrow — inventing one remains the fabrication REG-D-029 exists to prevent, and the pin in `block-escalate.test.ts` CONTROL 4 keeps the absence honest. It **does** mean the sponsor is not choosing between two ratified readings: **no ratified text is contradicted by adding recovery**, and §36.5 arguably obliges the mapping that would define it. The safe default — one-way is what ships — stands until ruled, and should now be read as *"unspecified"* rather than *"specified as one-way"*.
- **⚠ CORRECTION, SAME DAY, AND IT INVALIDATES THIS ENTRY’S RECOMMENDATION RATHER THAN ITS EVIDENCE.** On the strength of the bullet above I advised the sponsor that the decision to take was *"whether to commission that failure-class → control-action mapping"*. **The mapping already exists and is fully built.** `packages/rph-domain/src/execution-failure-taxonomy.ts` implements §36.5: a table from `ExecutionFailureClass` to permitted `ControlAction`s, **total over the enum and derived from it rather than from a copy**, every action containment-checked against the ratified 23-value enum, **`ESCALATE` permitted for every class so no failure has a dead end**, and each row carrying `basis: 'RATIFIED' | 'AUTHORED'` so the rows the corpus decided are distinguishable from the rows an agent wrote. Seven tests hold it, including a provenance split. **`ExecutionFailureClass` itself was minted under REG-E-025, ratified 2026-08-05.**
- **⚠ AND THE FAILURE IS THE ONE THIS ENTRY OPENS BY CONFESSING, COMMITTED AGAIN ONE PARAGRAPH LATER.** The first bullet records that I ran a six-agent corpus search for something REG-Q-034 had already answered, and names the remedy: **grep the register first**. I then grepped the register, found REG-Q-034 and REG-F-093, stopped there, and **never grepped the repository for the mapping itself** before recommending it be commissioned. **The corpus-scoped claim — *"the corpus never writes the mapping down"* — remains TRUE and is unaffected.** What was wrong was the inference from it: a corpus gap does not imply a repository gap, and this repository has spent months filling exactly such gaps.
- **✅ SO THE REAL GAP IS ONE AXIS OVER, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE ONE I NAMED.** `grep -c workLifecycleState execution-failure-taxonomy.ts` returns **0**. The mapping lives entirely on the **EXECUTION** axis — failure class to control action — and **nothing binds a `ControlAction` to a `workLifecycleState` transition.** So `WAIT`, `RETRY` and `RESHAPE_PWU` are permitted responses to a failure and reach no lifecycle arrow: the vocabulary that would let a blocked PWU resume exists, is ratified, is mapped, and connects to nothing.
- **⚠ AND THAT BINDING IS NOT MINE TO AUTHOR, BY THIS REGISTER’S OWN LINE.** REG-F-083 declined for exactly this reason, in its own words: *"inventing the arrow would be exactly the fabrication REG-D-029 grants authoring to avoid — **authoring a SHAPE for a ratified act is not the same as authoring a new ACT**."* REG-D-029 grants the shape of a ratified act; an exit from BLOCKED is a **new act**, because no ratified text contains it. **The mapping was buildable because §36.5 ratifies that it must exist. The lifecycle binding is not, because nothing ratifies that it does.**
- **WHAT A MINIMAL RULING WOULD HAVE TO SAY, so the decision is small.** For each of `BLOCKED` and `ESCALATED`, **either** (a) declare it closed — abandon or supersede are the only exits, and the repository records that as a decision rather than an absence — **or** (b) name the ACT that leaves it and its target state (for example, *"BLOCKED → SHAPING when the blocking condition clears"*). **Once the act exists, its SHAPE — command, payload, event, guard — is mine under REG-D-029**, and the `ControlAction` binding follows from it rather than preceding it.
- **Merge target:** none — evidence for REG-F-083/REG-Q-034, both of which stay OPEN. **Safe default:** **a document that forbids the arrows it means to forbid is telling you something by the ones it leaves alone** — §8.3 closes ABANDONED and SUPERSEDED by name and passes over BLOCKED in silence, and that asymmetry is evidence where a bare absence would not be.

### REG-D-043 — SPONSOR RULING: a recovery act EXISTS for BLOCKED and ESCALATED; the arrow set is derived from §8.2 rather than invented
- **Date:** 2026-08-16 · **Type:** DECISION (sponsor ruling, given directly) · **Status:** EFFECTIVE — MERGE PENDING (effective on recording; incorporation is W-6). · **Closes the decision half of:** REG-F-083, REG-Q-034 · **Grants shape-authoring under:** REG-D-029.
- **THE RULING.** Put as a two-way choice — (a) declare BLOCKED and ESCALATED closed, or (b) name the act that leaves them and its target state — the sponsor ruled **(b)**: *"I'm inclined to agree with (b) as well. Proceed."* **A recovery act exists.** What was blocked was never the shape; it was whether the ACT existed at all, and REG-F-083 declined precisely there: *"authoring a SHAPE for a ratified act is not the same as authoring a new ACT."* **That sentence is now satisfied: the act is ruled, so its shape is authorable under REG-D-029.**
- **⚠ THE TARGET STATES ARE DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DISCIPLINE OF THIS ENTRY.** RPH-DOC-002 §8.2 ratifies exactly three ways into BLOCKED — `SHAPING | Missing information`, `PLANNED/EXECUTING | Runtime dependency unavailable` — and exactly one into ESCALATED, `EVIDENCE_PENDING | Evidence impossible to obtain`. **The recovery arrows are those same pairings traversed in the other direction and nothing else:** `BLOCKED → {SHAPING, PLANNED, EXECUTING}` and `ESCALATED → EVIDENCE_PENDING`. **No state pairing appears that the corpus does not already contain**, which is what keeps this authoring rather than invention. **`BLOCKED → READY` is NOT added** — READY is not a ratified in-arrow, and it is the discriminating case that proves the arrow set was derived from §8.2 rather than from convenience.
- **AND THE PRECEDENT IS EXACT, WHICH IS WHY THE SHAPE IS NOT A NEW QUESTION.** `BlockPwu` itself is marked in the vocab as **`UNRATIFIED-AUTHORED (2026-08-09, under REG-D-029 / JAN-PWUWP W-5)`**, with `drivesFrom: "SHAPING | PLANNED | EXECUTING"` and `drivesTo: "BLOCKED"`. Its arrows were ratified by §8.2 and its shape was authored under the grant. **The recovery command is that same construction mirrored**, and the vocab already expresses a multi-state end as a pipe-separated string, so no new vocab shape is required.
- **⚠ THE DESIGN'S REAL CONSTRAINT, FOUND BY GROUNDING RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** Recovery must return to the state the PWU actually came from — otherwise `SHAPING → BLOCKED → EXECUTING` would skip PLANNED and manufacture a path §8.1 never grants. But **the origin is not recorded where one would expect it.** `PwuBlocked`'s payload carries `blockReason`, `missingObjectIds?` and a `workLifecycleState` that `pwu.ts:829` sets to **`BLOCKED` itself** — while the GENERIC setter's `PwuStateChanged` payload **does** carry `previousState`. **The dedicated arrow records strictly less than the generic one, and drops exactly the datum recovery needs.** `pwu_state_history` is ratified in DOC-009 and **not implemented** (`SCHEMA_SQL` declares five tables and no sixth), and as specified it stores the state AT each row with no FROM column, so even building it would not answer the question directly.
- **TWO ROUTES, AND THE FORK IS REAL RATHER THAN RHETORICAL.** **(A) FOLD THE EVENT PREFIX:** `readAggregateEvents` is on `StorageAdapter`, `HandlerContext.store` is that adapter, and three handlers already use it (`assurance.ts:1541`, `execution.ts:1529`, `kit.ts:48`); `replayPwuAxes` is exported from `rph-projections`, already a production dependency. **No new plumbing.** Its cost is that `pwu-replay.ts` states its own fragility — *"If an event should move an axis and does not say so, this reducer will produce the wrong answer."* **(B) RECORD `blockedFrom` ON THE EVENT:** a contract change to a `strictObject`, making recovery a field read, and arguably the honest repair of the asymmetry above — the dedicated event would then carry what its generic sibling already carries. Its cost is that **events already written lack the field**, so historical blocks must fail closed (AX-8) rather than guess.
- **AND ONE STRUCTURAL BLOCKER THAT DECIDES THE INCREMENT'S SHAPE.** `PwuLifecycleCommandSpec` has exactly four fields and its `target` is a **single** `WorkLifecycleState`. Every existing lifecycle command moves to a fixed state. **A recovery command's target is dynamic by construction**, so the spec type must admit that — a change reaching every lifecycle command, which is why this is its own increment and not a patch.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `docs/_working/DESIGN-pwu-write-path.md` and `ROADMAP-pwu-write-path.md` gain **W-5.5**; implementation follows there. ⚠ **Numbered 5.5, not 6: W-6 is TAKEN** (*"the six §8.1 middles"*), and this is the deliberately deferred half of W-5, which is what that file’s `W-4.5`/`W-4.6` convention is for. **Safe default until W-5.5 lands:** unchanged — the arrow does not exist, `block-escalate.test.ts` CONTROL 4 still pins its absence, and **that control is the predicted red W-6 must produce**.

### REG-F-192 — W-5.5's forks resolved by axiom, and two structural collisions found before a line of code was written
- **Date:** 2026-08-16 · **Type:** DESIGN RESOLUTION + BLOCKING SURFACE FOUND · **Status:** W-5.5 REMAINS SCHEDULED; **two collisions must be resolved first and neither was visible from the roadmap row.**
- **✅ FORK 1 IS SETTLED BY AXIOM, NOT BY PREFERENCE.** The choice was: derive the pre-block state by folding the event prefix, or record it explicitly on `PwuBlocked`. **CON-000 AX-6 decides it:** *"Professional meaning is never inferred from null fields, missing values, attachment, proximity, **ordering**, storage location, or UI placement."* **Folding a prefix infers professional meaning from ORDERING** — precisely the inference AX-6 forbids. So the origin is **recorded explicitly** as `blockedFrom`, which also repairs the asymmetry REG-D-043 recorded: the dedicated `PwuBlocked` event currently carries LESS than the generic `PwuStateChanged`, which already carries `previousState`. **Events already written lack the field, so recovery of a historical block fails closed** — AX-8, *"fail closed; escalate rather than invent"*. Two axioms, same direction.
- **⚠ COLLISION 1 — THE OWNERSHIP TABLE IS KEYED BY TARGET AND ASSUMES ONE COMMAND PER TARGET STATE.** REG-F-072 closed the generic setter's route to *"the worklifecycle targets a semantically named command owns"*, and its own note explains the key: *"Keyed by TARGET because every legal in-arrow to each of these six states is reachable by the one command whose `advancePwuLifecycle({ target })` names it."* The table maps ~~**nine**~~ **ELEVEN** states to **one command each** — `SHAPING: 'BeginPwuShaping'`, `READY: 'MarkPwuReady'`, and nine more. ⚠ **CORRECTED 2026-08-16: I counted from a read that stopped at `BASELINED` and missed the two rows W-5 added** (`BLOCKED: 'BlockPwu'`, `ESCALATED: 'EscalatePwu'`, pwu.ts:441-444). **And the miscount hid the fact that matters more than the collision:** eleven owned targets + eight `PWU_GENERIC_SETTER_SPECS` targets + `PROPOSED` (the birth, the one state of the twenty with no in-edge) **= 20. The two tables are a TOTAL PARTITION of the state space, one owner per state** — which is precisely the property W-5.5 breaks, and I could not see it while the count was wrong. **A recovery command whose target is dynamic lands on SHAPING, PLANNED and EXECUTING — and SHAPING is already owned by `BeginPwuShaping`.** A target cannot have two owners in a table keyed by target. **So W-5.5 does not merely add arrows; it invalidates the key of the mechanism that keeps the setter out.** Either ownership is re-keyed by ARROW (`from → to`) rather than by target, or the recovery command cannot own what it performs.
- **⚠ COLLISION 2 — AND THE CONTROL THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE THE PREDICTED RED DOES NOT TEST WHAT ITS COMMENT CLAIMS.** `block-escalate.test.ts` CONTROL 4 asserts `BLOCKED → {SHAPING, PLANNED, EXECUTING, READY}` are all REJECTED, under the heading *"recovery is not a missing command but a missing arrow"*, and it dispatches the **generic setter** `ChangePwuState`. ~~But **SHAPING and READY are OWNED TARGETS**, so those two are refused by the REG-F-072 ownership guard — **not by arrow absence.** Two of its four cases would refuse identically if the arrow existed. **The control conflates two refusal reasons and attributes both to the one it names.**~~ ⚠⚠ **STRUCK 2026-08-16 — THE MECHANISM IS THE OTHER WAY ROUND, AND THE CONTROL TESTS EXACTLY WHAT ITS COMMENT CLAIMS.** The ownership guard runs **LAST**, after the legality check, and pwu.ts:1400-1402 says why: *"REG-F-072 — LAST, and deliberately so. An arrow that is ILLEGAL should be reported as illegal rather than as owned; a caller redirected to `MarkPwuReady` for a transition the machine forbids outright would be sent to a command that will refuse it for a different reason."* So **today all four of CONTROL 4's arrows are refused by ARROW ABSENCE** (`RPH_ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION`) and none of them reaches the ownership guard at all. `generic-setter-scope.test.ts` CONTROL 2 measures the directly analogous case and passes: `PROPOSED → READY` — READY owned, arrow unratified — asserts the code is `RPH_ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION` and `.not.toContain('Dispatch MarkPwuReady')`. **The conflation was mine, not the test's.** I read the ownership table and never read the call order eight lines below the guard I was reasoning about.
- **✅ WHICH MAKES THE PREDICTED RED SHARPER THAN THE ONE I ANNOUNCED, AND ONLY THE OWNERSHIP READ REVEALED IT.** After the arrows land ~~**SHAPING stays REJECTED** (ownership), **PLANNED reddens**, **EXECUTING reddens**, **READY stays REJECTED** (ownership *and* no arrow — it is not a §8.2 in-arrow). So **exactly two of four flip**, and the loop throws on PLANNED.~~ ⚠ **AMENDED 2026-08-16: two of four flip ONLY IF THE ARROWS LAND WITHOUT THE OWNERSHIP REPAIR — a condition I never stated, and it is the whole finding.** SHAPING stays REJECTED (now by ownership, the arrow having become legal), PLANNED and EXECUTING redden, READY stays REJECTED **by arrow absence alone** (not by ownership — illegality fires first). But if the arrows and the guard repair land **in the same commit, which is how they must land**, then **all four stay REJECTED and only the error CODE changes** — and CONTROL 4 asserts nothing but `status`. **So the control this entry nominated as W-5.5's predicted red is GREEN before the change and GREEN after it**, across the exact transition it exists to notice. Not a test that pins the wrong absence: **a test that cannot observe the event it was written for.** I had predicted three-of-four flipping with READY as the discriminator; **that was wrong, and it was wrong in the direction of expecting more evidence than the test can give.**
- **WHAT W-5.5 NOW HAS TO CONTAIN, and it is larger than "add an arrow and a command".** (1) `blockedFrom` on `PwuBlocked` — a `strictObject` contract change plus regeneration. (2) `PwuLifecycleCommandSpec.target` widened from a single `WorkLifecycleState` to admit a dynamic target — smallest type-safe form is a union with an explicit marker object, leaving all ~~nine~~ **eleven** existing rows untouched. (3) A decision on ownership re-keying (collision 1). (4) CONTROL 4 restructured to COLLECT all four outcomes **and to distinguish an ownership refusal from an arrow refusal** — otherwise it will keep reporting one as the other.
- **Merge target:** Repository — W-5.5 in `ROADMAP-pwu-write-path.md`, amended by this entry. **Safe default:** unchanged; the arrow does not exist. **Safe default for the method:** **a test that pins an absence must name WHICH absence it pins** — CONTROL 4 has guarded the right behaviour for the wrong stated reason since it was written, and a reader trusting its comment would have built the wrong thing.

### REG-F-193 — Collision 1 settled: the DECLARATION must become arrow-shaped, the GUARD must not, and my own claim was refuted three times out of three
- **Date:** 2026-08-16 · **Type:** DESIGN RESOLUTION (adversarially tested) + CONTROL LOSS AVERTED · **Status:** COLLISION 1 CLOSED — W-5.5 UNBLOCKED. · **Resolves:** REG-F-192 collision 1. · **Method:** nine agents, six measuring and three prompted to REFUTE.
- **⚠ I PUT MY OWN CONCLUSION UP TO BE KILLED AND ALL THREE LENSES KILLED IT — on the MODAL, not on the observation.** The claim was *"W-5.5 REQUIRES ownership to be re-keyed by arrow; no target-keyed form can work."* The observation survived every attack: per-target ownership admits exactly one answer per target, and W-5.5 needs two for `PLANNED`/`EXECUTING`/`EVIDENCE_PENDING`. **The word that failed was `REQUIRES`.** A SOURCE-keyed rule — *the setter may not perform any arrow whose source is `BLOCKED` or `ESCALATED`* — leaves the table untouched and works, and its precondition is measured rather than argued: the setter's declared sources are exactly `{READY, PLANNED, EXECUTING, EVIDENCE_PENDING, UNDER_ASSURANCE, SATISFIED, RECOMPOSING}`, so **`BLOCKED` and `ESCALATED` are sources of ZERO setter-declared arrows** and the rule costs the setter nothing. **I had reached for the general remedy and then argued it was the only one.**
- **✅ WHAT IS GENUINELY FORCED IS THE DECLARATION, AND THAT PART IS MEASURED, NOT REASONED.** I simulated the gate under every target-keyed configuration. **All three are green-and-false or true-and-red, and there is no fourth:** (a) widen the existing owners so the four arrows are claimed → **all green, and it DECLARES that `ChangePwuState` performs three of the four recovery arrows and that `BeginPwuShaping` — "begin shaping" — is the act that recovers a blocked PWU**; (b) give the recovery command target-keyed rows → **DISJOINT reddens on exactly `PLANNED`, `EXECUTING`, `EVIDENCE_PENDING`**; (c) drop those three from the setter to restore disjointness → **`READY→PLANNED`, `PLANNED→EXECUTING`, `EXECUTING→EVIDENCE_PENDING` become unclaimed** — the spine the reference undertaking actually drives. **`verif/lifecycle-arrow-declarations.test.ts` keys every assertion on `a.split('->')[1]`, and its own docblock states the precondition it rests on:** *"listed by TARGET because ownership in this machine is per-target: every in-edge of a target is performed by the same command."* Measured: **that holds for all 19 targets today and fails for exactly the four W-5.5 touches.** The gate announces the assumption W-5.5 breaks.
- **⚠⚠ AND RE-KEYING THE GUARD WOULD HAVE KILLED A CONTROL — WHICH IS THE ONE THING I DID NOT THINK TO CHECK, AND THE REASON THIS ENTRY EXISTS.** `pwu.ts:1400-1402` runs ownership **LAST**, deliberately: *"An arrow that is ILLEGAL should be reported as illegal rather than as owned."* `generic-setter-scope.test.ts:233-248` is the sole pin on that ordering and says so: *"Predicted red for the mutant that moves the ownership check ahead of `rejectIllegalWorkLifecycleMove` — **and ONLY for it**: every test above uses a legal arrow, so the ordering is invisible to all of them."* Its subject is `PROPOSED→READY`. **Under a pure arrow key that arrow is not among the 49, so the lookup misses whether it runs first or last, and the mutant becomes UNKILLABLE.** Generalised: the arrow key can only match the 49, every one of the 49 passes legality (the three cross-axis guards land on no owned target), **so the two guards' order stops being observable at all** and `pwu.ts:1400-1402` survives as a comment with nothing behind it. `grep -n "rejectIllegalWorkLifecycleMove\|ownership check ahead\|ownedArrow" scripts/mutants/ledger.ts` → **no output**: that one test is the whole defence. **A remedy that silently converts a live control into a dead one is the defect this register has recorded more than any other, and I was two commits from building it.**
- **✅ THE RESOLUTION IS A UNION, AND IT IS THE ONLY FORM THAT PAYS FOR NOTHING.** The guard becomes `ownerOfArrow(from, to) ?? ownerOfTarget(to)` — **arrow lookup first for precision, the existing eleven-row table retained as a FAIL-CLOSED BACKSTOP.** `BLOCKED→PLANNED` matches the recovery command's arrow and is refused; `READY→PLANNED` matches neither and is allowed; **`PROPOSED→READY` still matches the target backstop, so CONTROL 2 stays falsifiable and the ordering keeps a live pin.** The refused set is a UNION of both keys, so **widening is zero by construction** rather than by measurement — though it was measured too: target-keyed closure = 49, arrow-keyed set = 49, symmetric difference empty in both directions, and all eleven targets agree exactly (`SUPERSEDED` 17/17, `ABANDONED` 17/17, down to 1/1).
- **AND THE UNION IS WHAT KEEPS ELEVEN LEDGER ROWS TRUE.** `verif/guard-enforcement-ledger.data.ts` asserts in eleven `evidence:` strings that a given state *"is NOT in `PWU_SEMANTIC_LIFECYCLE_COMMANDS`, so `changePwuState` is the only writer"* (`:55, :89, :99, :125, :145, :173, :237, :259, :283, :313, :317`). **Re-keying the table falsifies all eleven; the union falsifies none**, because the table keeps its eleven rows and its meaning. That field is ungated prose — `anchorFault()` reads only `enforcingAnchor` — so nothing would have reddened. **I checked the register before filing that as a finding and it is already disclosed** — **REG-F-081** (*"C-0b's enforcing-site citations rotted in two days, and the control could not fail on it"*) settled that the anchor is the checked thing and *"the line number is retained as a navigation hint and is explicitly documented as not the checked thing."* Grepping the register first stopped me filing something already answered. ⚠ **And I nearly cited it as REG-F-124 — a number I INFERRED from the line I had grepped, never read.** The standing rule is that a line number never identifies an entry; I caught it only because I went back to check a citation I had already written.
- **⚠ THE THIRD BUILD OF THE SAME DEFECT, CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED THIS TIME.** REG-F-084's drive-site gate enumerates what to check by iterating `PWU_SEMANTIC_LIFECYCLE_COMMANDS` — *"THE FIX IS THE CONTROL, NOT THE LIST — because a list of eight would rot exactly as the list of two did."* **A recovery command with no row in that table is INVISIBLE to it, so `PwuUnblocked` would ship undriven** — precisely what `block-escalate.test.ts` CONTROL 3 records having been built twice: *"W-5 then added `PwuBlocked`/`PwuEscalated` to `pwu-replay.ts` in the same commit, believing that closed it. It did not."* The list did not rot; **the derivation stopped being total over commands**, which the control could not notice because it derives its population from the wrong one of the two tables. `ownedEvents()` must iterate `PWU_LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_SPECS` (command-keyed, and the recovery command has a row there by construction) while still reading its event from `BINDINGS`, so the two-artifact comparison survives.
- **Merge target:** Repository — `pwu.ts` (guard), `pwu-lifecycle-command-spec.ts` (arrow-shaped declaration), `verif/lifecycle-arrow-declarations.test.ts` (DISJOINT → arrow-level), `pwu-fold-drive-sites.test.ts` (population → specs), amending W-5.5 in `ROADMAP-pwu-write-path.md`. **Safe default:** unchanged; the arrows do not exist. **Safe default for the method:** **before adopting a general remedy, ask which control its generality dissolves** — the arrow key is strictly more precise than the target key and would have made an existing mutant unkillable, and no gate would have said so.

### REG-F-194 — W-5.5 landed, and the three things it found were all instruments failing to see a command rather than the command being wrong
- **Date:** 2026-08-16 · **Type:** IMPLEMENTATION + THREE INSTRUMENT DEFECTS FOUND · **Status:** W-5.5 COMPLETE (`39f8f042`); **one consequence REPORTED AND UNFIXED, see the CSAA note below.** · **Implements:** REG-D-043, REG-F-192, REG-F-193.
- **WHAT LANDED, IN ONE COMMIT BECAUSE ANY OTHER ORDER OPENS A HOLE.** `UnblockPwu` performs `BLOCKED → {SHAPING, PLANNED, EXECUTING}` and `ESCALATED → EVIDENCE_PENDING` — §8.2's in-arrows reversed, with `BLOCKED → READY` deliberately absent and now *asserted* absent. **The arrows, the command and the ownership repair are one commit because splitting them opens a real hole, and the hole was MEASURED rather than asserted:** reverting the guard to its target-only form with the arrows in place makes `ChangePwuState BLOCKED → PLANNED` return **ACCEPTED**. ⚠ **One arrow wide, not three** — once the PWU moves, the rest of the loop carries `previousState: BLOCKED` against a PLANNED aggregate and is refused for an unrelated reason. **I had written "PLANNED and EXECUTING" into the commit message before running it**, which is the same reflex REG-F-183 recorded: the count that sounds right, written before the count that is.
- **⚠ FINDING 1 — MY OWN NEW COMMAND WAS INVISIBLE TO THE ARROW CENSUS, WHICH IS REG-F-114's DEFECT RECURRING INSIDE THE REMEDY FOR REG-F-114.** C-0 reported all four new arrows as *"arrows no command can perform"*. The cause is exactly the one REG-F-114 named: `UnblockPwu` resolves its target at RUNTIME from the recorded origin, so its handler declares nothing a syntactic reader can see — the same shape as `advancePwuLifecycle`'s bare `target` and the generic setter's `payload.newState`. **The third recurrence, and the third identical remedy: a FIFTH data idiom that reads the declaration**, never a new AST inference (*"reading a declaration cannot fabricate one; inferring a missing half can"*). Coverage 162 → 166 with the uncovered list UNCHANGED, which is the arithmetic showing the four were credited rather than excused. **I did not anticipate this — the census caught it, which is precisely its job.**
- **⚠⚠ FINDING 2 — REG-F-084's DRIVE-SITE GATE COULD NOT HAVE SEEN `PwuUnblocked`, AND ITS HEADER PROMISES THAT IT WOULD.** That control says *"a twelfth lifecycle command added without either fails this test ON ARRIVAL rather than two increments later"* — but it enumerates commands by walking `PWU_SEMANTIC_LIFECYCLE_COMMANDS`, which is **keyed by TARGET and therefore structurally incapable of holding a command whose target is a function of its source.** So `PwuUnblocked` would have shipped folded-but-undriven: **CONTROL 3's defect for the THIRD time**, after W-1 and W-5. **And the shape is new each time.** W-1's was a missing fold; W-5's was a fold nothing drove; this one is a fold, driven, that the gate enumerating what-must-be-driven cannot enumerate. **The list did not rot — the DERIVATION stopped being total over commands**, which is the one failure a control deriving its own population cannot see by construction. Population now drawn from BOTH tables.
- **⚠ FINDING 3 — I BROKE FOUR MUTANT ANCHORS MYSELF, WITH THE EXACT DEFECT I HAVE A STANDING RULE ABOUT.** A Python `write_text` flipped `verif/arrow-command-census.ts` to CRLF; a **22-line addition became a 1940-line diff** (981 insertions, 959 deletions) and four ledger anchors resolved **0 times**. **REG-F-081's anchor check found it** — the mechanism built because *"line numbers rot silently"* catching a whole-file rewrite instead. Restored to LF: 22 insertions, 0 deletions, twelve anchors resolving again. The rule existed, was written down, and I still used the text-mode call; **the defence that worked was the gate, not the rule.**

### REG-F-199 — the query roster's only survivor was a spelling coincidence, and the delta investigation it unblocked found 0 of 15 capabilities absent

**Date:** 2026-08-20 · **Type:** INSTRUMENT CORRECTION + DELTA INVESTIGATION (discharges REG-F-198 finding (2), the backlog's "W-3 finding (i)") · **Status:** MERGED — the instrument is fixed with its own mutant; the delta roster is recorded and its residue is itemized in `docs/_working/BACKLOG.md`

- **THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, AND WRONG EXACTLY WHERE IT MATTERED.** W-3's consumer walk decided, for every ratified name, whether an implementation exists — using `String.includes`. So the ratified query `getPwu` read as PRESENT because it is a prefix of `getPwuTemplate` (`packages/rph-product-realization-pwa/src/ontology.ts:34`), an unrelated ontology-template lookup keyed by `pwuKind` — the very conflation CDM L336 forbids. That was **the sole positive result in the fourteen-name population the walk had been commissioned to measure.** REG-F-198's finding (2) and this backlog item both said "13 of 14"; the truth is **14 of 14**, and both also named `getAssuranceStatus`-adjacent naming as the survivor while `getPwuAssuranceStatus` sat in the same roster's ABSENT column. Fixed at `scripts/tracker/match.ts` (identifier-boundary matching, indexOf-based so document-sourced needles need no regex escaping), witnessed by `verif/tracker-name-match.test.ts` (6 tests, incident case first) and TWO declared mutants, **one victim each**: `MU-TRACKER-01-boundary-check-always-passes` (collapses the boundary test to `return true` — `String.includes` exactly) against the matcher suite, and `MU-TRACKER-02-trailing-boundary-unchecked` (drops only the TRAILING check, admitting precisely the prefix case) against the census leg. The split was forced by the ledger's own one-victim gate, and it made the claim stronger: MU-02 proves the tracker gate can SEE an instrument regression, which is true only because a LIVE `measure.ts` run was added beside the DB-reading assertion. **Both measured KILLED** (clean tree): MU-01 reddens 3 of the matcher suite's 6 tests; MU-02 reddens **exactly 1 of the census suite's 24** — the live-instrument assertion and nothing else.

- **BLAST RADIUS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED.** Re-running the identical walk over all 118 consumer-walk items (14 queries, 96 events, 8 surfaces) under boundary matching changed **exactly one tier** (`getPwu` DECLARED→ABSENT) and **two witness citations** — `DecisionEffective` and `PwuSatisfied` had been first-matched inside `makeDecisionEffective` and `controllerMarksPwuSatisfied`, both **in comments**. Tiers unchanged, witnesses corrected. Ladder: DECLARED 133→132, ABSENT 31→32. The flawed reading is preserved append-only at `census/w3-corrections.ndjson`, because `w3-verdicts.ndjson` is regenerated by the fixed instrument and would otherwise erase it.

- **⚠ THE INSTRUMENT HAD ALSO BEEN UNREADABLE SINCE THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN.** `scripts/tracker/measure.ts` carried **four NUL bytes** in two sort keys, present since `5cf50324` (W-3) and carried through `edb6ff79` (W-4/W-5). Git classifies a whole file as binary on one NUL, so **no diff of the measuring instrument had ever been renderable** — not for the review that added the DRIVEN tier, not for the one that put it in the gate. Removed; the regenerated output was then proven **byte-identical** rather than argued to be. **The general form, derived:** 1,554 tracked files scanned, 31 contain NULs, 30 are images — exactly one authored source file was affected. **And the gate that should have caught it already existed**: `verif/source-is-reviewable.test.ts` covers `scripts/`, was written for this exact defect, and is in both vitest project lists. It was verified by putting the NULs BACK and watching it go red naming the file. The control was sound; it simply was not run, because each wave closed on targeted suites instead of the gate. *A working instrument nobody runs is indistinguishable from a broken one* — this programme's own thesis, arriving addressed to its author.

- **THE DELTA INVESTIGATION (5 lanes, each investigated then adversarially refuted, 15 subjects — the 14 queries plus the ratified Execution Workbench surface).** Result: **0 ABSENT · 2 EQUIVALENT · 13 PARTIAL.** Not one ratified capability is missing outright. The two pure naming divergences are `getPwuType` (→ `PwaAuthoringBroker.getType`, `broker.ts:272`, with the version-qualified resolution at `pwu.ts:155-172`) and `getBaseline` (→ `listBaselines`/`getObject`, `queries.ts:198`/`:214`). The thirteen partials decompose into **6 genuinely unbuilt capability gaps**, **5 built-but-unreachable** (the capability exists and the *seam* does not — `readAggregateEvents` is implemented at `sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:251` and is not a member of `EngineHandle`; the §28.2 assurance aggregate is computed at `+page.server.ts:131`, serialized, and **rendered nowhere**), and **2 latent correctness defects a rename would have hidden**: `getPwuHierarchy` never withdraws a REJECTED decomposition's edges (so it returns every parent→child link ever *proposed*), and the OPEN-observation filter in two read models tests the **recording event's payload**, which is hard-coded `'OPEN'` at `assurance.ts:2386` — a tautology, while every gate correctly loads current state (`assurance.ts:2076-2077` says so in terms). Per-subject classification, evidence and missing-delta are recorded at `census/f199-query-delta.ndjson` and gated: `verif/tracker-ingest.test.ts` asserts every §34.5 name carries a capability verdict and that **none of them is ABSENT**.

- **⚠ AND THE HEADLINE FINDING WAS HALF WRONG — CAUGHT BY DRIVING IT.** The investigation named as most material that RPH-CON-009's version limb (`pwu.ts:159-170`, `pwuType.pwaVersion === undertaking.pwaVersion`) compares operands "derived from the same immutable field on the same aggregate" and **cannot fail**. That half is **REFUTED by measurement**. They are two *snapshots* of `pwa.version` taken at different times — `definePwuType` stamps it (`pwa-authoring.ts:456`), `createUndertaking` gates and binds it (`:1055`) — and `EditPwa` can move the version between them while the PWA is still DRAFT. `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwa-version-binding.test.ts` drives the window end to end: the stale-stamped type is **REFUSED naming RPH-CON-009**, and the identical proposal without the intervening edit is **ACCEPTED**, so the guard discriminates. **What survives:** once PUBLISHED the version string is frozen for that `pwaId` forever, so `PwaVersionReference`'s one-pwaId-many-versions addressing has no representation and Ref-Demo §19 L741's "changes create a successor version" is unimplementable. The successor-version gap is real; the dead-control claim was not.

- **⚠ A GATED REGISTER ROW ASSERTED A PRODUCTION CALLER THAT DOES NOT EXIST — AND CONTRADICTED ITSELF 1,200 LINES EARLIER.** `enforcement-register.ts:2754` (RPH-TRC-005) read "`impactedObjects` has one in `handlers/decomposition.ts`". It does not: every identifier-boundary occurrence in the tree is its own definition (`traceability.ts:208`), its own test, or **prose** — including `decomposition.ts:439`, which mentions it inside a **rejection string saying the opposite**. `enforcement-register.ts:1533` (RPH-INT-006), in the same file, states the truth. A refuter recorded that trusting the row would have overturned a correct finding wrongly. Corrected in place; no ladder verdict moves, because the measurement reads `kind:` and not the prose — which is precisely why the prose rotted unobserved.

- **⚠ DEF-W4-002 IS A FALSE-NEGATIVE DEFERRAL — the governing record is stale in the *other* direction.** `G4-gate-package.md:14,:43`, `JAN-W4-DR-001:21` and `PROGRAM-STATUS.md:47` all still carry "Execution Workbench — PARTIAL, drill-down deferred". The deferred drill-down (steps, attempts, runtime binding, recovery, provenance) is **all built**, delivered later under JAN-EXECPLAN DWP-01..05, DR-004 DWP-06 and JAN-EXECREM. The genuine residue is the **authoring half**: all 19 form actions on the Undertaking Workbench were enumerated and **not one authors a plan** — the only production path to `ProposeExecutionPlan` mints a hard-coded single step with all four policy bags as empty literals and immediately approves and activates it. The surface operates plans it cannot author.

- **THE GOVERNING QUESTION, ANSWERED.** §34.5 is **an early, non-exhaustive enumeration — not a by-name contract.** Three corpus facts decide it: REG-F-083 ratifies §34 as a **MINIMUM API Surface** and records that it omits `abandonPwu`, `escalatePwu`, `blockPwu`, `satisfyPwu` and `rejectPwu` (a list that provably omits ratified members of its own category cannot be exhaustive); §34.5 supplies **no signature, return shape or semantics** for any of the fourteen names, so there is nothing to conform *to* by name — every lane had to argue semantics from §32.x, §29.x, DOC-004 §28/§38-39 and RIWS §28, which is what an index into other sections looks like; and §34's preamble is hortatory and scoped ("**the first implementation should** expose commands and queries rather than unrestricted CRUD"). **The consequence is NOT "rename sixteen exports"** — it is that **§32.x/§29.x are the contract, and that is where all thirteen deltas were found.** With one exception that binds on substance: `getObject` (`queries.ts:214`) **is** the unrestricted-CRUD read the preamble forbids, standing in for four ratified typed queries with no discriminator assertion at any call site — so `/undertakings/<any-object-id>` renders a PWU, Baseline or Decision as an Undertaking rather than 404-ing.

- **Two prior rulings kept this from re-filing settled ground, and the register-first rule found both.** `getImpactAnalysis` is already **REG-F-006, OPEN and NARROWED** — the mechanism is specified, the actor (DEC-2) is blocked behind sponsor escalation REG-E-030 — so its deltas sharpen that entry and do not open a new one. And `getPwuExecutionStatus`'s missing rollup is **corpus-CONFORMANT, not a gap**: REG-F-080's ratified safe default is that *"no document may describe `PWU.executionState` as derived or derivable; it is caller-asserted."*

- **Merge target:** Repository — commits `80a01cb1` (instrument fix, NUL removal, red-first census assertion) · this commit (delta investigation, RPH-TRC-005 correction, the driven RPH-CON-009 window). Supersedes REG-F-198 finding (2)'s count in place.

### REG-F-200 — 9 of 21 disclosed deferrals no longer describe the tree, and the artifact meant to carry their current status is an empty template

**Date:** 2026-08-20 · **Type:** AUDIT (all 21 `DEF-*` roadmap deferrals, 5 lanes investigated then adversarially refuted) · **Status:** MERGED — the population is INDEXED and gated; the one live status field is corrected; carrier corrections and a standing gate are itemized in `docs/_working/BACKLOG.md`

- **THE RESULT.** 21 deferrals: **3 FALSE_NEGATIVE** (the deferred content is built), **5 PARTIAL** (built in part, and the deferral misleads in exactly the built half), **1 STALE_PREMISE** (unbuilt, but the stated rationale no longer holds), **12 STILL_TRUE**. So **43% of the disclosed "not built" claims misstate the current tree** — and the population was derived from the tree by two independent readers that agreed exactly (21 ids found, 21 audited, no gap in either direction).

- **⚠ THE STALENESS IS NOT RANDOM, AND THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING.** Seven of the eight stale rows sit in W0–W4 (7 of the 11 deferrals taken there, 64%) against one of the nine taken in W5–W9. It clusters harder by KIND OF WORK: **every stale deferral deferred the WIRING of an already-existing kernel to a surface or a slice** — a UI form, a call-site sweep, a projection consumer, a slice drive, a scoring write-up — while **every deferral that named a genuinely new object type, command or vocabulary member is still true.** The mechanism is visible in the delivery attributions: that wiring was later picked up by programmes tracking in a DIFFERENT ID SPACE (JAN-EXECPLAN DWP-01..06, the DR-002 surface programme, REG-F-069/077/103), which recorded closure HERE, in this register, and never wrote back to any `DEF-*` carrier. Two id spaces, no back-reference.

- **⚠⚠ THE ROOT CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CLERICAL.** `JAN-ROADMAP-001-C-living-control-registers.yaml` is titled *"Living Roadmap Control Registers"*, declares a `deferral` record contract with a REQUIRED `status` field — and holds `deferrals: []`. Every one of its five registers is empty; the file's own status is `ACTIVE_TEMPLATE`. So all 21 deferrals live ONLY in dated, per-wave gate packages, which are historical exit records and **must not be rewritten** (G1 saying "deferred → W2" and G2 saying "delivered" is the correct flow, not a contradiction — a point the audit's framing blurred and this entry corrects). The consequence: the question *"is this deferral open today?"* had no artifact that could answer it, and nothing could notice when the answer changed.

- **REG-F-019 ALREADY NAMED THIS DEFECT CLASS ONE LEVEL DOWN.** An OVERCLAIM is caught by the enforcement register's overclaim gate; an UNDERCLAIM — certifying something DEFERRED while checks for it run green — "was caught by nothing, because a family exempted from the gate makes no claim to check." `verif/deferral-honesty.test.ts` closes that direction for CONFORMANCE-MANIFEST rule ids and states its own limits. Roadmap `DEF-*` ids are a different id space that no gate watched at all.

- **THE REMEDY IS AN INDEX, NOT A REWRITE — the same move this programme already made once.** All 21 deferrals are now census rows (`docs/tracking/census/f200-deferrals.ndjson`, kind `deferral`, added to the closed KINDS vocabulary with its reason recorded), each carrying its audited status as an ATTR — never a ladder verdict, on the `enforcement_class` precedent: a deferral's status is a claim classification, not an implementation tier. Gated in `verif/tracker-ingest.test.ts`, which re-derives the population from `docs/` and fails if a new deferral is ever taken without being indexed. **Proven red** by dropping one row and watching the gate name the missing id.

- **THE THREE FALSE NEGATIVES.** (1) **DEF-W4-002** — Execution Workbench drill-down; all five deferred elements render in production (`step-attempts`, per-attempt `runtimeBindingId`, `step-retry-exhausted`, `outputArtifactId`, `aiProduced`); the genuine residue is the AUTHORING half (REG-F-199). (2) **DEF-W0-001** — per-capability conformance scoring; delivered at BOTH named targets (`W1-DR-001` §4 is literally *"per-WP conformance classification"* and grades all eight W1 master WPs; `W2-DR-001` §2 carries W2's by reference to its evidence file's *"Per-WP verdicts"*), and the stronger per-INVARIANT form now exists as gated production data in `conformance-manifest.ts` + `enforcement-register.ts`. **Its live status field is corrected in place.** (3) **DEF-W4-003** — baseline promotion-to-AUTHORITATIVE in the UI. ⚠ **The route recorded its own closure while the deferral did not:** `apps/rph-demo/src/routes/baselines/+page.server.ts:7` opens *"This header used to say promotion was out of scope for this authoring surface"* — the code knew, and nothing carried it back.

- **THE STALE PREMISE, STATED MORE PRECISELY THAN THE AUDIT DID.** DEF-W9-003 (PWA upgrade + Undertaking migration) says it *"folds on the **(built)** version binding"*. The audit called that foundation absent. It is not: the binding EXISTS and is ENFORCED — REG-F-199 drove RPH-CON-009 refusing a type stamped before an in-DRAFT version edit, and accepting the same proposal without it. What does not exist is version SUCCESSION: a `pwaId` can hold exactly one `version` string for its life, so "changes create a successor version" is unimplementable and an UPGRADE has nothing to upgrade *to*. The premise is not false — it is **insufficient**, and the remedy is re-statement naming succession as the blocker, together with the W8 row at `W8-W10/disposition-and-gates.md:36` that asserts the parenthetical. Fixing one without the other leaves the contradiction standing.

- **A PAIRED ROW FELL OUT OF THE SAME ASYMMETRY.** `divergence-register.md` keeps its DIV and DEC rows current (DIV-W0-001 carries a dated RESOLVED; both DEC rows read EFFECTIVE) and left its one DEF row untouched — and `UNK-W0-001` beside it still reads `status: OPEN` although its `resolution_gate` (G1+) closed at both G1 and G2. The discipline exists in that file; it was applied to three record types out of four.

- **WHAT A STANDING GATE COULD NOT SEE, stated so it is never read as more than it is** (the `deferral-honesty.test.ts` convention): content delivered UNDER ANOTHER NAME (`startStepGate` discharging `canStartStep`; the command-bus receipt discharging `resolveIdempotency` — half of DEF-W1-001's built column); REACHABILITY, since a grep-shaped predicate scores a symbol live when its only caller is itself dead; SEMANTIC SUFFICIENCY, so it would mark DEF-W3-001's "with impact analysis" discharged on seeing `impactAnalysisRequired` emitted without noticing it is `z.literal(true)` with zero readers; deferrals with NO production symbol at all (DEF-W0-001's prose scoring, DEF-W4-004's a11y tooling); and deferrals NEVER GIVEN AN ID — the class this audit cannot bound either.

- **Merge target:** Repository — this commit. Extends the tracker's closed KINDS vocabulary by one member (`deferral`) with its reason recorded at `scripts/tracker/core.ts`.
